events.text: {npc} falls into step beside you on the white stairs, and says that you have a very particular way of climbing. {He} says it as a diagnosis. {He} has been watching you for a century, it turns out, and has notes.

choices.text: Ask to see the notes

effects.log: {npc} produces them, with a cough. They are accurate, and ruthless, and you take three pages home.

choices.text: Offer a raceter pace

effects.log: You pick up the pace. {npc} matches it, exactly, for nine flights, and neither of you says a word.

choices.text: Tell {him} to mind the stairs

effects.log: {npc} laughs, delighted, as if you had passed an examination.

events.text: At a Court reception a minister introduces you to {npc}, "who came up in your century, you must know each other." You do not. {npc} bows, precisely, and then looks you up and down like a sword on a rack.

choices.text: Return the look

effects.log: You look back. It is a long look. The minister coughs and moves to the next guest.

choices.text: Offer your hand

effects.log: {npc} takes it, for exactly as long as courtesy permits, and releases it with a faint air of having been stung.

choices.text: Make a joke about the minister

effects.log: {npc} laughs, once, against {his} will. A rivalry begins in the usual way: with a shared secret.

events.text: {npc} turns up at your gate with a jar of plum wine and a challenge to a game of stones. {He} says that anyone who has risen as fast as you must be either brilliant or lucky, and {he} would like to know which.

choices.text: Play, and play well

effects.log: You play. It takes all night, and ends in a draw that neither accepts. {npc} leaves at dawn, humming.

choices.text: Decline the wine and the game

effects.log: {npc} looks wounded, then amused. "Ah. Cautious." {He} takes the jar away. You have made an enemy, or a friend.

choices.text: Offer them tea instead

effects.log: The tea is better than the wine, and {npc} says so, bitterly, three times.

events.text: A new name is carved on the stone of the first rank, one place above yours, and under it is a very small, very confident signature: {npc}. {He} stands beside it, waiting for you to read it.

choices.text: Read it aloud, slowly

effects.log: You read it aloud. {npc} bows, and for the rest of the day your name is spoken near theirs.

choices.text: Compliment the carving

effects.log: "The lettering," you say, "is excellent." {npc} cannot decide if this is an insult, and thinks about it for ten years.

choices.text: Ask what rank is for

effects.log: {npc} has no answer. You have, for a moment, the advantage, and you both know you will not keep it.

events.text: You are told that someone has been asking, with great politeness, about your habits. The someone arrives and gives the name {npc}, of the same century, of a slightly better isle, and of a decidedly lower opinion of you.

choices.text: Say you are honoured

effects.log: {npc} narrows {his} eyes. It is the first time anyone has been honoured at {him} on purpose.

choices.text: Say the isle is a handsome one

effects.log: You say it exactly. {npc} thanks you with the formality of a closed door.

choices.text: Ask for the lower opinion in writing

effects.log: {npc} looks briefly, powerfully, annoyed. It is, you will come to see, the beginning of a friendship, or a war.

events.text: {npc} is the first immortal in a thousand years to have beaten the Jade Void's great trial in a single day, and the Court wants you to meet them. They stand there, very straight, looking as though they have been waiting a long time.

choices.text: Say you saw the trial

effects.log: You say you saw it. {npc} is pleased, and cannot decide whether to be flattered or alarmed.

choices.text: Ask what the single day felt like

effects.log: {npc} thinks, and says it felt like being the only one awake in a house of sleepers. You note it.

choices.text: Say you will beat the time

effects.log: {npc} does not smile. {He} says, "I would like that very much." It is the most frightening thing anyone has said to you.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion's seers have read your fate and {npc}'s together, and the reading will not separate them. {npc} is at the Pavilion door when you come out, holding the same slip of paper, and the same look.

choices.text: Compare the readings

effects.log: You compare. They differ in one word. The word is "second". You do not say which of you it is.

choices.text: Burn yours

effects.log: You burn yours. {npc} watches, and after a pause, burns theirs. It is the first thing the two of you do together.

choices.text: Say that stars are cheap

effects.log: {npc} agrees, with the loud, relieved laugh of someone who has been told something dreadful.

events.text: At a banquet, you are placed beside {npc}, whose reputation precedes {him} by several isles. {He} is courteous, clever, and polite to a degree that is clearly a weapon. By the third course, you have both noticed that you are matching each other bite for bite.

choices.text: Slow down

effects.log: You slow down. {npc} slows down. The third course takes a long time.

choices.text: Speed up

effects.log: You speed up. {npc} speeds up. The servants begin to murmur, quietly, about who will crack first.

choices.text: Put down your chopsticks and say it

effects.log: "We are doing it again," you say. {npc} sets down {his} chopsticks and laughs, startled, and the evening is ruined, and wonderful.

events.text: On the stair of the Ninth Cloud a stranger passes you going up, and does not look at you, and is so entirely not looking at you that you stop to watch. It is {npc}, who has decided this is a race and neglected to tell you.

choices.text: Race them to the top

effects.log: You race. {npc} wins by a step, and stands at the landing, entirely out of breath, entirely innocent.

choices.text: Call out the rules

effects.log: You call out the rules, loudly. {npc} stops, turns, and says that is not how the game is played, and a rivalry begins in earnest.

choices.text: Let them go ahead

effects.log: {npc} goes ahead, and glances back once, and you see in that glance that you have just been marked.

events.text: A mutual acquaintance brings you to a lecture by {npc}, an immortal reputed to have a theory about everyone. By the end of the hour, {he} has described your technique to a fault, down to the way you set your weight, and the room is looking at you.

choices.text: Stand and demonstrate the rebuttal

effects.log: You stand and show where the theory is wrong. It is, for the length of one hand, correct, and then it is not. The room applauds both of you.

choices.text: Take notes

effects.log: You take careful notes. {npc} sees you doing it and loses {his} place for the first time in two thousand years.

choices.text: Leave quietly

effects.log: You leave quietly. In the corridor, {npc} catches you up, and the conversation that follows is the longest of your life.

events.text: A letter arrives in an unfamiliar hand: "I have beaten everyone in my century but you. I would like to be told whether that is a boast or a complaint. Yours in some irritation, {npc}." There is a plum blossom pressed into the fold.

choices.text: Reply in kind

effects.log: You reply, three lines, no flourish. The answer comes in a week, and it is eight pages.

choices.text: Visit them

effects.log: You visit. {npc} receives you in a room full of unfinished scrolls and treats you as a long-expected disaster.

choices.text: Reply with nothing, only a blossom

effects.log: You send a blossom, and no word. {npc} will puzzle over it for a decade and be the better for it.

events.text: The Ministry of Rites sends you to inspect an isle, and {npc} is there before you, in the middle of the inspection, quite at home, and already correcting the Ministry's clerk. They look up, and say "Ah, you must be my rival."

choices.text: Accept the title

effects.log: You accept it with a small bow. {npc} is delighted. The inspection goes beautifully, and so do the next several.

choices.text: Dispute it

effects.log: You say that a rivalry takes two. {npc} says, mildly, that it has been taking two for a very long time now.

choices.text: Take their clerk's side

effects.log: You take the clerk's side, for no reason but spite. {npc} gives you a very slow nod, as of one fencer saluting another.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, you reach for the same scroll as someone else. It is {npc}, who withdraws {his} hand with a small formal bow and says, "Please. Apparently we are reading the same things."

choices.text: Offer to share it

effects.log: You share it. For six hours you sit across a table from a person you hardly know, and you disagree about everything, with great pleasure.

choices.text: Take it, and thank them

effects.log: You take it. {npc} watches you read it, and by the time you finish they have found three more.

choices.text: Yield the scroll

effects.log: You yield. {npc} looks at it, and at you, and puts it back, and says: "Not like that."

events.text: There is a fight on the lower stairs, two disciples, a spilled lantern, and you step in to part them. So does {npc}, from the other side. You each take one disciple, and the stairs look at the two of you, and you look at each other.

choices.text: Hand your disciple over politely

effects.log: You hand yours over, and {npc} hands you theirs, and for a moment you are holding the same trouble.

choices.text: Settle it with a word

effects.log: A single word from you, and the two disciples fall quiet. {npc} watches, narrow-eyed, and files it.

choices.text: Let {npc} do it

effects.log: {npc} does it, quite well. You stand aside, and feel something unfamiliar: that you have been outdone by a stranger and liked it.

events.text: The Court seats you at the same table as {npc} for the first time, and everyone at the table is quietly aware of it. {npc} lifts a cup to you, a very exact amount, and you realise the room has been waiting for this.

choices.text: Lift yours to the same height

effects.log: You lift yours. The room breathes. {npc}'s mouth twitches. It is the beginning of something.

choices.text: Lift yours a little higher

effects.log: You lift it higher. {npc}'s eyebrow goes up, a quarter of an inch, and stays there for a decade.

choices.text: Drink without ceremony

effects.log: You drink without ceremony. {npc} sets down the cup, and says to no one, "Oh, this will be tiresome."

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, {npc} remarks, to a circle of listeners, that your technique is "very sincere", and lets the word do its work. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Answer with a line of your own

ok.log: Your answer is repeated all over by evening, and {npc} is not the one repeating it.

fail.log: Your answer lands a beat late, and {npc} thanks you for it, warmly.

choices.text: Say nothing, and bow correctly

effects.log: You bow to the last hair, and the silence is worth more than any speech you had ready.

choices.text: Laugh, and mean it

effects.log: You laugh, and for a moment {npc} looks as if something kind had struck them from behind.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {npc} turns up at your gate in a hard rain with a sick disciple of yours slung over one shoulder, found on the wrong stair. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Accept it, and say thank you properly

effects.log: You say thank you, in full form. {npc} goes stiff, then pink, and leaves in a dignified hurry.

choices.text: Accept it, and say nothing

effects.log: You take the help and say nothing, and the nothing is understood, and is also, somehow, a debt of its own.

choices.text: Refuse it, politely

effects.log: You refuse, politely, and {npc} goes away with the look of someone who has lost an argument they did not know they were in.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {npc} has entered the same contest of arrays as you, with an array that is, unfortunately, good. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Meet it head on

ok.log: You take it, narrowly, and the Court talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: You lose it by a hair, and the hair is the thing everyone remembers.

choices.text: Withdraw, and choose another field

effects.log: You withdraw with grace, and choose another field, and {npc} is left in possession of an empty victory.

choices.text: Propose terms

effects.log: You propose terms. {npc} reads them twice, and accepts three, and sends back a counter-proposal that is a work of art.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a treatise you drafted fifty years ago has appeared under {npc}'s seal, with "improvements". The improvements are real, which is worse. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Correct the record, with sources

effects.log: You correct it with sources, politely and in detail, and the correction is longer than the original, and read.

choices.text: Let it stand, and do better work

effects.log: You let it stand and do better work, and in time the work corrects the record on its own.

choices.text: Confront {npc} in private

ok.log: {npc} admits it, in the end, in a voice that costs them a great deal, and offers a retraction.

fail.log: {npc} denies it with such grace that you almost believe it yourself.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, a cloud-wall comes down on the isle you share a bridge with, and {npc} is on the far side, holding the rope. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Hold your side with everything you have

ok.log: Your side holds, and so does theirs, and in the grey morning you are both still standing.

fail.log: Your side gives a little, and {npc} catches the slack without a word.

choices.text: Trust them with the dangerous half

effects.log: You hand {npc} the dangerous half, and they take it without a flicker, and it is the greatest compliment you have ever paid.

choices.text: Split the work by temper, not by rank

effects.log: You split it by temper. It is a raceter division than rank would have made, and the two of you are pleased in spite of yourselves.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, you find {npc} alone at the edge of the isle at dusk, looking at the sea of clouds the way you look at it when you think you are unobserved. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Say the true thing

effects.log: You say the true thing, and {npc} stares at it as if it were a bird that had landed on the table.

choices.text: Stay, and say nothing

effects.log: You stay, and the silence is the answer, and the two of you are quiet until the lamps need trimming.

choices.text: Make a joke, gently

effects.log: You make the joke, gently, and {npc} laughs, and the evening turns toward warmth.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, Your oldest disciple has been seen walking on {npc}'s isle, with a bundle of clothes, and a look. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You let them go, with a proper blessing, and the blessing is meant, and costs more than a refusal.

choices.text: Win them back

ok.log: You win them back with an offer that has nothing to do with money, and everything to do with remembering.

fail.log: You make the offer, and it is taken as an insult, and they leave faster.

choices.text: Counter-poach, politely

effects.log: You turn up with a polite offer to one of {npc}'s best, and the dance of the long quarrel gains a new step.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {npc} has been raised a rank, and the lamps burned late on their isle, and you could hear it from yours. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Congratulate them sincerely

effects.log: You write a very short note, and it is sincere, and {npc} reads it a great many times.

choices.text: Quietly resolve to catch up

effects.log: You resolve to catch up, and the resolve lasts a decade, and works.

choices.text: Do nothing, and feel it

effects.log: You do nothing, and feel all of it, and the feeling is a kind of work too.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, {npc} sends a very correct challenge, in a very correct hand, on very expensive paper, and the date is next week. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Accept, and give it everything

ok.log: You win it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

fail.log: You lose it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

choices.text: Postpone it a decade

effects.log: You postpone it a decade. They accept, with a tight, unreadable smile.

choices.text: Offer a different test

effects.log: You offer a different test, of patience, of memory, of something less showy. They accept, and it is harder.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, {npc} has been telling the Ministry of Rites that your last sword form was borrowed, and is generous enough to say from whom. The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Ask a pointed question in return

effects.log: Your question is so reasonable that the answer takes a quarter of an hour, and {npc} is not the one who enjoys it.

choices.text: Let it pass, and note it

effects.log: You file it, as you file everything about {npc}, in the part of the memory that does not forget.

choices.text: Return the courtesy with interest

ok.log: The Court admires the return, and {npc} is quiet for a full day.

fail.log: The return is too sharp, and the room takes against the sharper of you.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, {npc} warns you quietly that a ministry clerk is about to open a file on you, and leaves before you can say thanks. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send back something of equal weight

effects.log: You return the favour exactly, to the ounce, and the exactness is the message.

choices.text: Say thanks in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {npc} in public, which they hate, and which the Court is delighted by.

choices.text: Keep the debt and think about it

effects.log: You keep the debt in a drawer, and take it out on slow evenings, and turn it over.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, Two seats on the Jade Court's bench are open, and {npc} has quietly put their name beside yours on the list. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Outwork them

ok.log: You outwork them by a month, and the month decides it.

fail.log: You are outworked by a week, and the week stings more than a year would.

choices.text: Let them have it

effects.log: You let them have it, and they know you let them, and it is the one thing they cannot forgive.

choices.text: Share it, if the rules allow

effects.log: The rules do not allow. You find a way. The result pleases nobody, and is remembered as fair.

events.text: At a Court dinner, {npc} tells the story of your great deed so well that you begin to suspect you were not there. It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Publish your version at once

effects.log: Your version appears within the month, and it is clear, and plain, and hurries the matter along.

choices.text: Tell a friend and let it travel

effects.log: You tell one friend, and the story travels. By the next season, the truth has put its shoes on.

choices.text: Say nothing, and remember

effects.log: You say nothing. You remember. It is a long list, and it is getting tidy.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, Demon-light shows over the eastern edge, and the only immortal near enough to stand with you is {npc}. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Say what must be said, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} says "Yes." The word is a whole treaty.

choices.text: Take the greater risk

ok.log: The risk pays, by a thread, and {npc} looks at you across the wreckage with an entirely new expression.

fail.log: The risk costs you dearly, and {npc} pulls you out, and says nothing about it.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them lead

effects.log: You hold the line and let them lead. It is the hardest thing you have done in a century.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, a letter from {npc} arrives. It begins "I wrote this four times". There is nothing else in it that matters, and you read it twice. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Give them something of yours

effects.log: You give {npc} a small thing of yours. They look at it, then at you, then put it very carefully into a sleeve.

choices.text: Ask them a real question

effects.log: You ask a real question. The answer takes two cups of tea and a century, and is worth it.

choices.text: Keep the distance

effects.log: You keep the distance. You are not sure you were wrong. You are not sure you were right.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, the old patron who funded your first century has been invited to dinner by {npc}. The invitation is on very good paper. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Raise your own terms

effects.log: You raise your own terms and your own manners, and the staff, noting both, stay.

choices.text: Ask what {npc} offered

effects.log: You ask what was offered, and the answer is both humbler and kinder than you feared.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be a raceter host

effects.log: You say nothing, and become a better host, which is the only reply that lasts.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, a century of work finally pays off for {npc}: a book, a form, a pupil. The Court applauds, longer than you think necessary. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Go to the celebration

effects.log: You go to the celebration, and bow, and are very good at it, and are carried home by your own dignity.

choices.text: Send a modest gift

effects.log: You send a modest gift, so modest that it becomes a statement, and {npc} does not know what to say.

choices.text: Avoid the whole business

effects.log: You avoid the whole business, and find it follows you down the corridor anyway.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, {npc} turns up in your practice court and begins to stretch, and asks if you have a minute, and the answer is not optional. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Meet them on the first move

ok.log: You take the first move, and the second, and the Court sits up.

fail.log: They take the first move, and the second, and you are left explaining.

choices.text: Spar for form, not for stakes

effects.log: You spar for form, and the form is a pleasure, and neither of you will say so.

choices.text: Decline, and say why

effects.log: You decline, and say why, truthfully, and it is a surprise to both of you.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, {npc} bows to you exactly as low as precedence requires, and not a hair lower. A clerk has measured it. You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment, loudly

effects.log: You thank them for the kind words, loudly, and {npc} has to carry the rest of the evening on those words.

choices.text: Practise, privately, until midnight

effects.log: You go home and work until the lamps burn low, and the work is better for the insult.

choices.text: Let your reputation answer

effects.log: You answer by doing nothing, and doing it very well, and the room slowly leans your way.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, a crate arrives from {npc}: three rare herbs your alchemist has been hunting for two centuries, and a card reading only "Do not misunderstand." You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Ask why they did it

effects.log: "Because it was correct," says {npc}, and then, after a long moment, "and because it was you."

choices.text: Do not ask, and be grateful

effects.log: You do not ask, and the not asking makes room for something that was not there before.

choices.text: Suspect a trap, and watch

effects.log: You suspect a trap and watch for a year. There is no trap. It stays with you more than a trap would have.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, {npc} proposes a forfeit of years: whoever completes the harder form first gets the other's evening for a century. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Appeal to the arbiter

effects.log: The arbiter hears you with the face of someone who has heard everything, and rules for neither, which is a victory of a sort.

choices.text: Win it in front of an audience

ok.log: You win it in full view, and the applause belongs, for once, to you.

fail.log: You lose it in full view, and the sound is of a great many people not saying anything.

choices.text: Concede, but ask a favour

effects.log: You concede, and ask a favour, and {npc} grants it before you finish asking. Neither of you quite knows what to do with this.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, a ministry citation lists {npc} first and you second, on a matter that was your doing. A clerk apologises with their eyes. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment to your work

effects.log: You take it as a compliment. The work was good enough to steal. It is a strange comfort.

choices.text: Demand an apology in open court

ok.log: The apology is made, in the end, and it is exactly as graceless as you had hoped.

fail.log: The demand is heard as pettiness, and the Court takes it out on you.

choices.text: Quietly restore the credit yourself

effects.log: You write the true account in the margins of three copies, in your own hand, and wait.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, a ward you both helped build begins to fail, in the night, and the only two who know where it is weak are you and {npc}. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

effects.log: You stay to the end, and there is a grey dawn, and the two of you sit on the same step and do not talk.

choices.text: Share what you know

effects.log: You share the secret you have kept for a century, and the crisis passes, and the secret is not a secret any more.

choices.text: Take the credit later, and do the work now

effects.log: You do the work now. The credit can be argued about later, and is, with great relish.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {npc} asks, in the dark of a long hall, whether you ever wonder if the chase has made either of you better. It sounds like a real question. For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Take their hand, as a friend might

effects.log: You take their hand, briefly, and both of you recover with great dignity.

choices.text: Say you are tired too

effects.log: You say it. It is the first time you have said it aloud, and it is lighter than you thought.

choices.text: Change the subject to swords

effects.log: You talk about swords until it is safe. Both of you are relieved, and a little disappointed.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {npc} has hired the one array master on whom your plans depend, at a salary the Court calls "unpatriotic". Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Take it as a warning

effects.log: You take it as a warning, and spend a decade tidying the cracks you had stopped looking at.

choices.text: Confront {npc} directly

effects.log: You confront {npc}, who is entirely unrepentant and entirely charming, and offers you a chair.

choices.text: Outbid them quietly

ok.log: You outbid them quietly, and the quiet is the best part of it.

fail.log: You outbid them, and the bid is a little too loud, and the Court hears.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, {npc} is given the honour you had hoped for, and sends you a note that is, to your considerable irritation, gracious. It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Seize the moment and press the advantage

effects.log: You press the advantage, and for a season you are the one the Court looks at.

choices.text: Reach out, now, while it matters

effects.log: You reach out, now, when it would be easy not to, and it is accepted with a stiffness that is also gratitude.

choices.text: Say a prayer for them, privately

effects.log: You say a prayer for them, privately. You are surprised by how much you mean it.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, a friendly spar with {npc} on the white stairs becomes, by the third exchange, something the lower stairs stop to watch. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Fight your best fight

ok.log: It is your best fight, and the one you will describe on the day you die.

fail.log: It is your best fight, and it is not enough, and it is better than most victories.

choices.text: Ask for a witness you trust

effects.log: You ask for a witness you trust, and the match is fair, and the result is accepted even by those who lose it.

choices.text: Make it a lesson, not a duel

effects.log: You turn the duel into a lesson, for yourself, and let them win the points while you win the thing under the points.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, {npc} asks aloud whether you are the immortal who "used to be somebody on the lower stairs". There is a small, delighted silence. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Cut them with a quotation

ok.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has not read, and they feel its edge for a year.

fail.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has, and has annotated.

choices.text: Compliment them back, a little too well

effects.log: You praise {npc} so thoroughly and so exactly that the praise itself becomes a kind of reproach.

choices.text: Walk out with great dignity

effects.log: You walk out without haste, and the talk follows you, and the dignity is the main topic.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, {npc} sends word that your name came up in the Jade Court and that they spoke for you. Everyone else says it was a short speech. It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Pay it back at the first chance

effects.log: The first chance comes in four years, and you take it, and {npc} accepts it with the look of someone paid in the right coin.

choices.text: Offer a drink, as one equal to another

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} looks at theirs as if it might bite, and drinks it.

choices.text: Receive it, then beat them anyway

effects.log: You take the help, and the next time you face them, you win, and neither of you says a word of the other thing.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, the Ministries want one of you to lead the next survey of the outer isles. {npc} has already packed. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Prepare in silence for a decade

effects.log: You go quiet for ten years. When you come out, the field has changed, and so have you.

choices.text: Send a friendly note

effects.log: The note is friendly and perfectly unnerving, and {npc} loses a night's sleep over it.

choices.text: Take it by surprise

ok.log: The surprise lands, and for once the cloud falls your way.

fail.log: The surprise falls flat, and so do you, a little.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, {npc} has been telling the isles that the new array was "a collaboration". You have the receipts. They have the audience. Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Thank {npc} for the attention

effects.log: You thank {npc} for the attention, so sweetly that it is reported as a threat, and so it is.

choices.text: Outrun it with new work

effects.log: You publish something new, that cannot be misattributed, and say very little about the old.

choices.text: Forgive it, and mean it

effects.log: You forgive it. The forgiving takes a year, not a moment, and leaves you lighter than a victory would.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, the stair collapses under a procession. {npc} is already in the gap, and calls to you without any irony at all. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Face it together

ok.log: Together, you are better than either alone, and you both pretend not to notice.

fail.log: Together, you are not enough, and you both know it, and neither says so.

choices.text: Hold back, and watch what they do

effects.log: You hold back and watch. What they do tells you everything about them, and you are rather ashamed of the watching.

choices.text: Call for help from everyone

effects.log: You call for everyone, and everyone comes, and the crisis becomes a quarrel about who came first.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, {npc} has come to your gate with a jar of the tea from the lower stairs, the tea you both drank when you were poor. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Offer to practise together

effects.log: You offer to practise together. They hesitate for nine hundred years, and say yes.

choices.text: Offer nothing, but remember

effects.log: You offer nothing, but remember, and the memory becomes a warmth you do not deserve and keep anyway.

choices.text: Tell them they were right once

effects.log: You tell {npc} they were right, once, about something long ago. They are quiet for a very long time.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, a minister who used to nod at you has begun to nod at {npc}, and the nod has changed in angle. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Wish them well and mean it

effects.log: You wish them well, and mean it, and find that meaning it makes the loss lighter.

choices.text: Remind them of the old days

effects.log: You remind them of the old days. They look uncomfortable, and then moved, and then undecided.

choices.text: Make a quiet list

effects.log: You make a quiet list, in a book you do not show anyone, and the list has more names on it than you expected.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, you are raised a rank, and {npc} is the first to congratulate you, and the last to stop looking at the new robes. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Take the lesson

effects.log: You take the lesson, which is a long one, and put it to work in the next decade.

choices.text: Make the most of the lull

effects.log: You make the most of the lull, and by its end you are quite a different person.

choices.text: Walk over and speak to them

effects.log: You walk over, and speak, and the speaking is the whole thing.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {npc} proposes a duel with no stakes at all: no seats, no honour, no witnesses, just to see. It frightens you more than the others. The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Use the thing you have been hiding

ok.log: The hidden thing lands, and the Court gasps, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

fail.log: The hidden thing is read as it lands, and answered, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

choices.text: Hold the draw and call it fair

effects.log: You hold the draw, and call it fair, and the Court is both disappointed and relieved.

choices.text: Withdraw with a bow

effects.log: You withdraw with a bow, so full and strange that {npc} is the one left flustered.

events.text: In front of two ministers, {npc} corrects your pronunciation of a word you coined. There is no good reply, only several bad ones.

choices.text: Smile, and invite them to tea

effects.log: The invitation is accepted, to the horror of both parties, and the tea is long and strange.

choices.text: Leave a note on their desk

effects.log: You leave a note on {npc}'s desk, one line, and it is found, and it is not mentioned, and it is not forgotten.

choices.text: Ignore it entirely

effects.log: You ignore it so completely that it begins to look like a decision, and then like a victory.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, you find that someone has paid off your debt to the Star Sea seers. The receipt is in {npc}'s hand, a little shaky with pride. It is the most irritating kindness of your life.

choices.text: Admit, to yourself, that you misjudged

effects.log: You write it in your private book, and underline it, and do not look at it again.

choices.text: Tell the Court what they did

effects.log: You tell the Court, and the Court blinks, and {npc} never forgives you, quite, and never ceases to be grateful either.

choices.text: Say nothing at all, and nod

effects.log: You nod, once, across the room. It is a very small nod. It carries a very great deal.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, {npc} has challenged you to a duel of calligraphy, which is a joke, and which is also not a joke. The whole stair has taken sides.

choices.text: Step aside gracefully

effects.log: You step aside with a grace that is not entirely a performance, and a few watching are quite moved.

choices.text: Press the claim

ok.log: You press, and the claim holds, and {npc} bows, which is new, and goes away to train, which is not.

fail.log: You press, and the claim does not hold, and your pride takes the blow.

choices.text: Ask the Court to decide

effects.log: You ask the Court to decide. It takes a decade, and in that decade you each learn how well the other waits.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, you discover a footnote in a famous book: "see {npc}'s unpublished remark". The remark is yours, repeated over tea. The ink is dry, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Counter with a raceter story

effects.log: You tell a better story, with fewer errors, and the room is moved in the other direction.

choices.text: Ask the witnesses to speak

effects.log: The witnesses speak. Two of them remember. One of them remembers wrongly, in {npc}'s favour.

choices.text: Take the lesson and keep the receipts

effects.log: You keep every receipt thereafter, and your records become the envy of the isles.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, a storm of falling stars is due, and the Pavilion says two must hold the north stair. The names read: you and {npc}. The old quarrel will have to wait its turn.

choices.text: Take the front, without being asked

effects.log: You take the front. {npc} notes it, and does not argue, and later says only "You were always going to."

choices.text: Take the rear, and trust the front

effects.log: You take the rear, and trust, and the trust is the thing you will remember.

choices.text: Improvise, and ask them to follow

effects.log: You improvise, and {npc} follows, and the whole thing works, to the surprise of both.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, {npc} admits, in a flat voice, that they have not slept well since the Court ranked you above them, and cannot say why. The cloud-sea goes on being very large.

choices.text: Confess you envy them

effects.log: You confess you envy them. {npc} says "Of course you do," and then, much more quietly, "And I you."

choices.text: Say you will not forget this

effects.log: You say you will not forget it, and you do not, and it comes up at the strangest times.

choices.text: Leave first, so they need not

effects.log: You leave first, so that they will not have to. It is the kindest thing you can think of, and they know.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, {npc} has taken a very promising pupil of yours as a guest-scholar, "just for a season", with a cake. Loyalty at this altitude is a seasonal crop.

choices.text: Raise a toast to the departing

effects.log: You raise a toast, and the room, taken by surprise, joins in, and the departure becomes a feast.

choices.text: Offer a raceter seat

effects.log: You offer a better seat, and the seat, in the end, is the whole matter.

choices.text: Let the quarrel carry on elsewhere

effects.log: You let the quarrel carry on elsewhere, and discover you have a good deal more peace than you had thought.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, {npc} falls ill with a long, quiet illness, and for a season the rivalry has nothing to push against. The scales tip, as scales do.

choices.text: Hold your head up

effects.log: You hold your head up, and the Court, noting it, adjusts its opinion.

choices.text: Take a quiet year

effects.log: You take a quiet year, and the year is exactly what you needed.

choices.text: Challenge them to measure the gap

effects.log: You challenge them to measure the gap, and the measurement, whatever it is, is the beginning of the next chapter.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, you and {npc} are asked to demonstrate a form for visiting envoys, and the form has no way of ending in a draw. Both of you know the rules and neither is following them.

choices.text: Take the match

ok.log: You take it, and you hear it ring for a week, and it is not as sweet as you had planned.

fail.log: You lose it, and hear the sound of it for a week, and it is not as bitter as you had feared.

choices.text: Yield the field to them

effects.log: You yield the field, which is a great deal harder than winning it, and everyone sees.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch at once

effects.log: You ask for a rematch at once. They are delighted, and appalled, and agree.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {npc} sends a gift of one pressed leaf from the stair you climbed in your third century, with no note. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Answer with a line of your own

ok.log: Your answer is repeated all over by evening, and {npc} is not the one repeating it.

fail.log: Your answer lands a beat late, and {npc} thanks you for it, warmly.

choices.text: Say nothing, and bow correctly

effects.log: You bow to the last hair, and the silence is worth more than any speech you had ready.

choices.text: Laugh, and mean it

effects.log: You laugh, and for a moment {npc} looks as if something kind had struck them from behind.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {npc} lends you a sword for an audience at which yours was refused, with the stern remark that it is to be returned clean. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Accept it, and say thank you properly

effects.log: You say thank you, in full form. {npc} goes stiff, then pink, and leaves in a dignified hurry.

choices.text: Accept it, and say nothing

effects.log: You take the help and say nothing, and the nothing is understood, and is also, somehow, a debt of its own.

choices.text: Refuse it, politely

effects.log: You refuse, politely, and {npc} goes away with the look of someone who has lost an argument they did not know they were in.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, the question of who first crossed the Eighth Bridge has gone to arbitration, and {npc} has brought three witnesses and a map. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Meet it head on

ok.log: You take it, narrowly, and the Court talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: You lose it by a hair, and the hair is the thing everyone remembers.

choices.text: Withdraw, and choose another field

effects.log: You withdraw with grace, and choose another field, and {npc} is left in possession of an empty victory.

choices.text: Propose terms

effects.log: You propose terms. {npc} reads them twice, and accepts three, and sends back a counter-proposal that is a work of art.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, Your disciple returns from {npc}'s lecture quoting you at length, and with no idea that is what they are doing. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Correct the record, with sources

effects.log: You correct it with sources, politely and in detail, and the correction is longer than the original, and read.

choices.text: Let it stand, and do better work

effects.log: You let it stand and do better work, and in time the work corrects the record on its own.

choices.text: Confront {npc} in private

ok.log: {npc} admits it, in the end, in a voice that costs them a great deal, and offers a retraction.

fail.log: {npc} denies it with such grace that you almost believe it yourself.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, the Jade Void's great sword sings and will not be still, and the elders are away. {npc} looks at you across the courtyard. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Hold your side with everything you have

ok.log: Your side holds, and so does theirs, and in the grey morning you are both still standing.

fail.log: Your side gives a little, and {npc} catches the slack without a word.

choices.text: Trust them with the dangerous half

effects.log: You hand {npc} the dangerous half, and they take it without a flicker, and it is the greatest compliment you have ever paid.

choices.text: Split the work by temper, not by rank

effects.log: You split it by temper. It is a raceter division than rank would have made, and the two of you are pleased in spite of yourselves.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, you and {npc} are the last two awake at a very old funeral. They say the dead one was the only person who ever told them the truth. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Say the true thing

effects.log: You say the true thing, and {npc} stares at it as if it were a bird that had landed on the table.

choices.text: Stay, and say nothing

effects.log: You stay, and the silence is the answer, and the two of you are quiet until the lamps need trimming.

choices.text: Make a joke, gently

effects.log: You make the joke, gently, and {npc} laughs, and the evening turns toward warmth.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, the Pavilion's best seer has stopped calling on you and begun calling on {npc}, and says the stars changed their minds. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You let them go, with a proper blessing, and the blessing is meant, and costs more than a refusal.

choices.text: Win them back

ok.log: You win them back with an offer that has nothing to do with money, and everything to do with remembering.

fail.log: You make the offer, and it is taken as an insult, and they leave faster.

choices.text: Counter-poach, politely

effects.log: You turn up with a polite offer to one of {npc}'s best, and the dance of the long quarrel gains a new step.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, a stumble of yours at the Court is the talk of the week. {npc} is conspicuously not talking, which everyone notices. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Congratulate them sincerely

effects.log: You write a very short note, and it is sincere, and {npc} reads it a great many times.

choices.text: Quietly resolve to catch up

effects.log: You resolve to catch up, and the resolve lasts a decade, and works.

choices.text: Do nothing, and feel it

effects.log: You do nothing, and feel all of it, and the feeling is a kind of work too.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, {npc} has found your weak side, the one you thought hidden, and is walking toward it with the patience of a century. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Accept, and give it everything

ok.log: You win it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

fail.log: You lose it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

choices.text: Postpone it a decade

effects.log: You postpone it a decade. They accept, with a tight, unreadable smile.

choices.text: Offer a different test

effects.log: You offer a different test, of patience, of memory, of something less showy. They accept, and it is harder.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, {npc} has taken the seat that was kept for you, and is already deep in a conversation about you. The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Ask a pointed question in return

effects.log: Your question is so reasonable that the answer takes a quarter of an hour, and {npc} is not the one who enjoys it.

choices.text: Let it pass, and note it

effects.log: You file it, as you file everything about {npc}, in the part of the memory that does not forget.

choices.text: Return the courtesy with interest

ok.log: The Court admires the return, and {npc} is quiet for a full day.

fail.log: The return is too sharp, and the room takes against the sharper of you.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, {npc} arrives at your hour of need already carrying the right tool, and looks furious that it was the right one. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send back something of equal weight

effects.log: You return the favour exactly, to the ounce, and the exactness is the message.

choices.text: Say thanks in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {npc} in public, which they hate, and which the Court is delighted by.

choices.text: Keep the debt and think about it

effects.log: You keep the debt in a drawer, and take it out on slow evenings, and turn it over.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, {npc} has been named to teach the course you wanted, and sits very still, determined not to be pleased. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Outwork them

ok.log: You outwork them by a month, and the month decides it.

fail.log: You are outworked by a week, and the week stings more than a year would.

choices.text: Let them have it

effects.log: You let them have it, and they know you let them, and it is the one thing they cannot forgive.

choices.text: Share it, if the rules allow

effects.log: The rules do not allow. You find a way. The result pleases nobody, and is remembered as fair.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {npc} names a new form after you. It is a very good form. It is also the one you were saving. It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Publish your version at once

effects.log: Your version appears within the month, and it is clear, and plain, and hurries the matter along.

choices.text: Tell a friend and let it travel

effects.log: You tell one friend, and the story travels. By the next season, the truth has put its shoes on.

choices.text: Say nothing, and remember

effects.log: You say nothing. You remember. It is a long list, and it is getting tidy.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, a summons in the name of the Court names you and {npc}, and an old debt; whatever it is, it will take both of you to carry it. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Say what must be said, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} says "Yes." The word is a whole treaty.

choices.text: Take the greater risk

ok.log: The risk pays, by a thread, and {npc} looks at you across the wreckage with an entirely new expression.

fail.log: The risk costs you dearly, and {npc} pulls you out, and says nothing about it.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them lead

effects.log: You hold the line and let them lead. It is the hardest thing you have done in a century.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, {npc} shows you a scroll of private notes, on you, a thousand pages long, and says it is the best work they have ever done. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Give them something of yours

effects.log: You give {npc} a small thing of yours. They look at it, then at you, then put it very carefully into a sleeve.

choices.text: Ask them a real question

effects.log: You ask a real question. The answer takes two cups of tea and a century, and is worth it.

choices.text: Keep the distance

effects.log: You keep the distance. You are not sure you were wrong. You are not sure you were right.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, Your quartermaster is now, mysteriously, short of the stones you ordered, and {npc}'s isle is, mysteriously, well supplied. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Raise your own terms

effects.log: You raise your own terms and your own manners, and the staff, noting both, stay.

choices.text: Ask what {npc} offered

effects.log: You ask what was offered, and the answer is both humbler and kinder than you feared.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be a raceter host

effects.log: You say nothing, and become a better host, which is the only reply that lasts.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, {npc} loses a patron, and for a time has no seat at the Court at all, and does not ask you for anything, which is somehow worse. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Go to the celebration

effects.log: You go to the celebration, and bow, and are very good at it, and are carried home by your own dignity.

choices.text: Send a modest gift

effects.log: You send a modest gift, so modest that it becomes a statement, and {npc} does not know what to say.

choices.text: Avoid the whole business

effects.log: You avoid the whole business, and find it follows you down the corridor anyway.

events.text: At the Court's feast of swords, you and {npc} are drawn against one another by lots, and by someone's sense of humour. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Meet them on the first move

ok.log: You take the first move, and the second, and the Court sits up.

fail.log: They take the first move, and the second, and you are left explaining.

choices.text: Spar for form, not for stakes

effects.log: You spar for form, and the form is a pleasure, and neither of you will say so.

choices.text: Decline, and say why

effects.log: You decline, and say why, truthfully, and it is a surprise to both of you.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, {npc} speaks of "friends who remember when you were promising", and makes promising sound like an illness. You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment, loudly

effects.log: You thank them for the kind words, loudly, and {npc} has to carry the rest of the evening on those words.

choices.text: Practise, privately, until midnight

effects.log: You go home and work until the lamps burn low, and the work is better for the insult.

choices.text: Let your reputation answer

effects.log: You answer by doing nothing, and doing it very well, and the room slowly leans your way.

events.text: In a quarrel over precedence, {npc} stands up and says that you came up first. It costs them a year of standing, and they do not mention it. You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Ask why they did it

effects.log: "Because it was correct," says {npc}, and then, after a long moment, "and because it was you."

choices.text: Do not ask, and be grateful

effects.log: You do not ask, and the not asking makes room for something that was not there before.

choices.text: Suspect a trap, and watch

effects.log: You suspect a trap and watch for a year. There is no trap. It stays with you more than a trap would have.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, a new disciple of repute is deciding between your isle and {npc}'s. They are visiting both, and both of you are being very casual. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Appeal to the arbiter

effects.log: The arbiter hears you with the face of someone who has heard everything, and rules for neither, which is a victory of a sort.

choices.text: Win it in front of an audience

ok.log: You win it in full view, and the applause belongs, for once, to you.

fail.log: You lose it in full view, and the sound is of a great many people not saying anything.

choices.text: Concede, but ask a favour

effects.log: You concede, and ask a favour, and {npc} grants it before you finish asking. Neither of you quite knows what to do with this.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, a bard of the lower stairs sings of two immortals who saved an isle. One of the names is {npc}'s, and the order is not right. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment to your work

effects.log: You take it as a compliment. The work was good enough to steal. It is a strange comfort.

choices.text: Demand an apology in open court

ok.log: The apology is made, in the end, and it is exactly as graceless as you had hoped.

fail.log: The demand is heard as pettiness, and the Court takes it out on you.

choices.text: Quietly restore the credit yourself

effects.log: You write the true account in the margins of three copies, in your own hand, and wait.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, you and {npc} are cut off together by a stalled bridge with a night to spend, a lantern between you, and a long list of unfinished remarks. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

effects.log: You stay to the end, and there is a grey dawn, and the two of you sit on the same step and do not talk.

choices.text: Share what you know

effects.log: You share the secret you have kept for a century, and the crisis passes, and the secret is not a secret any more.

choices.text: Take the credit later, and do the work now

effects.log: You do the work now. The credit can be argued about later, and is, with great relish.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, you discover a small shrine in {npc}'s isle, and the tablet on it bears your name, and a date, and the word "measured". For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Take their hand, as a friend might

effects.log: You take their hand, briefly, and both of you recover with great dignity.

choices.text: Say you are tired too

effects.log: You say it. It is the first time you have said it aloud, and it is lighter than you thought.

choices.text: Change the subject to swords

effects.log: You talk about swords until it is safe. Both of you are relieved, and a little disappointed.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a friend of three centuries sends a stiff note: they have accepted {npc}'s offer, and hope you will understand. Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Take it as a warning

effects.log: You take it as a warning, and spend a decade tidying the cracks you had stopped looking at.

choices.text: Confront {npc} directly

effects.log: You confront {npc}, who is entirely unrepentant and entirely charming, and offers you a chair.

choices.text: Outbid them quietly

ok.log: You outbid them quietly, and the quiet is the best part of it.

fail.log: You outbid them, and the bid is a little too loud, and the Court hears.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, a new talent, a very young one, appears and overtakes both of you in a decade. You and {npc} exchange a glance. It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Seize the moment and press the advantage

effects.log: You press the advantage, and for a season you are the one the Court looks at.

choices.text: Reach out, now, while it matters

effects.log: You reach out, now, when it would be easy not to, and it is accepted with a stiffness that is also gratitude.

choices.text: Say a prayer for them, privately

effects.log: You say a prayer for them, privately. You are surprised by how much you mean it.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, a match with {npc} on a bridge of cloud, the rule being that the loser must walk home on the other side. Neither of you has ever lost gracefully. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Fight your best fight

ok.log: It is your best fight, and the one you will describe on the day you die.

fail.log: It is your best fight, and it is not enough, and it is better than most victories.

choices.text: Ask for a witness you trust

effects.log: You ask for a witness you trust, and the match is fair, and the result is accepted even by those who lose it.

choices.text: Make it a lesson, not a duel

effects.log: You turn the duel into a lesson, for yourself, and let them win the points while you win the thing under the points.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, a poem about an immortal who counts every step has appeared on the walls. Everybody knows who it is about, and that {npc} wrote it. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Cut them with a quotation

ok.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has not read, and they feel its edge for a year.

fail.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has, and has annotated.

choices.text: Compliment them back, a little too well

effects.log: You praise {npc} so thoroughly and so exactly that the praise itself becomes a kind of reproach.

choices.text: Walk out with great dignity

effects.log: You walk out without haste, and the talk follows you, and the dignity is the main topic.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {npc} mends a bridge rope you were about to cross, saying it was an eyesore and has nothing to do with you. It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Pay it back at the first chance

effects.log: The first chance comes in four years, and you take it, and {npc} accepts it with the look of someone paid in the right coin.

choices.text: Offer a drink, as one equal to another

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} looks at theirs as if it might bite, and drinks it.

choices.text: Receive it, then beat them anyway

effects.log: You take the help, and the next time you face them, you win, and neither of you says a word of the other thing.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, {npc} posted a better time on the stair-race than yours, and has offered to run it again "if that would help". It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Prepare in silence for a decade

effects.log: You go quiet for ten years. When you come out, the field has changed, and so have you.

choices.text: Send a friendly note

effects.log: The note is friendly and perfectly unnerving, and {npc} loses a night's sleep over it.

choices.text: Take it by surprise

ok.log: The surprise lands, and for once the cloud falls your way.

fail.log: The surprise falls flat, and so do you, a little.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, a sword manual on the highest shelf cites you eleven times and, in the preface, thanks {npc} for "the inspiration". Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Thank {npc} for the attention

effects.log: You thank {npc} for the attention, so sweetly that it is reported as a threat, and so it is.

choices.text: Outrun it with new work

effects.log: You publish something new, that cannot be misattributed, and say very little about the old.

choices.text: Forgive it, and mean it

effects.log: You forgive it. The forgiving takes a year, not a moment, and leaves you lighter than a victory would.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, a fire breaks out in the library you both used as children, and {npc} has already gone in. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Face it together

ok.log: Together, you are better than either alone, and you both pretend not to notice.

fail.log: Together, you are not enough, and you both know it, and neither says so.

choices.text: Hold back, and watch what they do

effects.log: You hold back and watch. What they do tells you everything about them, and you are rather ashamed of the watching.

choices.text: Call for help from everyone

effects.log: You call for everyone, and everyone comes, and the crisis becomes a quarrel about who came first.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, {npc} leaves a sword form at your door, unsigned, with one error deliberately written in. You know it is theirs by the error. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Offer to practise together

effects.log: You offer to practise together. They hesitate for nine hundred years, and say yes.

choices.text: Offer nothing, but remember

effects.log: You offer nothing, but remember, and the memory becomes a warmth you do not deserve and keep anyway.

choices.text: Tell them they were right once

effects.log: You tell {npc} they were right, once, about something long ago. They are quiet for a very long time.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, {npc} has enlisted the cook you trained, whose bean paste had made your name. The taste of the Court is shifting. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Wish them well and mean it

effects.log: You wish them well, and mean it, and find that meaning it makes the loss lighter.

choices.text: Remind them of the old days

effects.log: You remind them of the old days. They look uncomfortable, and then moved, and then undecided.

choices.text: Make a quiet list

effects.log: You make a quiet list, in a book you do not show anyone, and the list has more names on it than you expected.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, you and {npc} are both passed over for the same post, and share a bench in the ante-room, looking at the same painting for an hour. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Take the lesson

effects.log: You take the lesson, which is a long one, and put it to work in the next decade.

choices.text: Make the most of the lull

effects.log: You make the most of the lull, and by its end you are quite a different person.

choices.text: Walk over and speak to them

effects.log: You walk over, and speak, and the speaking is the whole thing.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, {npc} asks for a duel in the garden, at night, with the lamps put out, "to see which of us is really seeing". The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Use the thing you have been hiding

ok.log: The hidden thing lands, and the Court gasps, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

fail.log: The hidden thing is read as it lands, and answered, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

choices.text: Hold the draw and call it fair

effects.log: You hold the draw, and call it fair, and the Court is both disappointed and relieved.

choices.text: Withdraw with a bow

effects.log: You withdraw with a bow, so full and strange that {npc} is the one left flustered.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, {npc} introduces you to a visiting envoy as "my oldest competitor", with such warmth that it is difficult to take offence. There is no good reply, only several bad ones.

choices.text: Smile, and invite them to tea

effects.log: The invitation is accepted, to the horror of both parties, and the tea is long and strange.

choices.text: Leave a note on their desk

effects.log: You leave a note on {npc}'s desk, one line, and it is found, and it is not mentioned, and it is not forgotten.

choices.text: Ignore it entirely

effects.log: You ignore it so completely that it begins to look like a decision, and then like a victory.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, {npc} sends a physician from their own isle when you were ill, and a note: "Get well so I can win properly." It is the most irritating kindness of your life.

choices.text: Admit, to yourself, that you misjudged

effects.log: You write it in your private book, and underline it, and do not look at it again.

choices.text: Tell the Court what they did

effects.log: You tell the Court, and the Court blinks, and {npc} never forgives you, quite, and never ceases to be grateful either.

choices.text: Say nothing at all, and nod

effects.log: You nod, once, across the room. It is a very small nod. It carries a very great deal.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, the Court asks the two of you to settle a border between your holdings. {npc} arrives with surveyors and a picnic. The whole stair has taken sides.

choices.text: Step aside gracefully

effects.log: You step aside with a grace that is not entirely a performance, and a few watching are quite moved.

choices.text: Press the claim

ok.log: You press, and the claim holds, and {npc} bows, which is new, and goes away to train, which is not.

fail.log: You press, and the claim does not hold, and your pride takes the blow.

choices.text: Ask the Court to decide

effects.log: You ask the Court to decide. It takes a decade, and in that decade you each learn how well the other waits.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, a rival's student wins a prize with your method, and thanks {npc} from the stage. The ink is dry, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Counter with a raceter story

effects.log: You tell a better story, with fewer errors, and the room is moved in the other direction.

choices.text: Ask the witnesses to speak

effects.log: The witnesses speak. Two of them remember. One of them remembers wrongly, in {npc}'s favour.

choices.text: Take the lesson and keep the receipts

effects.log: You keep every receipt thereafter, and your records become the envy of the isles.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, a cloud-beast of the old kind has come to drink at your gate. {npc} is on the roof, and has a plan, and no pride about it. The old quarrel will have to wait its turn.

choices.text: Take the front, without being asked

effects.log: You take the front. {npc} notes it, and does not argue, and later says only "You were always going to."

choices.text: Take the rear, and trust the front

effects.log: You take the rear, and trust, and the trust is the thing you will remember.

choices.text: Improvise, and ask them to follow

effects.log: You improvise, and {npc} follows, and the whole thing works, to the surprise of both.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, {npc} says in passing, at a ministry gathering, that they are tired. Then they look horrified, and leave. The cloud-sea goes on being very large.

choices.text: Confess you envy them

effects.log: You confess you envy them. {npc} says "Of course you do," and then, much more quietly, "And I you."

choices.text: Say you will not forget this

effects.log: You say you will not forget it, and you do not, and it comes up at the strangest times.

choices.text: Leave first, so they need not

effects.log: You leave first, so that they will not have to. It is the kindest thing you can think of, and they know.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, {npc} turns up at your disciple's wedding as a guest of honour, and gives a speech that is, annoyingly, wonderful. Loyalty at this altitude is a seasonal crop.

choices.text: Raise a toast to the departing

effects.log: You raise a toast, and the room, taken by surprise, joins in, and the departure becomes a feast.

choices.text: Offer a raceter seat

effects.log: You offer a better seat, and the seat, in the end, is the whole matter.

choices.text: Let the quarrel carry on elsewhere

effects.log: You let the quarrel carry on elsewhere, and discover you have a good deal more peace than you had thought.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, {npc} has retired to a hermitage for a season. Their isle is shuttered. You catch yourself walking by it. The scales tip, as scales do.

choices.text: Hold your head up

effects.log: You hold your head up, and the Court, noting it, adjusts its opinion.

choices.text: Take a quiet year

effects.log: You take a quiet year, and the year is exactly what you needed.

choices.text: Challenge them to measure the gap

effects.log: You challenge them to measure the gap, and the measurement, whatever it is, is the beginning of the next chapter.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, a form {npc} has invented to beat you stands waiting. You can feel it from across the court, polished, patient, rude. Both of you know the rules and neither is following them.

choices.text: Take the match

ok.log: You take it, and you hear it ring for a week, and it is not as sweet as you had planned.

fail.log: You lose it, and hear the sound of it for a week, and it is not as bitter as you had feared.

choices.text: Yield the field to them

effects.log: You yield the field, which is a great deal harder than winning it, and everyone sees.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch at once

effects.log: You ask for a rematch at once. They are delighted, and appalled, and agree.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {npc} publicly wishes you a very long life, so that you might finally catch up. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Answer with a line of your own

ok.log: Your answer is repeated all over by evening, and {npc} is not the one repeating it.

fail.log: Your answer lands a beat late, and {npc} thanks you for it, warmly.

choices.text: Say nothing, and bow correctly

effects.log: You bow to the last hair, and the silence is worth more than any speech you had ready.

choices.text: Laugh, and mean it

effects.log: You laugh, and for a moment {npc} looks as if something kind had struck them from behind.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a rumour that would have ruined you dies a strange death at {npc}'s door, and nobody will say how. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Accept it, and say thank you properly

effects.log: You say thank you, in full form. {npc} goes stiff, then pink, and leaves in a dignified hurry.

choices.text: Accept it, and say nothing

effects.log: You take the help and say nothing, and the nothing is understood, and is also, somehow, a debt of its own.

choices.text: Refuse it, politely

effects.log: You refuse, politely, and {npc} goes away with the look of someone who has lost an argument they did not know they were in.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, There is only one cloud-whale left for hire this season, and you and {npc} have sent the same message to its keeper. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Meet it head on

ok.log: You take it, narrowly, and the Court talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: You lose it by a hair, and the hair is the thing everyone remembers.

choices.text: Withdraw, and choose another field

effects.log: You withdraw with grace, and choose another field, and {npc} is left in possession of an empty victory.

choices.text: Propose terms

effects.log: You propose terms. {npc} reads them twice, and accepts three, and sends back a counter-proposal that is a work of art.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, the Jade Court's annals record a victory with {npc}'s name large and yours small, in a hand you suspect was chosen. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Correct the record, with sources

effects.log: You correct it with sources, politely and in detail, and the correction is longer than the original, and read.

choices.text: Let it stand, and do better work

effects.log: You let it stand and do better work, and in time the work corrects the record on its own.

choices.text: Confront {npc} in private

ok.log: {npc} admits it, in the end, in a voice that costs them a great deal, and offers a retraction.

fail.log: {npc} denies it with such grace that you almost believe it yourself.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, the sea of clouds begins to draw down, as it does every nine hundred years. You and {npc} are the two nearest the lowest stair. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Hold your side with everything you have

ok.log: Your side holds, and so does theirs, and in the grey morning you are both still standing.

fail.log: Your side gives a little, and {npc} catches the slack without a word.

choices.text: Trust them with the dangerous half

effects.log: You hand {npc} the dangerous half, and they take it without a flicker, and it is the greatest compliment you have ever paid.

choices.text: Split the work by temper, not by rank

effects.log: You split it by temper. It is a raceter division than rank would have made, and the two of you are pleased in spite of yourselves.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {npc} asks you to teach them one thing, only one, the thing you do before a fight. They say it so lightly that it must have taken a century to say. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Say the true thing

effects.log: You say the true thing, and {npc} stares at it as if it were a bird that had landed on the table.

choices.text: Stay, and say nothing

effects.log: You stay, and the silence is the answer, and the two of you are quiet until the lamps need trimming.

choices.text: Make a joke, gently

effects.log: You make the joke, gently, and {npc} laughs, and the evening turns toward warmth.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, Two of your best sentries now wear {npc}'s ribbon, and salute you with the faintly apologetic care of the newly employed. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You let them go, with a proper blessing, and the blessing is meant, and costs more than a refusal.

choices.text: Win them back

ok.log: You win them back with an offer that has nothing to do with money, and everything to do with remembering.

fail.log: You make the offer, and it is taken as an insult, and they leave faster.

choices.text: Counter-poach, politely

effects.log: You turn up with a polite offer to one of {npc}'s best, and the dance of the long quarrel gains a new step.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, the Court names a new immortal "the pride of the isles", and it is neither of you. You and {npc} meet by accident in the garden afterwards. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Congratulate them sincerely

effects.log: You write a very short note, and it is sincere, and {npc} reads it a great many times.

choices.text: Quietly resolve to catch up
