effects.log: You resolve to catch up, and the resolve lasts a decade, and works.

choices.text: Do nothing, and feel it

effects.log: You do nothing, and feel all of it, and the feeling is a kind of work too.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, {npc} arrives with a new sword and an old grudge and says they're tired of being polite about either. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Accept, and give it everything

ok.log: You win it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

fail.log: You lose it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

choices.text: Postpone it a decade

effects.log: You postpone it a decade. They accept, with a tight, unreadable smile.

choices.text: Offer a different test

effects.log: You offer a different test, of patience, of memory, of something less showy. They accept, and it is harder.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, {npc} yawns, politely, while you are being praised. The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Ask a pointed question in return

effects.log: Your question is so reasonable that the answer takes a quarter of an hour, and {npc} is not the one who enjoys it.

choices.text: Let it pass, and note it

effects.log: You file it, as you file everything about {npc}, in the part of the memory that does not forget.

choices.text: Return the courtesy with interest

ok.log: The Court admires the return, and {npc} is quiet for a full day.

fail.log: The return is too sharp, and the room takes against the sharper of you.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, {npc} turns up at a bad moment to ask a favour, and the favour is small, and plainly the first they have ever asked of anyone. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send back something of equal weight

effects.log: You return the favour exactly, to the ounce, and the exactness is the message.

choices.text: Say thanks in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {npc} in public, which they hate, and which the Court is delighted by.

choices.text: Keep the debt and think about it

effects.log: You keep the debt in a drawer, and take it out on slow evenings, and turn it over.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {npc} has finished the long form, the one you swore nobody would finish in a thousand years. It took nine hundred and ninety. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Outwork them

ok.log: You outwork them by a month, and the month decides it.

fail.log: You are outworked by a week, and the week stings more than a year would.

choices.text: Let them have it

effects.log: You let them have it, and they know you let them, and it is the one thing they cannot forgive.

choices.text: Share it, if the rules allow

effects.log: The rules do not allow. You find a way. The result pleases nobody, and is remembered as fair.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, a gift arrives from the Star Sea: a star chart that has been quietly redrawn to put {npc} nearer the throne than you. It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Publish your version at once

effects.log: Your version appears within the month, and it is clear, and plain, and hurries the matter along.

choices.text: Tell a friend and let it travel

effects.log: You tell one friend, and the story travels. By the next season, the truth has put its shoes on.

choices.text: Say nothing, and remember

effects.log: You say nothing. You remember. It is a long list, and it is getting tidy.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, a false messenger leads you and {npc} to the same empty courtyard. Whoever sent them wanted both of you away from something. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Say what must be said, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} says "Yes." The word is a whole treaty.

choices.text: Take the greater risk

ok.log: The risk pays, by a thread, and {npc} looks at you across the wreckage with an entirely new expression.

fail.log: The risk costs you dearly, and {npc} pulls you out, and says nothing about it.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them lead

effects.log: You hold the line and let them lead. It is the hardest thing you have done in a century.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, you are walking the same path home, and {npc} keeps pace a stride behind you, out of habit, and says nothing the whole way. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Give them something of yours

effects.log: You give {npc} a small thing of yours. They look at it, then at you, then put it very carefully into a sleeve.

choices.text: Ask them a real question

effects.log: You ask a real question. The answer takes two cups of tea and a century, and is worth it.

choices.text: Keep the distance

effects.log: You keep the distance. You are not sure you were wrong. You are not sure you were right.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, a rival of yours both would agree to dislike has been offered a seat at {npc}'s table, and has accepted. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Raise your own terms

effects.log: You raise your own terms and your own manners, and the staff, noting both, stay.

choices.text: Ask what {npc} offered

effects.log: You ask what was offered, and the answer is both humbler and kinder than you feared.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be a raceter host

effects.log: You say nothing, and become a better host, which is the only reply that lasts.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, {npc} announces a very long retreat, forty years, to perfect a form. It is clearly aimed at you, and clearly quite sincere. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Go to the celebration

effects.log: You go to the celebration, and bow, and are very good at it, and are carried home by your own dignity.

choices.text: Send a modest gift

effects.log: You send a modest gift, so modest that it becomes a statement, and {npc} does not know what to say.

choices.text: Avoid the whole business

effects.log: You avoid the whole business, and find it follows you down the corridor anyway.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, you and {npc} have been told to settle your quarrel by the old way before the Court takes sides. The old way is a bridge, a sword, and a bow. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Meet them on the first move

ok.log: You take the first move, and the second, and the Court sits up.

fail.log: They take the first move, and the second, and you are left explaining.

choices.text: Spar for form, not for stakes

effects.log: You spar for form, and the form is a pleasure, and neither of you will say so.

choices.text: Decline, and say why

effects.log: You decline, and say why, truthfully, and it is a surprise to both of you.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, It is reported that {npc} has called your isle "charming". It is not clear that this was meant kindly. It is clear that it was meant. You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment, loudly

effects.log: You thank them for the kind words, loudly, and {npc} has to carry the rest of the evening on those words.

choices.text: Practise, privately, until midnight

effects.log: You go home and work until the lamps burn low, and the work is better for the insult.

choices.text: Let your reputation answer

effects.log: You answer by doing nothing, and doing it very well, and the room slowly leans your way.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, Stranded by a cloud-storm, you shelter on {npc}'s isle. The meals are excellent and the silences are tremendous. You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Ask why they did it

effects.log: "Because it was correct," says {npc}, and then, after a long moment, "and because it was you."

choices.text: Do not ask, and be grateful

effects.log: You do not ask, and the not asking makes room for something that was not there before.

choices.text: Suspect a trap, and watch

effects.log: You suspect a trap and watch for a year. There is no trap. It stays with you more than a trap would have.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, a Ministry examination has placed {npc} and you in the same hall, in adjoining cells, with a thin screen between. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Appeal to the arbiter

effects.log: The arbiter hears you with the face of someone who has heard everything, and rules for neither, which is a victory of a sort.

choices.text: Win it in front of an audience

ok.log: You win it in full view, and the applause belongs, for once, to you.

fail.log: You lose it in full view, and the sound is of a great many people not saying anything.

choices.text: Concede, but ask a favour

effects.log: You concede, and ask a favour, and {npc} grants it before you finish asking. Neither of you quite knows what to do with this.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {npc} is invited to give the memorial address for an old friend of both of you, and gets the story slightly wrong, in your favour. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment to your work

effects.log: You take it as a compliment. The work was good enough to steal. It is a strange comfort.

choices.text: Demand an apology in open court

ok.log: The apology is made, in the end, and it is exactly as graceless as you had hoped.

fail.log: The demand is heard as pettiness, and the Court takes it out on you.

choices.text: Quietly restore the credit yourself

effects.log: You write the true account in the margins of three copies, in your own hand, and wait.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, a child of the lower stairs has fallen into the cloud-sea, and {npc} is a better swimmer than you, and a worse liar. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

effects.log: You stay to the end, and there is a grey dawn, and the two of you sit on the same step and do not talk.

choices.text: Share what you know

effects.log: You share the secret you have kept for a century, and the crisis passes, and the secret is not a secret any more.

choices.text: Take the credit later, and do the work now

effects.log: You do the work now. The credit can be argued about later, and is, with great relish.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, an old song comes on the wind from a tavern on a lower isle, and {npc} hums it, and then stops, caught. For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Take their hand, as a friend might

effects.log: You take their hand, briefly, and both of you recover with great dignity.

choices.text: Say you are tired too

effects.log: You say it. It is the first time you have said it aloud, and it is lighter than you thought.

choices.text: Change the subject to swords

effects.log: You talk about swords until it is safe. Both of you are relieved, and a little disappointed.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, the seamstress who dresses the Court has produced a new robe in {npc}'s colours, and pointedly thanked you for the "inspiration". Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Take it as a warning

effects.log: You take it as a warning, and spend a decade tidying the cracks you had stopped looking at.

choices.text: Confront {npc} directly

effects.log: You confront {npc}, who is entirely unrepentant and entirely charming, and offers you a chair.

choices.text: Outbid them quietly

ok.log: You outbid them quietly, and the quiet is the best part of it.

fail.log: You outbid them, and the bid is a little too loud, and the Court hears.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, you break through, and for one evening are far ahead. {npc} arrives, unannounced, with wine, and says only "Show me". It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Seize the moment and press the advantage

effects.log: You press the advantage, and for a season you are the one the Court looks at.

choices.text: Reach out, now, while it matters

effects.log: You reach out, now, when it would be easy not to, and it is accepted with a stiffness that is also gratitude.

choices.text: Say a prayer for them, privately

effects.log: You say a prayer for them, privately. You are surprised by how much you mean it.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, you and {npc} are arranged, by ministerial ill-humour, to open a festival with a match. The audience has brought snacks. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Fight your best fight

ok.log: It is your best fight, and the one you will describe on the day you die.

fail.log: It is your best fight, and it is not enough, and it is better than most victories.

choices.text: Ask for a witness you trust

effects.log: You ask for a witness you trust, and the match is fair, and the result is accepted even by those who lose it.

choices.text: Make it a lesson, not a duel

effects.log: You turn the duel into a lesson, for yourself, and let them win the points while you win the thing under the points.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {npc} arrives late to your lecture, sits at the back, and takes notes visibly, in a very small hand. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Cut them with a quotation

ok.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has not read, and they feel its edge for a year.

fail.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has, and has annotated.

choices.text: Compliment them back, a little too well

effects.log: You praise {npc} so thoroughly and so exactly that the praise itself becomes a kind of reproach.

choices.text: Walk out with great dignity

effects.log: You walk out without haste, and the talk follows you, and the dignity is the main topic.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, {npc} hands you a scroll: a copy of the one your own master burned. They had it all along, and kept it for you, grimly. It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Pay it back at the first chance

effects.log: The first chance comes in four years, and you take it, and {npc} accepts it with the look of someone paid in the right coin.

choices.text: Offer a drink, as one equal to another

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} looks at theirs as if it might bite, and drinks it.

choices.text: Receive it, then beat them anyway

effects.log: You take the help, and the next time you face them, you win, and neither of you says a word of the other thing.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, {npc} announces a sword demonstration on the very day of yours, at the very hour, on the very next isle. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Prepare in silence for a decade

effects.log: You go quiet for ten years. When you come out, the field has changed, and so have you.

choices.text: Send a friendly note

effects.log: The note is friendly and perfectly unnerving, and {npc} loses a night's sleep over it.

choices.text: Take it by surprise

ok.log: The surprise lands, and for once the cloud falls your way.

fail.log: The surprise falls flat, and so do you, a little.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, the immortals now say "as {npc} proved" about a matter that was proved by you, at some cost, a long time ago. Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Thank {npc} for the attention

effects.log: You thank {npc} for the attention, so sweetly that it is reported as a threat, and so it is.

choices.text: Outrun it with new work

effects.log: You publish something new, that cannot be misattributed, and say very little about the old.

choices.text: Forgive it, and mean it

effects.log: You forgive it. The forgiving takes a year, not a moment, and leaves you lighter than a victory would.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, a fever goes through the isle and you and {npc} are the last on your feet, back to back, one ward each. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Face it together

ok.log: Together, you are better than either alone, and you both pretend not to notice.

fail.log: Together, you are not enough, and you both know it, and neither says so.

choices.text: Hold back, and watch what they do

effects.log: You hold back and watch. What they do tells you everything about them, and you are rather ashamed of the watching.

choices.text: Call for help from everyone

effects.log: You call for everyone, and everyone comes, and the crisis becomes a quarrel about who came first.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, {npc} shows you, without explanation, the first scar you ever gave them, and the date. It has healed very neatly. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Offer to practise together

effects.log: You offer to practise together. They hesitate for nine hundred years, and say yes.

choices.text: Offer nothing, but remember

effects.log: You offer nothing, but remember, and the memory becomes a warmth you do not deserve and keep anyway.

choices.text: Tell them they were right once

effects.log: You tell {npc} they were right, once, about something long ago. They are quiet for a very long time.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, the old keeper of the stairs, who had always saved you a good seat, is retiring to {npc}'s isle. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Wish them well and mean it

effects.log: You wish them well, and mean it, and find that meaning it makes the loss lighter.

choices.text: Remind them of the old days

effects.log: You remind them of the old days. They look uncomfortable, and then moved, and then undecided.

choices.text: Make a quiet list

effects.log: You make a quiet list, in a book you do not show anyone, and the list has more names on it than you expected.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, the first time in a century that {npc} is truly ahead of you, they say nothing. They simply stand a little taller on the stair. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Take the lesson

effects.log: You take the lesson, which is a long one, and put it to work in the next decade.

choices.text: Make the most of the lull

effects.log: You make the most of the lull, and by its end you are quite a different person.

choices.text: Walk over and speak to them

effects.log: You walk over, and speak, and the speaking is the whole thing.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, {npc} wants to see, once, what you would do if you did not win. They want to see your face. They say so. The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Use the thing you have been hiding

ok.log: The hidden thing lands, and the Court gasps, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

fail.log: The hidden thing is read as it lands, and answered, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

choices.text: Hold the draw and call it fair

effects.log: You hold the draw, and call it fair, and the Court is both disappointed and relieved.

choices.text: Withdraw with a bow

effects.log: You withdraw with a bow, so full and strange that {npc} is the one left flustered.

events.text: You have beaten {npc} three times, and the Court has noticed, and so has {he}. {npc} comes to your gate with nothing in {his} hands, and says that {he} can go on, but would rather not. "Name it," {he} says. "Friends, or finished."

choices.text: Friends

effects.log: {npc} is silent. Then {he} says "Good," in the voice of someone who has held a breath for a century.

choices.text: Finished

effects.log: You say finished. {npc} nods, and goes, and does not look back, and it is correct, and it is lonely.

choices.text: Both, in time

effects.log: You say both. {npc} thinks about it for a very long time and agrees, to your surprise, to the first half.

events.text: {npc} bows, deeply, for the third time you have defeated {him}. "I am done," {he} says. "I do not hate you. I am simply out of reasons." It is a hard sentence, and plainly {he} has rehearsed it.

choices.text: Embrace it as an ending

effects.log: You tell {npc} that the quarrel was the best of your centuries. They look as if you had handed them something heavy and warm.

choices.text: Ask them to stay

effects.log: You ask them to stay, and they stay, awkwardly, for tea, and the tea becomes several centuries.

choices.text: Tell them to try again in a hundred years

effects.log: {npc} gives you a look of true despair, and then, slowly, a small smile. "In a hundred years," {he} agrees, and goes.

events.text: After your third victory over {npc}, the stair is oddly quiet. {He} has stopped coming to court. You find {him} at the edge of the isle, looking at the sea of clouds, and sit beside {him}, and for a long time neither of you speaks.

choices.text: Say you were afraid of losing

effects.log: You say you were afraid every time. {npc} laughs, very softly, and says that so was {he}, and the two of you sit there until the light changes.

choices.text: Say nothing, and rise to go

effects.log: You rise, and bow, and go. It is the right ending and it is cold.

choices.text: Offer them your hand

effects.log: {npc} takes it. It is warm, and shaky, and held a moment longer than courtesy requires.

events.text: {npc} sends a message by a disciple: "Three. You have it. I should like the whole matter closed, with a seal, in front of witnesses, so that I do not take it up again at three in the morning, as I will." The seal is already enclosed.

choices.text: Sign it, with witnesses

effects.log: You sign it, in front of two ministers, a priest, and a very surprised cook. The matter is closed, and {npc} sends a cake.

choices.text: Refuse the seal, and keep the friendship

effects.log: You send the seal back, with a note. "I will not close it. I will only stop winning." {npc} sends a longer note.

choices.text: Add a clause

effects.log: You add a clause: "except at stones." {npc} accepts the clause, and the quarrel takes a new, gentler form.

events.text: The third victory over {npc} comes at a feast, in front of everyone, and the sound it makes in the hall is enormous. {npc} gets up, straightens {his} robe, and walks over to you, and the whole hall waits to see what an enemy does in defeat.

choices.text: Bow first

effects.log: You bow first, and so deeply that the hall has a moment to rethink the whole thing. {npc} bows after you, and the matter is, in its odd way, settled.

choices.text: Stand your ground

effects.log: You stand your ground. {npc} looks at you for a long moment, and bows, and goes. The hall is not sure what it has seen.

choices.text: Pour them a cup

effects.log: You pour a cup, and {npc} drinks it, and the hall exhales.

events.text: {npc} comes to you in the winter of the isles, when the clouds are thin, and says, with great formality, that {he} no longer wishes to be your rival. "I wish to be something with a raceter name. I do not know what," {he} adds. "Help me."

choices.text: Offer an old name for it

effects.log: You offer the old word for a friend who is also a whetstone. {npc} turns it over like a coin, and finds it good.

choices.text: Say the name does not matter

effects.log: You say the name does not matter. {npc} says it matters very much, and the argument takes a year, and is the best of your lives.

choices.text: Say you need a rival still

effects.log: You say you need a rival. {npc} says {he} understands, and {he} does, and goes away to be one at a distance.

events.text: When you win the third time, {npc} does not bow. {He} laughs. {He} laughs for a very long time, hands on knees, until the tears come, and when {he} straightens up, {he} says, "Oh, thank the stars. I thought it would never end."

choices.text: Laugh with them

effects.log: You laugh with them. It is the first time you have laughed together, and it goes on for a quarter of an hour, and ends in tea.

choices.text: Ask what they mean

effects.log: You ask what {he} means. {npc} tells you, in six sentences, and you find you have been thinking the same, and neither of you has said it.

choices.text: Bow, and let them go

effects.log: You bow. {npc} bows. They go. The rivalry is done, and the long relief is of a kind that neither of you will name.

events.text: {npc} is waiting at the foot of the stair after your third victory, with a small, plain box. In it is a seal, an old one, the seal of their isle. "Take it," {he} says. "Or throw it in the clouds. Either is an answer."

choices.text: Take it, and keep it

effects.log: You take it. It is heavier than it looks. {npc} watches you pocket it, and for a moment looks as young as a new disciple.

choices.text: Throw it into the clouds

effects.log: You throw it, and it falls a long way, and {npc} watches it go, quietly, and says: "Yes. Thank you."

choices.text: Hand it back, and say "Not yet"

effects.log: You hand it back. {npc} laughs, a little shakily, and puts it away for another century.

events.text: The Court makes a small ceremony of it: three victories, three bows, a scroll. {npc} accepts the scroll with grace. Only you see {his} hand shake. Afterwards, in the corridor, {he} turns to you and says, "Well. Now what do we do?"

choices.text: Suggest dinner

effects.log: You suggest dinner. {npc} considers it for a full minute, and the dinner that follows lasts four days.

choices.text: Suggest a new quarrel

effects.log: You suggest a new quarrel, on a friendlier subject. {npc} is delighted. The next hundred years are mostly about calligraphy.

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: You say you do not know. {npc} nods, and the two of you walk the length of the corridor in a silence that is neither easy nor hostile.

events.text: {npc} has lost to you three times, and the ministers are saying that {he} is finished. You go to see {him}. {He} is in a small room with the shutters closed, and when you enter, {he} looks up and says, "Have you come to gloat? Please do. I shall feel better."

choices.text: Gloat, briefly, for form

effects.log: You gloat for three sentences, and it is so badly done that {npc} actually laughs, and the room opens up like a window.

choices.text: Say they are not finished

effects.log: You say they are not finished, and mean it, and the saying is the thing {npc} was waiting for.

choices.text: Say nothing and leave

effects.log: You leave. At the door, {npc} says "Thank you," very quietly. You will wonder for a century what it was for.

events.text: You win the third time with a move {npc} taught you, years ago, in a spar neither of you called a lesson. {He} sees it, and goes very still, and says, "Where did you get that?" You tell {him}. {He} says nothing for a long time.

choices.text: Say it was a gift

effects.log: "A gift," {npc} repeats. "Yes. I suppose it was." They sit down on the steps, and look as if they have found a coin they lost.

choices.text: Say you stole it

effects.log: "You stole it," {npc} says. "Well. Good. Stealing is the sincerest form." The quarrel ends in an uneasy truce.

choices.text: Offer to teach it back

effects.log: You offer to teach it back. {npc} accepts, stiffly, and the lesson that follows is the beginning of a very long peace.

events.text: {npc} says that three is the number the old masters used. "After three, it is not a contest, it is a habit. I have had enough of habits." {He} puts down {his} sword, quite formally, in front of you, hilt toward you.

choices.text: Pick it up, and hand it back

effects.log: You pick it up, and hand it back, hilt first. {npc} takes it, and something in the air shifts, and settles.

choices.text: Leave it on the ground

effects.log: You leave it. {npc} waits, and then picks it up, and bows. It is a clean ending and it hurts.

choices.text: Take it and keep it a year

effects.log: You keep it a year. When you give it back, {npc} says the edge is better, and the quarrel has a different weather.

events.text: {npc} is on the stairs ahead of you again, as in other lives, and turns, and says, "Third landing. You took the left last time, and it did not end well." {He} remembers. {He} has not forgiven you the left.

choices.text: Duel them, here and now

ok.log: You take the duel, and the White Stairs are very quiet for a very long time, and the result is a thing both of you will remember into the next life.

fail.log: You take the duel, and it goes the way the old stories suggest, and you walk down the stair a little lighter and a little worse.

choices.text: Match wits with them

ok.log: You match wits, and the wit of an old life comes to your help, and {npc} bows, narrowly.

fail.log: You match wits, and {npc} knows you too well, and the wit of an old life is theirs.

choices.text: Sit, and let it rest a while

effects.log: You sit on the step beside {npc}. The stair is cold. Neither of you moves, and for a moment the long argument is only a long afternoon.

events.text: {npc} climbs the White Stairs beside you without a word, and at the ninth landing says, quite pleasantly, "We have done this before." You have the odd sensation of agreeing without knowing.

choices.text: Take the challenge

ok.log: You take it, and for the first time in several lives, the old pattern breaks, and falls your way.

fail.log: You take it, and the old pattern holds, and you hear a very faint sound like a lock turning.

choices.text: Answer with charm, not steel

ok.log: You answer lightly, and {npc} cannot, for the life of them, find the heavy reply, and laughs, defeated by a joke.

fail.log: You answer lightly, and {npc} answers lightly, and somehow you lose the exchange, and are fond of it.

choices.text: Walk on, and let them follow

effects.log: You walk on. After a moment you hear {npc}'s steps behind you, steady, a pace behind. It is a comfort.

events.text: A cold wind comes off the sea of clouds, and {npc} looks at you in it, and says, "You hate the cold, you know. You always have." You did not know. It is true.

choices.text: Fight, and fight clean

ok.log: You fight clean, and win it, and {npc} says "Better," and means it.

fail.log: You fight clean, and {npc} fights cleaner, and you lose well, which is something.

choices.text: Out-think them

ok.log: You out-think them, for once, by a very small margin, and the stair applauds in the silence of the clouds.

fail.log: You try to out-think them, and every thought was theirs first, and the margin is heavy.

choices.text: Ask them what the last life was like

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It takes the night, and by the end you are not sure whether it was theirs or yours.

events.text: {npc} sets a small cup of tea on the stair in front of you, and says, "The last time, we did not get to this part." {He} looks tired in a way that is older than the face.

choices.text: Wait for them to sit

effects.log: You wait, and {npc} waits, and a herald brings a third chair and the Court decides to take it as a joke.

events.text: {npc} finds you on the roof of the library after a gathering and says: "I have been working out how many lives it is. Eleven. I have been counting the ones in which we did not meet, and there are more of those. I do not know which kind I prefer."

choices.text: Say which you prefer

ok.log: You say which you prefer, plainly, and {npc} is quiet for a long while and then says, "So do I." The wind covers the rest.

fail.log: You say which you prefer, and say it badly, and {npc} nods and says "Ah," and the conversation does not recover.

choices.text: Count them together

effects.log: You count them together, using fingers, and arrive at thirteen. {npc} is outraged and delighted.

events.text: A bird of the cloud-sea lands on {npc}'s shoulder and will not leave. It has done this to them in several lives, {he} says, and always dies when {he} does. This one looks at you and then at {npc}, and seems to be waiting for a decision.

choices.text: Offer the bird your wrist

ok.log: You offer your wrist, and the bird steps across, and sits there like a small grey judge. {npc} is very quiet, and a little pleased.

fail.log: You offer your wrist and the bird looks at it and goes back to {npc}'s shoulder, which is a kind of verdict.

choices.text: Leave the bird to choose

effects.log: You leave the bird to choose. It chooses neither, and sits on the rail between you, and watches the sea.

events.text: The Ministry of Rites has set a new rule: the oldest living grudge at the Court will be settled by a public game of stones, and the two oldest are, by the Ministry's count, yours and {npc}'s. A clerk walks to your gate with the board.

choices.text: Play to win

ok.log: You play to win and do: a long, slow, careful game, and {npc} resigns with grace and a bruised hand. The clerk is delighted.

fail.log: You play to win and do not: {npc} traps you on the fourth edge and you lose by a hair. The clerk, apologetic, takes the board home.

choices.text: Play for a draw

effects.log: You play for a draw. The Ministry has no rule for it, and creates one, and names it after the two of you.

events.text: {npc} stands outside the Pavilion in the rain, without an umbrella, looking up at the star-lens, and says, "I wanted to know how long ago it began. The seer says before the stars. I thought you should hear it from me."

choices.text: Ask what they need

ok.log: You ask what they need, and {npc} says "Company," in a small voice, and you give it, and it is enough.

fail.log: You ask what they need and {npc} says "Nothing," too fast, and goes into the rain, and you are left with the question.

choices.text: Offer an umbrella

effects.log: You offer an umbrella. {npc} takes it, opens it, and holds it over both of you, in the rain, for a long time.

events.text: A challenge comes to both of you from a third party, a young immortal who wants to defeat "the oldest rivalry of the isles". The challenger has been practising for ten years and arrives with a speech. {npc} sighs and looks at you.

choices.text: Face the challenger together

ok.log: You and {npc} take the challenger on together, from either side, and win, fairly, in a very short time. The challenger bows and asks to be taught.

fail.log: You and {npc} take the challenger on and get in each other's way; the challenger wins by sheer luck and is mortified.

choices.text: Stand aside for the challenger

effects.log: You stand aside and the challenger fights {npc}, who wins gently; afterwards the two of you give the challenger a lesson in the art of losing.

events.text: {npc} has taken to leaving small gifts at your door in the night: a pressed leaf, a button, a coin of the old kind. You have been leaving gifts at {npc}'s door too. Neither of you has said so, and on the night of the great bell you meet in the lane, both holding something.

choices.text: Hand over your gift first

ok.log: You hand yours over first, a small jade fish, and {npc} grins and produces a tiny jade fish, the same, from a sleeve. It is uncanny.

fail.log: You hand yours over first, a plain button, and {npc} hands you theirs, a gold coin. The imbalance hangs in the air, and then you both laugh.

choices.text: Put the gifts away, unspoken

effects.log: You put the gifts away, unspoken, and walk home with the one in your pocket that is not yours.

events.text: An old song from the Demon Realm, played by a wandering band in the lower market, makes {npc} stop dead. It is a song about two warriors who were never sure which of them was the shadow. {He} looks at you and does not smile.

choices.text: Ask the band to play it again

ok.log: You ask for the song again and the band obliges, and {npc} listens with you this time. You stay for the whole thing, and for the one after.

fail.log: You ask for it again, but too brightly, and {npc} turns and leaves in the middle of the second verse.

choices.text: Walk {npc} home

effects.log: You walk {npc} home. At the door, they say, "I do not think it is us." You say, "No." And neither of you is quite sure.

events.text: On the last night of the old year, the whole Court lights a candle for the grudges it will carry into the next, and each immortal puts a name in the flame. {npc} writes a name on a slip and does not show it. You write one too. The slips go in together.

choices.text: Look at the slips afterwards

ok.log: You look through the ashes and find a corner of {npc}'s slip that bears a single character of your name. It is a kind one.

fail.log: You look through the ashes and find only soot. Whatever {npc} wrote is gone, and so is yours.

choices.text: Leave the ashes alone

effects.log: You leave the ashes alone. In the morning, a gardener sweeps them into the roses.

events.text: At a ministry reception, a young clerk whispers that the chief seer of the Star Sea has foretold that you and {npc} will "meet again at the end". {npc} overhears and says, "I should hope not at the end. The middle will do."

choices.text: Ask the seer yourself

ok.log: You ask the seer. The seer will say only, "That depends how you read the end," and you find the answer, in the end, in the grammar of the question.

fail.log: You ask the seer. The answer is a poem you cannot make sense of, and {npc} makes sense of it first, and keeps it.

choices.text: Laugh it off

effects.log: You laugh it off, and {npc} laughs too, and neither laughs for as long as the other expects.

events.text: {npc} comes to you at the end of a long age, on the white stairs, and says: "I have been your enemy for lives. I would like to stop. If you wish it, I will lay down every claim. If you do not, I will understand." {He} holds out an open hand.

choices.text: Take their hand, and end it

effects.log: You take it. A sound like a great door closing, very softly, in a far room. The knot between you does not break. It changes grain.

choices.text: Refuse, and finish it properly

effects.log: You refuse, and what follows is the last duel, and its winner is not the point. When it is over, the thing between you has a finish.

choices.text: Say you need a year

effects.log: You ask for a year. {npc} nods, gravely, and gives it, and neither of you knows what you will answer.

events.text: The Jade Court calls it the last duel, though nobody is sure why. {npc} comes to the stair without a sword. "You choose," {he} says. "The last blow, or the first honest word."

choices.text: The honest word

effects.log: You say the honest word. It is two syllables. {npc} cries, quietly, and so, you find, do you.

choices.text: The last blow

effects.log: You strike, and it is clean, and it is over, and the stair has never been so quiet. {npc} bows, once, and is gone.

choices.text: Neither, for now

effects.log: You decline both. {npc} looks at you with a kind of fond exhaustion, and says, "As ever."

events.text: {npc} says that the knot between your souls is thin now, worn almost to nothing by use. {He} asks whether you would prefer to cut it, with a clean stroke, or let it be, and fray, and carry what remains, forever, as a friend.

choices.text: Let it be, and carry it

effects.log: You let it be. It frays, and the fraying is slow, and years later you find it has become something like a bridge.

choices.text: Cut it, and be free

effects.log: You cut it. The silence afterwards is the cleanest you have ever heard, and the loneliest, and entirely your own.

choices.text: Say neither

effects.log: You say neither. {npc} smiles, and the knot hums, and both of you pretend not to hear.

events.text: At the end of a thousand years on the stair, {npc} comes to you and kneels. "I yield," {he} says. "Not because you are stronger. Because I am tired of being the thing that is never enough." {He} looks up. "Will you take it?"

choices.text: Raise them up

effects.log: You raise them up, and say that there was never a contest, only two people, and it is the truest thing you have said. {npc} weeps.

choices.text: Accept the yielding

effects.log: You accept. The weight of it settles on you like snow. It is a victory and it is not at all what you wanted.

choices.text: Decline to take it

effects.log: You decline to take it, and decline to give it back, and the matter stays unsettled, and warm.

events.text: You come upon {b3_legend} at the end of a stair that is not on any map, sitting very still. They do not look up. The silence is of the kind that has been practised for centuries and is not, you realise, an insult.

choices.text: Sit down and wait

effects.log: You sit. An hour passes, then a day. When you rise, you have been taught something, though you could not say what.

choices.text: Ask the one question you have

effects.log: You ask. The answer is five words, and it will take you three hundred years to understand all of them.

choices.text: Bow and leave

effects.log: You bow and go. The legend lifts one finger, perhaps a blessing, perhaps a fly. You will never know.

events.text: Everyone has a story of {b3_legend}, and no two agree. You find the legend in a tea-house on an unnamed isle, quite alive, arguing mildly with a pot of tea about its temperature. The tea is losing.

choices.text: Join the argument

effects.log: You take the tea's side. The legend is delighted. The afternoon is long, and unexpectedly useful.

choices.text: Ask which of the stories is true

effects.log: "All of them," says the legend, "in their fashion. Pour me some more."

choices.text: Pay for the tea

effects.log: You pay. The legend accepts, with great seriousness, as if the payment were the point of the visit. Perhaps it was.

events.text: {b3_legend} sees you across a crowded hall at the Jade Court and crosses the room to you, ignoring three ministers. "You," they say. "I have been meaning to look at you." They look for a very long time.

choices.text: Hold the look

effects.log: You hold it. The look goes on, and on, and then ends, and the legend says only "Good", and walks away, leaving the ministers in your debt.

choices.text: Look back, and ask what they see

effects.log: "A very slow fuse," says the legend. "Lit." They are gone before you can ask more.

choices.text: Bow low

effects.log: You bow low. The legend grunts. It is, as far as the Court can tell, an endorsement.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, {b3_legend} is dropping pebbles into the sea of clouds, one at a time, and listening. "There," they say, as you come up. "That one fell a long way. Did you hear?" You did not, but you listen.

choices.text: Drop a pebble yourself

effects.log: You drop one. The legend cocks its head. "Not bad," they say. "Not good, but not bad. You have the ear for it."

choices.text: Ask what they listen for

effects.log: "For when it stops," they say. "It never does. That is the secret. Do not tell anyone."

choices.text: Stand silent beside them

effects.log: You stand beside them. After an hour, the legend sighs, contentedly, and you feel something in you set down a load.

events.text: The isle is nearly empty and the gate unlocked. Inside, {b3_legend} is sweeping a courtyard that looks as if it had never been dirty. They look up, say "Thank goodness, someone to hold the other end," and hand you a broom.

choices.text: Sweep

effects.log: You sweep. It takes three days. At the end of it, the legend inspects the yard, and nods, and you have the odd sense of having passed an examination.

choices.text: Ask why this courtyard

effects.log: "Because somebody must," says the legend, and leaves it at that, and it stays with you for a thousand years.

choices.text: Hand it back, politely

effects.log: You decline the broom, with an apology. The legend smiles, takes it, and goes on sweeping, quite unoffended.

events.text: You meet {b3_legend} at a ferry landing between isles, both of you waiting for a boat that has not come in forty years. They tell you the boat is coming. They say it with such confidence that you begin to feel it, too.

choices.text: Wait with them

effects.log: You wait. Nothing arrives. But the waiting has a shape, and the shape is a lesson in patience of the kind that cannot be hurried.

choices.text: Ask what they are waiting for

effects.log: "For the next thing," they say. "It is always the next thing." You note it down, and cannot read the note later.

choices.text: Offer to row

effects.log: You offer to row, and the legend laughs until it has to sit down, and accepts, and you row the whole afternoon, round and round in sunlight.

events.text: {b3_legend} challenges you to a contest of silence, a strange sort of match, and the stakes, they say, are a single secret each. You are curious enough to accept. The contest lasts three days.

choices.text: Hold the silence to the end

ok.log: You hold it, and in the end it is the legend who speaks first, and gives you the secret, kindly.

fail.log: You break first, and the legend takes your secret with a very gentle expression.

choices.text: Concede at once

effects.log: You concede at once. The legend is a little disappointed, a little pleased, and tells you a smaller secret, as a consolation.

choices.text: Offer a draw

effects.log: You offer a draw, and the legend, to the astonishment of three listening disciples, accepts.

events.text: You find {b3_legend} asleep under a tree on a very small isle, snoring gently, and the tree is shedding petals all over them. You are not sure whether to wake them. A single petal falls on your sleeve, and it is warm.

choices.text: Wake them gently

effects.log: The legend wakes, blinks, and says, "Ah, you again," as if you had met every century. It is a pleasant lie, and you are not sure it is one.

choices.text: Sit and watch the petals

effects.log: You sit. The petals fall. When the legend wakes at last, you are a little calmer than you were.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea beside them

effects.log: You leave a cup. It is cold when they wake, and they drink it anyway, and the gesture is repaid, in time.

events.text: The great gate of an unnamed isle opens before you, and {b3_legend} is standing in the courtyard, looking at the sky. "I have been told," they say, "that you are a person who gets to the point. Get to the point."

choices.text: Say what you want, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. The legend nods, and tells you the one thing you needed, and a second thing, free of charge.

choices.text: Say you have come to learn

effects.log: You say you have come to learn. The legend sighs, "Ah. Everyone says that," and then teaches you anyway.

choices.text: Say you only came to see

effects.log: You say you only came to see. The legend roars with laughter, and for the rest of the afternoon you are a guest.

events.text: Rain, the first in a long age, falls on a tiny shrine at the edge of an isle, and {b3_legend} sits in the doorway, watching it, with the look of someone seeing an old friend. They gesture you in, out of the wet.

choices.text: Sit in the doorway beside them

effects.log: You sit beside them. The rain falls for two days, and nothing is said, and it is the best conversation of your life.

choices.text: Ask whether they remember a rain like it

effects.log: "There was one," says the legend, "and I was not the same after." That is all, and it is a great deal.

choices.text: Leave them to it

effects.log: You go. The rain follows you down the stair for an hour, and then it clears.

events.text: At the lowest landing of the White Stairs, {b3_legend} is picking up the pebbles that fall from above, one at a time, and putting them in a bag. "Somebody has to," they say. "They all come from somewhere."

choices.text: Help them gather

effects.log: You help. The bag is heavy and the work slow, and when you finish, the legend hands you a pebble, a plain one. It is warm.

choices.text: Ask where they go

effects.log: "To the next stair," says the legend. "Always to the next." You watch the pebbles, and see them differently.

choices.text: Offer a bigger bag

effects.log: You offer a bigger bag. The legend looks at it, and at you, and says, "That is the first sensible thing anyone has said all year."

events.text: {b3_legend} has been told that you have a sharp tongue. They ask for a demonstration, in front of an audience of nobody. You are not sure whether it is an invitation or a trap, but the legend waits, patient as a cliff.

choices.text: Show them your best

ok.log: Your best is very good. The legend laughs, applauds, and tells three stories in return, each better.

fail.log: Your best falls flat, and the legend, kindly, pretends not to have heard.

choices.text: Decline, with grace

effects.log: You decline. The legend nods, as if that were the real demonstration.

choices.text: Ask them for theirs

effects.log: They give you theirs. It is one sentence. It is better than your best.

events.text: There is a story that {b3_legend} gives one thing to every traveller who passes, and you have come to see whether it is true. They are leaning on a gatepost, with a bag of small objects at their feet, and look you over with great care.

choices.text: Wait to be given something

effects.log: You wait. They give you a smooth black stone, and tell you to keep it until it is of use. It is very heavy for its size.

choices.text: Ask for something specific

effects.log: You ask. The legend looks at you for a long time, and gives you what you asked, and something else you did not.

choices.text: Offer them something in return

effects.log: You offer a small, plain thing of yours. The legend takes it with the care of a jeweller, and gives you a blessing in the old tongue.

events.text: {b3_legend} is judging a contest of paper lanterns at the edge of the isles, and has no idea they are the judge. You are a bystander. They turn to you and ask which of the lanterns is best. A hundred hopeful makers hold their breath.

choices.text: Choose with care

effects.log: You choose with care, and the legend says you have chosen the same one as they would have, and gives you a very long, warm look.

choices.text: Choose the humblest

effects.log: You pick the humblest. A small child bursts into tears of joy. The legend nods, slowly, and writes something in the air.

choices.text: Say that all are best

effects.log: You say all are best. The legend laughs, and the crowd laughs, and the lanterns rise, a hundred small suns.

events.text: You hear a piece of music from a closed room in a very old isle, and it is more beautiful than anything you have heard in a thousand years. You open the door. {b3_legend} looks up from a battered instrument, and sets it aside, embarrassed.

choices.text: Ask them to play on

effects.log: They play. It is not as good now that they know you are listening, and then it is better, and then it is the best thing you have ever heard.

choices.text: Apologise for the intrusion

effects.log: You apologise. The legend waves a hand. "It was only a tune," they say, and hums the last bar, and you will carry it for centuries.

choices.text: Ask to be taught

effects.log: You ask. They say no, and teach you anyway, in the way that is not a lesson, for three weeks.

events.text: A messenger finds you with a very odd invitation: {b3_legend} wishes to see you, today, at noon, at a particular rock. You go. The legend is there, with a flask, a pair of cups, and the air of someone who has had a long, long walk.

choices.text: Drink with them

effects.log: You drink. The talk is of nothing, for hours, and the nothing is exact, and unforgettable.

choices.text: Ask why you were summoned

effects.log: "Because you were on the list," says the legend, mildly. "I am working through the list." It is a short answer and a long list.

choices.text: Accept the cup, and decline the flask

effects.log: You accept the cup, and decline the flask, and they say that is also the right answer.

events.text: A very old rumour says that {b3_legend} will lend a single blessing to anyone who can show a true scar. You have several. The legend, when found, wants to see all of them, and listens to each of them as though it were a poem.

choices.text: Show all of them, honestly

effects.log: You show them all. The legend is silent a long time, and then gives you a blessing so quiet you only notice it years later.

choices.text: Show one, the oldest

effects.log: You show the oldest. The legend traces it with a finger and says that it has healed well, and that is all, and it is enough.

choices.text: Show none, and tell the story instead

effects.log: You tell the story instead. The legend nods, "That is also a scar," they say, and you feel a great deal lighter.

events.text: Somebody tells you that {b3_legend} has been seen in the market of the lowest isle, haggling, with the vigour of a young merchant, over a bag of dried plums. You go. It is true. They are winning.

choices.text: Help them haggle

effects.log: You help. The legend and you take the merchant for a good deal of plums, and share them on a wall, and it is a fine afternoon.

choices.text: Haggle against them

effects.log: You haggle against them. It is a close fight, and a dear one, and the merchant goes home with a very good story.

choices.text: Buy them the plums

effects.log: You buy the plums. The legend takes them, solemnly, and bows. "I will remember the plums," they say. You hope so.

events.text: The Jade Court has asked {b3_legend} to give a lecture, and they have agreed, and when the day comes they stand at the lectern, look at the three hundred immortals in front of them, and say, "I have nothing to say," and sit down. The hall is silent. Then someone claps.

choices.text: Clap, too

effects.log: You clap. The hall follows. The legend looks up, astonished, and then, very slowly, pleased.

choices.text: Stay seated, and think

effects.log: You stay seated, and think about what had been said by not saying it. The thought will keep you busy for a century.

choices.text: Go up to them afterwards

effects.log: You go up. "That was the best lecture I have ever given," says the legend, softly. "Thank you for not asking what it was about."

events.text: You and {b3_legend} are the only two awake on an isle at four in the morning. The legend is awake because they never sleep. You are awake because you cannot. They offer you a bowl of something warm. It is delicious. You do not ask what it is.

choices.text: Eat in silence

effects.log: You eat in silence. The bowl is warm, and the silence is wide, and when you are done you find the world is slightly less heavy.

choices.text: Ask what it is

effects.log: "Soup," says the legend. "Mostly soup." You decide not to push.

choices.text: Ask what keeps them awake

effects.log: "I am not awake," they say. "I am simply not asleep. There is a difference, and it is the whole of what I know."

events.text: When you reach {b3_legend}'s door, a notice is pinned to it: "Out. Back in a century. Please take a number." There are, truly, a great many numbers, curled on the hook, and the one on the top is yours.

choices.text: Take your number, and wait

effects.log: You take it. You wait. The century passes, in small ways, and when the legend returns, you are still there, and the door opens.

choices.text: Take a number, and go away

effects.log: You take a number, and go, and put it on your shelf, and think of it on odd days with a warm, unfinished feeling.

choices.text: Leave a note beneath it

effects.log: You leave a note. Years later, a reply arrives, one word. It is "Yes."

events.text: There is an old custom on the isles: to meet {b3_legend}, you must come with something to give and nothing to ask. You have thought about this for a long time. You arrive with a loaf of plain bread, and the legend looks at it for a long time.

choices.text: Give the bread

effects.log: The legend takes the bread, and eats it, slowly, and says it is the best they have had. It is not, but they mean it as a kind of blessing.

choices.text: Ask if they would like something else

effects.log: You ask. They say bread is the right thing, and you are the first to bring it in three hundred years.

choices.text: Keep the bread, and give nothing

effects.log: You keep the bread. The legend watches you, and says "Ah," in a tone that is not unkind, and does not say what it means.

events.text: A very small dispute, over a bridge toll of one pebble, has gone to {b3_legend} for judgement, and they have been hearing it for three days. They look at you, a passing traveller, and say, "You. You decide." Both parties turn.

choices.text: Rule for the toll-keeper

effects.log: You rule for the toll-keeper. The traveller grumbles, pays, and then, at the last, grins. The legend nods, and says that is the kind of thing that makes a bridge.

choices.text: Rule for the traveller

effects.log: You rule for the traveller. The toll-keeper takes it with grace, and the legend says, mildly, "Interesting."

choices.text: Make them share it

effects.log: You make them share. Both are unsatisfied. Both go away to tell it as a victory. The legend says that is the best kind of justice.

events.text: You find {b3_legend} in a garden of white stones, rearranging them with infinite care, one by one. Every so often they step back and look, and move one a hair to the left. You realise they have been doing this for a century.

choices.text: Offer to move one

effects.log: You move one. The legend considers it for a long time and moves it back, a hair to the right, and says, "Better." You do not see the difference. You will, in a hundred years.

choices.text: Ask what the garden is for

effects.log: "For being a garden," they say, without turning. "That is all any of us are for."

choices.text: Sit and watch

effects.log: You sit and watch. You watch for three days. At the end of it, the garden looks the same, and you do not.

events.text: {b3_legend} stops you on the stair, with a hand on your sleeve, and says, quite seriously: "You are about to make a mistake. A large one. I cannot say what. I only wanted to say that I will not think less of you."

choices.text: Thank them, and take care

effects.log: You thank them, and take extra care for a century, and the mistake, when it comes, is smaller than it would have been.

choices.text: Ask what the mistake is

effects.log: "I do not know," says the legend. "I am only old, not clever." You have never been so reassured.

choices.text: Go on, regardless

effects.log: You go on, regardless, and make the mistake, and the legend, when you next meet, says nothing about it, and that is the kindest thing.

events.text: Somebody has told {b3_legend} that you have been looking for them for decades, and they have come to your door, mildly annoyed, to find out why. They stand in your doorway, rainy and sceptical, like a very old cat.

choices.text: Invite them in

effects.log: You invite them in. They sit by the fire, and say nothing, and drink three cups of tea, and leave, and the room is warmer for it.

choices.text: Ask your question at once

effects.log: You ask. They answer in a dozen words, and turn to go, and then turn back and add a thirteenth, which is the one that matters.

choices.text: Say you have forgotten the question

effects.log: You say you have forgotten. They look at you for a long moment, and say, "Good. Then you are ready," and walk off, leaving you more confused than ever.

events.text: At a lantern-festival on a very old isle, the crowd parts for {b3_legend} as for a ship, and the legend, spotting you at the edge, takes you by the sleeve and hauls you through, and says to the people: "This one is with me."

choices.text: Go along, smiling

effects.log: You go along. For a night, you are a legend's guest, and the whole isle bows to you, and you are very, very careful where you put your feet.

choices.text: Ask where you are going

effects.log: "Wherever it gets interesting," says the legend, and leads you on, and it gets interesting.

choices.text: Slip away in the crowd

effects.log: You slip away. The legend does not seem to mind. At dawn, you find a lantern at your door, and a smile you cannot place.

events.text: {b3_legend} teaches a class at the lowest school of the isles, for children of the new-risen, and has done for a thousand years. They look up from a lesson about how to hold a brush and say, "Ah, a visitor. Good. You hold it. Show them."

choices.text: Show them the brush

effects.log: You show. The children watch, rapt, and the legend corrects your grip, mildly, in front of all of them. It is a very good lesson.

choices.text: Say you are not a teacher

effects.log: "No one is," says the legend. "Show them anyway." You do, and the children learn from your errors, which is the best kind.

choices.text: Sit among the children

effects.log: You sit among them. It is a very small stool. You learn to hold a brush properly for the first time in a thousand years.

events.text: You wake to find {b3_legend} sitting at the foot of your bed, quite unalarmed, looking at the wall. "I came to borrow a cup of tea," they say. "And then I forgot why I came, and have been sitting here, thinking. Do you mind?"

choices.text: Make them tea

effects.log: You make tea. They sip it, and say it is nearly as good as the tea they came for, and tell you three things you did not know.

choices.text: Ask what they are thinking about

effects.log: "About whether to go on," they say, so simply that you almost miss it. You find you have a great deal to say.

choices.text: Go back to sleep, and let them be

effects.log: You go back to sleep. In the morning they are gone, and a fresh pot of tea sits cooling on the table, and a faint warmth in the cup.

events.text: {b3_legend} stands at the bottom of a great well in the middle of an isle and calls up to you: "Lower me a rope, or leave. I will not be lectured about my choices." You look down. They are not, in fact, in any danger. They are reading.

choices.text: Lower a rope, anyway

effects.log: You lower it. They tie a book to the end and ask you to read it aloud. It is very long, and you read it all.

choices.text: Ask what they are reading

effects.log: "Myself," says the legend, from the dark. "A very old edition. It has some errors."

choices.text: Leave them to it

effects.log: You leave. Years later you find a book on your table, tied with a rope, and an inscription in a very old hand.

events.text: The one fate knotted to you has had a bad century, and you know it the way you know the weather. A messenger would say it was nothing to do with you. Something in you says it is. You find yourself sending a small gift, without a name.

choices.text: Send it anyway

effects.log: You send it. It is received, and traced, and neither of you mentions it, and the knot between you hums quietly.

choices.text: Hold it back

effects.log: You hold it back. The pride is old and the habit older. You will think of it on stairs, for a long time.

choices.text: Send it with your name on it

effects.log: You send it with your name. The reply is three lines, and the third is a joke, which is the best thing it could have been.

events.text: There is an immortal on the White Stairs who looks at you sometimes as if you were a word on the tip of their tongue. You have the same feeling in return. Neither of you has ever spoken of it. Tonight, for no reason, you find yourself saying hello.

choices.text: Say hello properly

effects.log: You say hello properly. It is the beginning of a conversation that will last, on and off, for several centuries.

choices.text: Nod, and go on

effects.log: You nod and go on. It is very correct, and it is a small, odd grief.

choices.text: Ask if they, too, feel it

effects.log: You ask. They look at you with huge, startled eyes, and say "Yes."

events.text: You wake with a name in your mouth that you do not know, and by the end of the day you learn that someone with that name has risen a rank, and that you are, to your shame, rather jealous. You do not know the person. You are quite sure you know them.

choices.text: Send them a note of congratulation

effects.log: You send it. The reply comes by return, and says only: "Thank you. I felt that."

choices.text: Work harder, privately

effects.log: You work harder, for no reason you can name, and in the morning you are a little better than you were.

choices.text: Pretend you did not wake

effects.log: You pretend. It is a very poor pretence, and you carry it all week.

events.text: A seer in the Star Sea Pavilion says, without being asked, that you and someone you have not yet met will be "an old song sung in two keys". You ask who. The seer cannot say. She only says to be kind, when the time comes.

choices.text: Promise you will be kind

effects.log: You promise. The seer looks relieved, and rather sad, and gives you a very small coin, for luck.

choices.text: Ask what happens if you are not

effects.log: "Then you will do it again, in the next life," she says. "It is the only rule."

choices.text: Say you do not believe in songs

effects.log: You say so, loudly. The seer smiles, very kindly, as one smiles at a child.

events.text: The old, unaccountable ache has come back, the one that surfaces in the second week of the autumn rains: that someone is behind you on the stair, a step back, and has been for lives. You turn. There is nobody. There is a lantern, still swinging.

choices.text: Wait for them

effects.log: You wait. For an hour, then two. Nobody comes. But the waiting is a small, warm thing, and you carry it home.

choices.text: Walk on, a little faster

effects.log: You walk on faster. Behind you the lantern swings, and the stair, for a moment, seems to hold its breath.

choices.text: Call out a name you do not know

effects.log: You call a name. The wind brings it back to you. It is, you realise, your own, in somebody else's voice.

events.text: You have a sense, in the middle of a Court dinner, that the one who has been following your fate is in the room, and you scan every face. A stranger at the far end meets your eyes and holds them. Neither of you looks away for a very long time.

choices.text: Cross the room

effects.log: You cross the room. It takes a long time, and a great deal of nerve, and at the end of it there is a very ordinary introduction, and a very unordinary silence.

choices.text: Raise your cup

effects.log: You raise your cup. They raise theirs. That is all. It is a great deal.

choices.text: Look away first

effects.log: You look away. It is a small cowardice, and you will remember it, and the next time you meet, you will not.

events.text: Someone leaves a plum blossom on your windowsill in the night, every year, on the same night. You have never seen them. This year you wait up, and in the small hours, a shadow comes, and stops, and sees you, and does not run.

choices.text: Say thank you

effects.log: You say it. The shadow says "You are welcome," and then, rather quietly, "You always say that."

choices.text: Ask who they are

effects.log: "I do not know," says the shadow. "I only know that I have to." It is, you realise, the truest answer you have heard.

choices.text: Offer them tea

effects.log: You offer. They sit, awkwardly, in the one good chair, and the two of you are quiet for a very long time.

events.text: When you were young, a stranger on the stair said, "I will see you again, whatever happens." You had forgotten. Today, in a corridor of the Jade Court, a pair of eyes meet yours, and a voice from long ago says, softly, "There."

choices.text: Answer, as if you had been waiting

effects.log: You answer. It is the only thing you can do, and it is entirely right, and the rest of the century is never quite the same.

choices.text: Say you do not remember

effects.log: You say you do not. The stranger says, "No. But I will wait." It is an unkind kind of kindness.

choices.text: Walk past, trembling

effects.log: You walk past, and your hands do not stop shaking until midnight.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, {b3_rival} has had a bench carved for the Jade Void's courtyard and had your name cut into the underside, where only people lying down will read it. The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Have the bench set in the middle of the courtyard

effects.log: You have it turned over and set in the courtyard's middle, name to the sky, and the Court sits on it all season, thanking {b3_rival} for the seat.

choices.text: Lie down on it and read the carving aloud

ok.log: You lie back, read your name to the clouds in your best voice, and the stair-keepers applaud the hour {b3_rival} spent on the chisel.

fail.log: You lie back to read it and the bench is damper than the cloud, and the stair-keepers file past a soaked immortal.

choices.text: Sit on it and watch the clouds

effects.log: You sit, and the clouds really are very soft, and the name below you bothers you less each century.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, a fire in your alchemy hall is out before the bells ring. {b3_rival}'s disciples are leaving by the back gate with soot on their faces, and nobody has asked them to. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send a basket of cloud-rice to their gate, unsigned

effects.log: The basket arrives unsigned, and the soot comes off, and the following week your gate is found swept.

choices.text: Rebuild the hall wall they scorched putting it out, and leave no note

effects.log: You rebuild the hall at your own cost and leave no note, and each of you quietly knows the other knows.

choices.text: Say nothing and leave the soot on the back gate

effects.log: The soot stays on the back gate a season, a small black proof, and neither of you mentions it.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {b3_rival} has entered the same exhibition of hanging gardens as you. Both have used the same rare orchid, which was supposed to be a secret. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Show yours first, with a better arrangement

ok.log: Your arrangement is judged the finer, and the ministers, delighted, remark that the orchid was perhaps never a secret at all.

fail.log: Your arrangement is judged the finer, but {b3_rival}'s orchid is the livelier, and the garden goes to them.

choices.text: Swap orchids with {b3_rival} quietly before the judging

effects.log: You swap the pots, and the ministers award a prize to the right orchid in the wrong hands, and you laugh together afterwards.

choices.text: Withdraw the garden and enter the ferns

effects.log: You withdraw the orchid and enter ferns, and the ferns win a small ribbon and the ministers' relief.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, {b3_rival}'s name has been carved on the cornerstone of the new bridge, above the stonemasons' and, by three finger-widths, above your design. It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Have a second line cut beneath the first, naming the design

effects.log: You pay the masons for a second line, and the bridge carries both names, and passers-by assume two founders.

choices.text: Appeal to the Ministry of Works with the original drawings

ok.log: The drawings are in your hand and dated, and the stone is recut with the line corrected and the Ministry's apology.

fail.log: The drawings are missing a sheet, and the Ministry shrugs.

choices.text: Walk across the bridge once a year and say nothing

effects.log: You walk across each spring and your boots know the design better than any stone, and that is a kind of record.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, a great chain of the cloud-bridge snaps overhead while you and {b3_rival} are crossing beneath it, and the pair of you are the only ones near a winch. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Take the winch and tell {b3_rival} to hold the chain

ok.log: You wind the winch together, and the chain takes hold, and for a breath you are only two backs against the sky.

fail.log: The chain slips twice, and you both come out bruised, the bridge half held.

choices.text: Hold the chain yourself and let {b3_rival} work the winch

effects.log: You hold the iron and {b3_rival} winds, and you hear them breathing, and nobody speaks of the hands afterwards.

choices.text: Step back and let the bridge-wardens come

effects.log: You step to the edge, shout for the wardens, and wait, and they come with the proper rope.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, {b3_rival} is sitting on the roof of the empty library at night, watching the sea of clouds go silver, and offers you half a pear without turning round. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Take the half pear and sit beside them in silence

effects.log: You sit, and the pear is sweet, and the cloud-sea goes silver, and neither of you speaks until the stars are out.

choices.text: Ask what they come up here to think about

ok.log: {b3_rival} answers truly, haltingly, about a sister they have not seen in four hundred years, and you listen until the pear is gone.

fail.log: {b3_rival} shrugs and says nothing, and the roof grows chilly.

choices.text: Eat the pear and go down without a word

effects.log: You eat the pear, nod, and climb down the ladder, and the roof is theirs again.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, the Star Sea's best apprentice seer has been seen carrying {b3_rival}'s tea tray, and there are rumours of an offer made in the dark of the moon. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Offer the apprentice a post of their own at twice the pay

effects.log: You make the offer at the Pavilion door, and the apprentice, who is dizzy at the sums, asks for a night to think.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} directly whether an offer was made

ok.log: {b3_rival} answers with unexpected frankness, and the offer was real, and the apprentice stays with you out of pure surprise.

fail.log: {b3_rival} smiles blandly and says it was a mere courtesy, and the apprentice goes.

choices.text: Wish the apprentice well, and teach the next one better

effects.log: You wish them well and take a new apprentice, whom you teach more carefully than you taught the last.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, {b3_rival} is named a Warden of the Eastern Isles, and the lamps of their isle burn the whole night, and you can see them from your bridge. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Light a lamp on your bridge in answer, and keep it burning

effects.log: You light your bridge-lamp each night, and across the water the two lights are watched all season, one on each side.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a note of true congratulation, in plain words

ok.log: The note is two lines, honest, and {b3_rival} keeps it unsealed in their desk, and it is the kindest war in the Court.

fail.log: The note reads, to {b3_rival}, as a taunt, and the lamp across the water burns a little harder.

choices.text: Put out your lamp and sleep, for once

effects.log: You put out the lamp, and sleep like a stone, and wake with the sun on your face.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {b3_rival} proposes a duel of tea-making in the Jade Void's courtyard, a thing not seen since the Second Cloud War, with a Court judge. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Make the tea with the whole Court watching, and win by a leaf

ok.log: Your tea is judged the finer by the Court judge, who sips twice, and the Jade Void courtyard applauds.

fail.log: Your tea is judged too bitter by a leaf, and {b3_rival} accepts the cup with great formality.

choices.text: Propose that you brew one pot together and judge each other

effects.log: You brew one pot, and judge each other, and the Court judge is left with nothing to rule on, and writes it up as a draw.

choices.text: Decline with a bow and offer a seat at your own table

effects.log: You decline, and offer a seat at your own table, and the tea there is excellent, and {b3_rival} comes in the end.

events.text: At the Star Sea Pavilion, {b3_rival} asks the seer to read you "something encouraging", loudly enough that the seer has to charge for it. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Pay the seer double to read it truthfully

effects.log: You pay double for the truth and the seer, startled, gives you three accurate sentences and a discount on the next reading.

choices.text: Ask the seer to read {b3_rival} in return, as an encouragement

ok.log: The seer reads {b3_rival} aloud, gently, and the encouragement is so exactly aimed that the Pavilion goes quiet in admiration of you.

fail.log: The seer reads {b3_rival} a long and glowing future, and the Pavilion warms to {b3_rival} instead.

choices.text: Raise your cup and applaud the craft

effects.log: You lift your cup to {b3_rival} across the pavilion, craftsman to craftsman, and then let the seer finish.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, you find the lost seventh volume of your magnum opus on your desk, rebound, with a repair slip: "Found it in the Star Sea archive. Do not thank me." It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Send back a torn volume of theirs, equally mended

effects.log: You find a torn volume in {b3_rival}'s own style, rebind it, and send it without a note.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival} in the Star Sea archive, in front of the archivist

ok.log: You thank them in front of the archivist, who tells every scholar in the isle by evening.

fail.log: You thank them in front of the archivist, and {b3_rival} flees through the stacks.

choices.text: Read the repair slip twice and keep it in the book

effects.log: You put the slip in the seventh volume, where it still lives, and the book is the better for it.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, the Jade Court holds a race of cloud-boats round the nine isles, and {b3_rival} has refitted their entry with a keel you could swear came from your yard. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Race them, keel for keel

ok.log: Your boat noses past the finish in the last spar-length, and the keel, you feel, was always better in yours.

fail.log: Your boat loses by a spar-length and a half, and the keel wins the argument.

choices.text: Lodge a protest with the race-warden about the keel

effects.log: The warden measures both keels with a string and rules them siblings, and the race goes on, a little warmer.

choices.text: Let them race, and watch from the quay with tea

effects.log: You watch from the quay, and the boats go by in a blur of sail, and the tea is excellent.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, an old woman on the lower isles, asked who invented the weaving-array, says {b3_rival}, with a trust that makes it hard to correct her. Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Teach the old woman the array you actually made

effects.log: You sit with the old woman and weave it together, and she tells it differently the next time, with your name in it.
