choices.text: Mention it to {b3_rival} at the next festival, lightly

ok.log: You mention it, lightly, and {b3_rival} goes pale, and the next time the old woman is asked, she says both names.

fail.log: You mention it lightly, and {b3_rival} laughs it off so well that the old woman hears of it as a joke.

choices.text: Let her keep the tale, and keep the thread

effects.log: The old woman has her tale, and you keep the thread in your pocket, and the array stays the same either way.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, a rogue comet drags a tail of fire across the Nine Clouds Palace, and {b3_rival} is on the roof of the gate-tower holding a bucket of nothing in particular. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Climb the gate-tower and take the other bucket

effects.log: You climb up with a bucket of your own and fill it with cloud, and between you the sparks are put out one by one.

choices.text: Call the Palace's rain-array to the roof

ok.log: The array answers, and a cold shower puts out the comet's tail, and {b3_rival} stands dripping with an empty bucket, laughing.

fail.log: The array coughs and gives a drizzle, and the sparks go on.

choices.text: Watch the comet pass from the lower stair

effects.log: You watch it burn over the Palace from the stair below, and the Palace stands, and the comet goes.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, you catch {b3_rival} on a lower stair practising, alone and badly, a sword form they have always insisted they dislike. They leave in great haste, and forget the sword. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Pick up the forgotten sword and return it, unlooked at

effects.log: You return the sword at their gate, wrapped in cloth, and say only that you found it on the stair.

choices.text: Offer to practise the form with them, on the lower stair

ok.log: You practise together, badly and then not badly, and {b3_rival} admits, at the end, that they have always liked it.

fail.log: {b3_rival} hears the offer as pity, and leaves the stair for good.

choices.text: Watch the form from the shadow and learn it

effects.log: You watch from the shadow until the form is yours, and one day you will use it, and say nothing of its source.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, Your steward of a hundred years announces, with enormous regret, that the Ministry of Works has asked them to oversee {b3_rival}'s new wing. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Give the steward a leaving gift and a fair reference

effects.log: You give a lacquered box and write a reference so warm it embarrasses you, and the steward weeps a little at the gate.

choices.text: Ask the steward what {b3_rival} offered that you could not

ok.log: The steward, after a pause, says "a seat that I would not have to stand behind", and you spend a night reflecting on that.

fail.log: The steward says only that it was time, and the question goes unanswered.

choices.text: Train the under-steward and let the old one go

effects.log: You promote the under-steward, who is nervous and brilliant, and the household runs better by spring.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, you are given a seat at the Jade Court's inner table, and the first to rise and bow is {b3_rival}, who looks as though the bow cost them a tooth. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Bow back, lower than the occasion needs

effects.log: You bow lower than the rite requires, and the inner table sees two immortals at a sort of truce, and {b3_rival} straightens with a wince.

choices.text: Raise a toast to {b3_rival} by name at the first course

ok.log: You toast {b3_rival} by name, and the table drinks, and {b3_rival} has to drink to their own toast, and does so with a grim grace.

fail.log: You toast {b3_rival} a beat too late, and the table drinks without noticing.

choices.text: Take your seat, and speak of the weather

effects.log: You take your seat, and speak of the weather, and the table is relieved by the dullness.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, a match on the white stairs is declared; the loser must walk down backward, and the Court has taken stakes, and {b3_rival} is cheerfully giving odds against themselves. The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Take the match and walk the stairs forward to win

ok.log: You win on the stair, and {b3_rival} walks down backward all nine hundred steps with great cheer and a full set of admirers.

fail.log: You lose on the stair, and walk down backward with great dignity and the Court's eyes on your back.

choices.text: Take a stake against {b3_rival} at their own odds

effects.log: You place a stake on yourself at {b3_rival}'s odds, and the Court, scandalised, adds more, and the whole match becomes a side-show.

choices.text: Decline the match and offer to hold the lantern at the bottom

effects.log: You hold the lantern at the bottom, and the loser is lit safely down, and the quiet crowd goes home.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a visiting Demon Realm general asks which of the immortals present is the famous one. {b3_rival} points at the wrong person, with perfect sincerity, three times. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Correct the general, courteously, in the Demon Realm tongue

effects.log: You name yourself in the general's own tongue and he laughs out loud, and the bridge is more at ease than it has been in a century.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival} for the introduction to the wrong immortal

ok.log: You thank {b3_rival} so warmly that the wrong immortal believes it and brims with pride, and the general decides you are the cleverest on the bridge.

fail.log: Your thanks arrives a beat late and sounds like sulking, and the general, puzzled, bows to the wrong one a fourth time.

choices.text: Stay where you are and let the general work it out

effects.log: You stay by the rail with the cloud-sea slow below, and the general works it out on his own and, privately, rather admires you for it.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, {b3_rival} speaks to the Ministry of the Treasury about the stones owed to your isle, in a tone that gets the stones moved by dusk. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Ask the Treasury how they were persuaded

effects.log: The Treasury clerk smiles and says only that {b3_rival} wrote very politely, which is worse than a threat.

choices.text: Give {b3_rival} a seat at your next council

ok.log: You give them the high seat at the council, and the Treasury sees the isle's friends are well placed.

fail.log: Your offered seat looks like a bribe, and the Treasury clerk writes that down.

choices.text: Spend the stones on the isle's roofs

effects.log: You spend every one on roofs, and the isle is dry for the first time in a century.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, a rare scroll of the Star Sea is up for bid, in the old fashion of a silent auction, and every bidder is a friend of one of you or the other. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Bid just above what you guess {b3_rival} will bid

ok.log: You read {b3_rival} correctly to the stone, and the scroll comes home with you in a wrapper of cloud-silk.

fail.log: You read {b3_rival} a little low, and the scroll goes home in their sleeve.

choices.text: Ask your friends to bid in your name, and tell {b3_rival} so

effects.log: Your friends bid and {b3_rival}'s friends bid, and the Ministry's sums come out so large that both sides withdraw, laughing.

choices.text: Withdraw and ask to read the scroll after the sale

effects.log: You withdraw, and the winner, who is neither of you, lets you read it in the library for a cup of tea.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, a festival play about the founding of your isle has been staged, and the part of the wise immortal is played by someone made up to look like {b3_rival}. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Go to the play and applaud the actor's best moment

effects.log: You applaud at the actor's one good line, and the company, which was told it was {b3_rival}, wonders who you might be.

choices.text: Offer the playwright the real story, over tea

ok.log: The playwright takes notes all night, and the second season of the play has a different wise immortal, and a better one.

fail.log: The playwright takes your story for a dramatic invention and loves it, and the original remains in place.

choices.text: Write the three letters and keep them in a drawer

effects.log: You write all three, very well, and read them over once a decade, and none of them has aged.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, a pack of cloud-wolves has got into the Jade Void's sheep-pens, and the only two immortals awake in the hour of the hare are you and {b3_rival}, in nightclothes. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Drive the wolves out with the shepherd's cry

ok.log: You and {b3_rival} corner the wolves at the pen gate, and they bolt over the edge into the cloud, and the sheep, aggrieved, are counted.

fail.log: The wolves scatter the flock, and you spend the night chasing sheep in the dark.

choices.text: Bar the pen gate and keep the wolves in the dark, at bay

effects.log: You bar the gate from the outside, and {b3_rival} beats a pot, and the wolves eye the bars all night and give up at dawn.

choices.text: Let {b3_rival} take the pens and mind the stairs yourself

effects.log: You hold the stair and {b3_rival} holds the pens, and by the hour of the dragon the sheep are all alive and the nightclothes are ruined.

events.text: On a lull between two ministerial sessions, {b3_rival} asks what you will do when you have won, in a voice that makes it clear they have been wondering for a century. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: you have not planned that far

effects.log: You admit you have no plan beyond winning, and {b3_rival} laughs, a little ruefully, because neither have they.

choices.text: Ask them the same question, and wait

ok.log: {b3_rival} answers at last, in a few words, and the answer is not an enemy's, and you take it home with you.

fail.log: {b3_rival} turns the question into a joke, and the hour closes.

choices.text: Say you will sleep for a decade, and change the subject

effects.log: You say you will sleep for a decade, and the Court bell calls the session, and the question lingers in the corridor.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {b3_rival} has persuaded the lower-stair ferrymen to land at their isle first. You are left waiting at the quay, among the baggage and the disappointed. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Offer the ferrymen a better berth and a proper quay-fee

ok.log: The ferrymen like your quay-fee and your tea and land at your isle first on three days of the week.

fail.log: The ferrymen smile and keep to their routes.

choices.text: Wait among the baggage and talk to the other waiters

effects.log: You wait among the baggage and learn more of the isles from the disappointed than from the Court in a decade.

choices.text: Build a small ferry-stage of your own, below the isle

effects.log: You build a stage for private barges, and the ferrymen, in time, come to your isle in the evenings for supper.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, {b3_rival}'s first treatise is accepted into the Court library, and you learn of it from the shelf-boy who is carrying it, reverently, past your door. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Read the treatise cover to cover before the end of the week

effects.log: You read it all in five nights and find three errors and one idea you wish were yours, and write to {b3_rival} about the idea.

choices.text: Review it in the Court library, honestly and in print

ok.log: Your review is long, fair and exact, and the library prints it as a preface to the second edition.

fail.log: Your review has a mistake in its second page and {b3_rival} writes back with it underlined.

choices.text: Tip the shelf-boy for the trouble and say nothing

effects.log: You tip the boy a ring of copper and let him go, and your door closes on the sound of his feet.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, you and {b3_rival} are made to demonstrate sword forms on the quay, for a delegation from the Demon Realm, and the demonstration is slowly forgotten as it becomes a fight. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Let the demonstration turn into the fight it wants to be

ok.log: The forms turn real by the third exchange, and the Demon Realm delegation stands to watch, and you win by an inch.

fail.log: The forms turn real, and you lose by an inch in front of the delegation.

choices.text: Stop the demonstration and bow to the delegation together with {b3_rival}

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} stop mid-cut and bow, and the delegation, which wanted a fight, gets a lesson in manners.

choices.text: Lower your sword and let the bets go unpaid

effects.log: You lower your sword, and the bets go unpaid, and the quay laughs.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, the Nine Clouds Palace sends out its annual list of the century's notable alchemists. {b3_rival} has been so kind as to write the margin notes on your entry: "present". You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Write "present" beside every entry in {b3_rival}'s margin notes

effects.log: You annotate {b3_rival}'s own entry the same way, and the Palace, which circulates margins, spends a decade not saying which hand is meaner.

choices.text: Petition the Palace to publish your real record

ok.log: Your petition has the dates, and the Palace reprints the list with a corrected entry in a wider margin.

fail.log: Your petition is one date wrong, and the Palace reprints it, as an example.

choices.text: Brew a better elixir, and say nothing

effects.log: You go back to the furnaces and brew the best draught of the century, and "present" starts to look like an understatement.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, a Demon Realm envoy who had been planning to humiliate you at the banquet finds, to his dismay, that {b3_rival} has seated himself beside him and is being very interesting. You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a note across the banquet: "Take your time"

effects.log: You send the note and {b3_rival} keeps the envoy talking until the soup is cold, and you give the speech you wanted to.

choices.text: Join the envoy and {b3_rival} and carry the talk yourself

ok.log: You join them, laugh at the right place, and the envoy, who came to humiliate, gives up and tells you a good story.

fail.log: You join them and the envoy, spotting a fresh target, turns his whole attention on you.

choices.text: Let the envoy be as dreary as he likes

effects.log: You sit at the far end and eat the soup. The envoy never once looks your way.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, the Ministry of Works posts a notice: one new bridge, to the western isles, to be built by whichever of two named immortals can submit a better plan. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Submit a plan with a toll-free western stair

ok.log: Your plan is the cheaper and the cleverer, and the Ministry of Works stamps it before the ink is dry.

fail.log: Your plan has a beam that cannot bear its own load, and the Ministry returns it with a polite sketch.

choices.text: Offer {b3_rival} a joint plan, and split the credit

effects.log: The joint plan is half yours and half {b3_rival}'s and entirely sound, and the Ministry asks which of you drew the bridge. You say both.

choices.text: Withdraw your plan and wait for the Ministry to tire

effects.log: You withdraw, the Ministry tires, and a third plan is chosen, and it is dull, and it stands.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, the Ministry of Records lists {b3_rival} as "coauthor" on a commentary you wrote alone, and your signature has been moved to the footnote. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: File your own signature again, above the commentary

effects.log: You file the commentary a second time with your signature in the title, and the Ministry of Records lists it as a "second edition".

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to withdraw the coauthor line in front of the clerks

ok.log: {b3_rival} withdraws it with a small, stiff bow, and the clerks move your name back up with visible relish.

fail.log: {b3_rival} explains that it was a clerical kindness, and the clerks agree, and leave your name in the footnote.

choices.text: Add a footnote of your own, in the margin of the copy that matters

effects.log: You write a footnote in your copy, and it is an excellent one, and a few readers get that copy instead.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, the star-lamp that guides ships over the cloud-sea goes out, and a convoy of pilgrims is on its way in. {b3_rival} is the only one who knows the old signal. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Trim the star-lamp and light it with the old signal

ok.log: The old signal blinks, three long and one short, and the convoy turns, and nobody in the harbour will ever know who lit it.

fail.log: The old signal blinks wrong, and the convoy turns the wrong way for a minute before righting itself.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to teach you the old signal, there and then

effects.log: {b3_rival} teaches it in four lines, and you flash it together, and the convoy comes in on two lamps instead of one.

choices.text: Send a runner for the pilot-guild and keep watch

effects.log: You send the runner and keep watch at the rail, and the guild lights the lamp with an hour to spare.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, {b3_rival} sends you a scroll in an old, shaking hand: a list of everything they once wished to say to you, with the dates. It ends mid-sentence. For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Finish the last sentence for them, in your own hand

ok.log: You finish the sentence and send it back unsigned, and a week later a reply arrives, one line, in the same shaking hand.

fail.log: You finish the sentence badly, and {b3_rival} never answers.

choices.text: Answer each date with a line of your own

effects.log: You answer every date in turn, over a month, and the scroll goes back twice as long as it came.

choices.text: Roll up the scroll and keep it unanswered

effects.log: You roll it up and put it on the shelf where the old letters go, and it waits for a better day.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, the Jade Void's swordsmith, who made yours, is now making a sword for {b3_rival}. The sword on the rack looks very like yours. Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Visit the smithy and ask the smith to put a flaw in no blade

effects.log: The smith is affronted and promises that every blade is flawless, which is exactly what you hoped to hear.

choices.text: Commission a second sword in a form {b3_rival} would never choose

ok.log: The smith produces a curved blade of dark steel, wholly unlike, and the Jade Void Court looks at both and prefers yours.

fail.log: The smith makes the sword, and it is the same as R's after all.

choices.text: Keep the old sword, and let theirs look like a copy

effects.log: You keep your old sword at your hip and the Court, comparing, thinks {b3_rival}'s a pale imitation.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, a portrait of you is hung in the Star Sea Pavilion. {b3_rival} arrives the same hour to have theirs hung beside it, a little higher. It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Have your own portrait rehung a hand higher

effects.log: You have the portrait lifted a hand, and the next week {b3_rival} raises theirs, and the Pavilion warden quietly buys a longer ladder.

choices.text: Hang a mirror between the two portraits

ok.log: The mirror hangs between you, and every visitor sees themselves between the two faces, and the Pavilion talks of nothing else.

fail.log: The mirror is taken down by the warden, with a reproving look.

choices.text: Leave the portraits as they are and go for a walk

effects.log: You leave them as they are, and walk the isle's edge until your mood clears.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {b3_rival} arrives wearing the grey of a duellist, the Court's old colour, and a look that says it has been waiting for this since the last century. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Accept the old courtesy and meet {b3_rival} on the plain at dawn

ok.log: You meet them at dawn in the old grey, and the duel settles nothing and matters entirely, and you stand when it is done.

fail.log: You meet them at dawn in the old grey, and fall short, and the grey is soaked with dew.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} what they have waited since the last century to say

effects.log: {b3_rival} says it, at some length, and it is not an insult but a grievance, and you listen to all of it.

choices.text: Wear grey yourself and refuse to draw

effects.log: You wear grey, stand at the foot of the stair, and refuse to draw, and the Court does not know what to make of it.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, {b3_rival} has trained a parrot of the cloud-sea to say your title, slowly, with a pause in the middle. It is being passed around the Court as a curiosity. There is no good reply, only several bad ones.

choices.text: Teach the parrot a title for {b3_rival}

ok.log: The parrot learns it in a week and says it with the same pause in the middle, and the Court passes it around for a month.

fail.log: The parrot refuses your title and keeps its first lesson, to the Court's delight.

choices.text: Buy the parrot and give it a quiet home

effects.log: You pay a fair price and keep the bird in your orchard, where it says your title only in the evenings, to the plum trees.

choices.text: Float a lantern for it with the others

effects.log: The lantern goes over the edge with the others, and the parrot, perched on the rail, says your title once more, to the dark.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, Your cloud-whale, sick for a month, is found in the hold of {b3_rival}'s ship, eating what the vet-immortal of the Nine Clouds Palace called a medicine. It is the most irritating kindness of your life.

choices.text: Visit your whale in the hold, and bring it a blanket

effects.log: You sit beside the great beast in the hold, and the whale, which is better, leans against your shoulder, and {b3_rival} pretends to be looking at maps.

choices.text: Ask the vet-immortal for the medicine's recipe

ok.log: The recipe is ridiculous and brilliant, and you improve it, and the Palace takes it up.

fail.log: The recipe has an ingredient you cannot name and the vet-immortal will not say.

choices.text: Take the whale home, and grumble the whole way

effects.log: You grumble from dock to gate, and the whale is deeply happy, and so are you.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {b3_rival} challenges you to a contest of memory: the order of the first thousand stairs, backwards, in front of an audience of tired scholars. The whole stair has taken sides.

choices.text: Recite the stairs backwards at speed

ok.log: You recite all thousand, cleanly, down to the first, and the scholars wake up to cheer.

fail.log: You lose the count at the six hundred and twelfth, which was always the one with the crack.

choices.text: Propose that both of you recite the forward order together

effects.log: You recite forwards in unison and the audience, expecting a duel, receives a hymn.

choices.text: Take your seat among the tired scholars and listen

effects.log: You sit in the second row and listen to {b3_rival} recite, and find, to your annoyance, that you could not have done better.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, {b3_rival} is awarded a jade seal for the pacification of an eastern isle. You were there. So was a great deal of your work, and a Demon Realm general who will say nothing. The ink is dry, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Ask the Demon Realm general, privately, to confirm who was there

effects.log: The general, who says nothing, sends a single black feather, and you keep it, and that is a kind of testimony.

choices.text: Raise it at the seal-giving, in the full Court

ok.log: You raise it with courtesy and a list, and the Court, embarrassed, adds a smaller seal for your share.

fail.log: You raise it at the wrong moment, and the Court takes it for envy.

choices.text: Keep the work, and give the honour its due

effects.log: You applaud {b3_rival} at the seal-giving, loudly, and the Court notes, with unease, how little you needed the jade.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a Demon Realm raiding party is sighted at the lower docks, only a handful, and the guard-captain asks whether you and {b3_rival} would "take a look". The old quarrel will have to wait its turn.

choices.text: Go down to the docks with {b3_rival} and meet the raiders as a pair

ok.log: The handful of raiders see two immortals stepping off the stair in step, and think better of it, and their boat is gone by the hour.

fail.log: The raiders are fewer but fiercer than the captain said, and you both come back cut and short of breath.

choices.text: Ask the raiders their business first, in their own tongue

effects.log: The raiders turn out to be lost, and hungry, and you and {b3_rival} send them home with rice and a map.

choices.text: Tell the captain to take a look himself

effects.log: The captain looks, and the raiders leave, and the old quarrel keeps its place.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, you and {b3_rival} are both hiding in the same disused tower from the same dreadful reception. Neither of you says why you are there, and neither leaves. The cloud-sea goes on being very large.

choices.text: Offer them the second chair and the window

effects.log: You give them the window, take the draught, and the two of you watch the reception below through a crack in the shutters.

choices.text: Admit what you are hiding from

ok.log: You name the dreadful reception and the dreadful host, and {b3_rival} adds a third dreadful guest, and you laugh until the lamp flickers.

fail.log: You name the reception and {b3_rival} goes stiff, because it is their cousin's.

choices.text: Stay quiet until the music stops and leave first

effects.log: You wait for the last drum to fade and slip out, leaving {b3_rival} the tower.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, a promising young array master turns down your offer, politely, and then accepts one from {b3_rival}, impolitely, in the same afternoon, in your hearing. Loyalty at this altitude is a seasonal crop.

choices.text: Make the young master a counter-offer on the spot

ok.log: The counter-offer comes with a library key and a free hand, and the young master takes yours after all, red in the face.

fail.log: The counter-offer comes a minute too late, and the young master has already shaken hands.

choices.text: Congratulate the young master and ask for one lecture a year

effects.log: You congratulate them and ask for the lecture, and they give it, and it is excellent, and the lecture hall fills.

choices.text: Withdraw the offer and keep your temper

effects.log: You withdraw gracefully, in the hearing of the others, and the library, which is mostly library, remembers.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, you are passed over for a Ministry post that you did not want, and {b3_rival} sends a note of condolence that is a little too sincere. The scales tip, as scales do.

choices.text: Reply with a gift of thanks for the sincere condolence

effects.log: You send a bag of your best tea, so sincerely that {b3_rival} cannot tell whether it is a barb.

choices.text: Visit {b3_rival} and talk about what the post would have cost you

ok.log: You describe the post and what it would have taken, and {b3_rival} hears it in silence and says, quietly, that they wanted it too.

fail.log: You describe the post and {b3_rival} hears a boast, and the visit ends.

choices.text: Go home and do the work you meant to do

effects.log: You go home to the work you had put off, and it is better than a post.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, a new array has been laid across the practice isle, and {b3_rival} says it will only work if two skilled immortals test it by attacking each other. They look at you. Both of you know the rules and neither is following them.

choices.text: Test the array against {b3_rival}, with limits agreed beforehand

ok.log: The array hums as you trade measured blows, and it works, and the practice isle shines, and neither of you is hurt.

fail.log: The array overloads at the third blow, and you are both thrown clear.

choices.text: Inspect the array first and say what is wrong with it

effects.log: You find a flaw in the third line of the array, and {b3_rival} admits they had spotted it too and wanted to see if you would.

choices.text: Send a disciple of each of you to test it instead

effects.log: The disciples test it, and break it, and the array is redrawn, and nobody has to fight.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, {b3_rival} returns your borrowed book with every page you dog-eared smoothed flat and a slip tucked in: "In case you meant to read it." The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Dog-ear the same pages again, and send it back

effects.log: You crease every page you smoothed and send the book back with a slip: "In case you meant to remember." {b3_rival} never answers, and keeps it.

choices.text: Return the slip, annotated with a long argument

ok.log: Your argument runs three pages and is correct, and {b3_rival}, unable to answer before the Court sits, sends only a flat jade seal of respect.

fail.log: Your argument runs three pages and has a hole in the second, which {b3_rival} finds before the bell.

choices.text: Read the book properly this time

effects.log: You read the whole book before the bell and are annoyed to find it is good.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {b3_rival} has quietly trained your lost courier's apprentice for a year, and returns the lad at your gate with a letter that says only "he can read, now". Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Give the lad a post in your own mail-house

effects.log: You hire him on the spot, and he reads your first letter aloud with such pride that the mail-house forgives everything.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a letter, in his hand, saying thank you

ok.log: The lad writes it himself, in a fine round script, and {b3_rival} keeps it flat in a book for good.

fail.log: The lad's hand shakes and the ink blots, and the letter reads like an apology.

choices.text: Ask the lad what {b3_rival} taught him first

effects.log: The lad says "to wait before saying no", and you carry the sentence round for years.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, There are two boys of promise at the Nine Clouds exam. {b3_rival} has taken a liking to one, you to the other, and the two have become best friends, to your mutual disgust. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Take both boys to supper with {b3_rival}

effects.log: The boys eat, and talk, and by the third course everyone is too busy being proud to quarrel.

choices.text: Argue your boy's case before the examiners

ok.log: Your boy is placed, narrowly, above the other, and the other boy thanks you anyway.

fail.log: Your boy is placed second, and your argument is remembered as a mistake of style.

choices.text: Stand back and let the boys find their own level

effects.log: You stand back, and the boys, who are friends, write each other's essays, and both pass.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, a book on cloud-beasts, newly bound, thanks every immortal on the shore except you, who gave it its chapter on migration. It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Write to the author with the migration data attached

effects.log: The author answers in three days, mortified, and the second printing has your name on the chapter.

choices.text: Review the book in the Court gazette, kindly and precisely

ok.log: Your review praises every page but one, and the gazette prints it, and readers find the one.

fail.log: Your review contains an error about the second migration, and the gazette prints that, too.

choices.text: Go out to the migration yourself, and watch

effects.log: You go to the high edge in autumn and watch the cloud-beasts go over for a week, unthanked and content.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, a bridge of rope and jade swings under both your weights, three hundred stairs above nothing, and the only way across is to hold it for each other. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Anchor your end and call out the steps to {b3_rival}

effects.log: You count the steps aloud, and {b3_rival} crosses on your voice alone, and then holds the rope for you in turn.

choices.text: Cross together, keeping the rope taut between you

ok.log: The bridge swings, but the weights balance, and you land on the far stair with the jade still humming.

fail.log: The bridge swings badly, and you both end up hanging on until the wardens come.

choices.text: Wait it out where you stand and breathe

effects.log: You wait, and the swing settles with the wind, and you say nothing for a long time.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, {b3_rival} comes to your gate with a bag of seeds from their mother's garden on an isle that no longer exists, and asks if you have somewhere they might grow. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Plant the seeds in the best bed of your orchard, and say so

effects.log: You plant them in the warmest bed, under the plum tree, and mark the bed with a small flat stone.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} what the plants are called, and learn the song to plant them by

ok.log: {b3_rival} sings the planting song, thin and sweet, and the seeds are in before dusk.

fail.log: {b3_rival} cannot remember the second verse, and the seeds go in quietly.

choices.text: Take the bag, and promise nothing aloud

effects.log: You take the bag and promise nothing, and in the spring something small and green comes up.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, the old gatekeeper of the Nine Clouds Palace, who knew the day-names of all your disciples, has retired. {b3_rival} gave the farewell dinner and the carpet. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Send the old gatekeeper a gift of your own, a day early

effects.log: You send a cask of plum wine and your oldest compliment, a day before the dinner, so that it is read first.

choices.text: Invite the gatekeeper to tea at your isle, as an honoured guest

ok.log: The gatekeeper comes and sits in your best chair and tells stories about every disciple, and goes home delighted.

fail.log: The gatekeeper declines, kindly, citing the dinner.

choices.text: Learn the day-names yourself, from the gatekeeper's book

effects.log: You copy the gatekeeper's book, and learn the day-names of all of your disciples as they once did.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {b3_rival} collapses on the stair of an overwork of the spirit, and is carried home by their disciples. You are offered the position they were due to take. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Decline the post and send your best physician to {b3_rival}

effects.log: You decline the post in writing and send your physician with a basket, and the Court draws its own conclusions about both of you.

choices.text: Take the post, and keep it warm for {b3_rival}

ok.log: You take the post and keep a chair empty beside it, and when {b3_rival} recovers they find the chair waiting.

fail.log: You take the post and the Court calls you a vulture, and {b3_rival}'s disciples do not forgive it.

choices.text: Wait at {b3_rival}'s bedside and say nothing about the post

effects.log: You wait through the night at the bedside, and the post waits too, and neither of you speaks of it.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, the Nine Clouds Palace's seer prophesies that the next duel of the century will be between two familiar names, and the next morning {b3_rival} comes to see if the prophecy is accurate. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to tell you the prophecy, and offer yours in exchange

effects.log: You swap prophecies over tea and discover they are the same, and agree to prove it wrong together.

choices.text: Fight {b3_rival} in the morning to see if the seer was right

ok.log: You fight them in the morning and the prophecy comes true, in your favour, in front of the seer, who looks smug.

fail.log: You fight them in the morning and the prophecy comes true, in theirs, and the seer looks smug.

choices.text: Visit a different seer and ask for a second opinion

effects.log: You visit a different seer, who says the opposite, and you leave with the pleasant sense that nobody knows.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, the Ministry of Rites seats you beside the door. {b3_rival}, seated by the dais, sends down a cushion, with a note regretting the draught. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Accept the cushion and sit on it with great ceremony

effects.log: You sit on the cushion in full view of the dais, and the draught, with the Ministry's whole table watching, becomes a minor incident of etiquette.

choices.text: Send the cushion back with a note regretting the altitude

ok.log: Your note is two lines, correct in form, and the dais passes it from hand to hand.

fail.log: Your note is witty and slightly too long, and the dais reads it as grumbling.

choices.text: Move your own seat to the draught, and say nothing

effects.log: You move your seat nearer the door and the fresher air, and sit through the whole rite with a clear head and a sore neck.

events.text: In the Jade Void's sword hall, {b3_rival} gives up the stronger place in a drill to cover a weakness of yours that nobody else has noticed. It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Return the favour at the next drill, quietly

effects.log: At the next drill you take the weak flank on {b3_rival}'s side and say nothing, and {b3_rival} fights much better there than anyone expected.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} after the drill how they saw the weakness

ok.log: They show you how to read a stance from the shoulder, and your guard improves by the next season.

fail.log: They shrug and say it was obvious, and you leave a little more sure you are being watched.

choices.text: Train the weakness out, on your own, until dawn

effects.log: You drill the flaw out in the empty sword hall by lamplight, and in a month it is gone.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, the Jade Void's annual sword-tree trimming is judged, this century, by a mute old man who has never been wrong. {b3_rival} is pruning beside you, in silence. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Trim your tree to a perfect cone before the old man looks

ok.log: Your cuts come clean, one by one, and the mute old man, for the first time in years, nods.

fail.log: Your last cut slips and the tree stands crooked, and the old man looks at it, and at you, and away.

choices.text: Prune slowly and listen to {b3_rival}'s shears

effects.log: You prune to {b3_rival}'s rhythm and the two trees come out matching, which the old man, mute, takes in with a long look.

choices.text: Hang your shears up and watch the old man work

effects.log: You put the shears down and watch, and the old man works as if no one were there, and you learn more than a century of lectures gave.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, the Nine Clouds Palace unveils a new elixir under {b3_rival}'s name. It is your formula, with a drop of lavender, and the lavender is being called the breakthrough. Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Brew your original elixir in public and let them taste both

effects.log: You brew yours at the Palace gate, and the crowd tastes both and the lavender is said to be a pleasant garnish.

choices.text: Ask the alchemists' guild to examine the formula

ok.log: The guild examines the notes, finds your hand throughout, and rules the lavender a garnish.

fail.log: The guild examines your notes, loses one page, and rules the matter unclear.

choices.text: Plant lavender yourself and brew a new elixir

effects.log: You plant lavender at the edge of the herb garden, and in five years it is yours, and entirely different.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, the great bell of the Court cracks in the middle of a ceremony, and {b3_rival} reaches the rope a moment before you do, and both haul, and the sound is terrible. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Haul the rope again and stop the crack running

ok.log: You and {b3_rival} haul in step until the note smooths, and the bell survives with a flaw only a scholar would hear.

fail.log: The haul only widens the crack, and the sound is terrible for a long time.

choices.text: Let go together and ask the Court to forgive the noise

effects.log: You both let go, and the bell hums down, and the Court, astonished, hears an apology from two directions.

choices.text: Stay quiet through the ceremony and ring a small hand-bell after

effects.log: You ring a hand-bell instead for the rest of the rite, and the Court calls it the better sound.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, an evening rain on the Jade Void's roof tiles holds you and {b3_rival} for a long hour in a gatehouse, and {b3_rival} sings, off-key, a lullaby from an earlier age. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Hum the second line of the lullaby with them

effects.log: You hum the second line, a note lower, and the rain on the tiles keeps time, and {b3_rival} does not stop.

choices.text: Ask where they learned it

ok.log: {b3_rival} says it was sung to them on a barge, by a boatman now long gone, and speaks of him for an hour.

fail.log: {b3_rival} goes quiet and the song ends.

choices.text: Listen to the rain and the song, and leave when it stops

effects.log: You listen until the rain eases, and then walk out under the dripping eaves, unsure why you are lighter.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, {b3_rival} has offered the Demon Realm's liaison a better seat, a better wine and, as you hear it, a better joke, and the liaison has laughed. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Tell a better joke to the liaison, in the Demon Realm accent

ok.log: Your joke is about a Demon Realm general and a goose, and the liaison laughs until she must be fanned.

fail.log: Your joke needs a footnote, and the liaison apologises for not getting it.

choices.text: Seat the liaison at your own table next time, and ask her about her family

effects.log: You ask about her children and her garden, and she answers at length, and a friendship that no joke could buy begins.

choices.text: Pour the wine and let {b3_rival} have the evening

effects.log: You pour for the liaison, and let {b3_rival} have the evening, and keep the next one for yourself.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, a new Marshal of the Celestial Ministries is appointed, and it is neither you nor {b3_rival}, but a former disciple of both, who is mortified by the whole thing. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Send the new Marshal a gift from both of you

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} choose it together, and it is a plain sword-belt, and the Marshal, mortified, wears it for a century.

choices.text: Take the new Marshal aside and offer advice, before {b3_rival} does

ok.log: You offer a plain piece of advice about the Ministries, and the Marshal is grateful, and {b3_rival}'s advice comes later.

fail.log: The Marshal takes your advice as a rebuke, and bows to {b3_rival} for theirs.

choices.text: Applaud and go home

effects.log: You applaud with the others and go home, and are, to your own surprise, glad.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, It is the night of the lantern-fall, and {b3_rival} has chosen the narrow bridge between the two highest isles, to see what happens when neither can step back. The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Walk forward until the two of you meet in the middle

ok.log: You meet in the middle, shoulder to shoulder, and the bridge sways, and it is {b3_rival} who gives a half-step.

fail.log: You meet in the middle and the bridge sways, and it is you who gives the half-step.

choices.text: Sit down on the bridge, where you stand, and offer {b3_rival} tea

effects.log: You sit down on the bridge with a flask, and {b3_rival}, thwarted, sits too, and the lantern-fall goes on around you.

choices.text: Step back with a bow and let them have the bridge

effects.log: You step back with a deep bow and let them pass, and from the island's edge you watch them cross, alone, under the lanterns.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, a lantern-maker on the lower stair says a "very senior immortal" ordered one hundred lanterns shaped like your face. {b3_rival}'s steward collected them. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Have the lanterns hung in the Rites hall

effects.log: You have all hundred hung in the Ministry of Rites, glowing, and the ministers are made to bow to your face for a month.

choices.text: Pay {b3_rival}'s steward a visit to count the lanterns

ok.log: The count comes out to ninety-nine, and the steward pays you the price of one, and the story spreads in your favour.

fail.log: The count is a hundred and one, and you leave with the bill.

choices.text: Light one, for the lantern-maker

effects.log: You light one on the lower stair for the lantern-maker, and it burns until morning, and it is very ugly.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, a rumour that you took a bribe goes round the Ministries, and {b3_rival} produces the true ledger, which is a great deal duller, and kills the rumour. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival} in front of the Ministry that carried the rumour

effects.log: You thank them where the rumour was loudest, and the Ministry has to hear it twice.

choices.text: Carry the dull ledger to every clerk who whispered

ok.log: The ledger is so dull that everyone agrees you could never have hidden anything in it.

fail.log: The ledger is so dull that nobody reads it, and the whispers go on a while.

choices.text: Burn the old rumour with the old tea leaves

effects.log: You throw the leaves in the brazier and the rumour with them, and it never comes back.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, the Court is appointing a Keeper of the Autumn Tide. You and {b3_rival} have been asked to hold a public debate on the nature of tides, which neither of you has studied. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Debate from the library of the Star Sea, quoting what you read overnight

ok.log: You have three nights of reading in your arguments and the Court, which has never studied tides either, is convinced.

fail.log: You quote a tide-chart upside down, and {b3_rival} finds it.

choices.text: Admit at once that neither of you knows, and ask for the tide-keeper

effects.log: You ask for the oldest tide-keeper on the isle, who speaks for an hour, and the Court appoints the keeper, with thanks to you both.

choices.text: Bring an umbrella and let {b3_rival} argue the case

effects.log: You open the umbrella and sit, and {b3_rival} argues for the full hour while you note down the best points for your next debate.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, a Jade Court painter shows a canvas of the Great Rescue: there is an immortal in the foreground who is shaped like {b3_rival} and holds a rope you tied. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Commission a second canvas, showing the rope-tying

effects.log: You commission a second canvas, a quiet one, and it hangs in the same gallery, rope and all.

choices.text: Send the painter the knot, tied correctly

ok.log: The painter reads the knot and repaints the rope, and the Court, which loves knots, whispers about you.

fail.log: The painter cannot read the knot and paints a smaller rope, also yours.

choices.text: Look at the rope in the picture a long time

effects.log: You look at the rope for a long time, and it is, you decide, quite a good rope.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, a child-immortal on a school outing wanders off the edge of the isle chasing a lantern. {b3_rival} goes after the lantern. You go after {b3_rival}. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Dive after the child with a cloud-rope round your waist

ok.log: You catch the hem of the child's robe, {b3_rival} catches your rope, and the three of you come up on the isle, wet and astonished.

fail.log: You miss the child by a hand, and {b3_rival} gets there first, and you end up hanging on with a bruised shoulder.

choices.text: Throw {b3_rival} your sash and anchor it on the rail

effects.log: The sash reaches, and {b3_rival} comes up with the child and the lantern, and the lantern is still lit.

choices.text: Call the isle-wardens and watch the edge

effects.log: You shout, the wardens come with their nets, and the child is hauled up, giggling, with the lantern.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, {b3_rival} asks you to stand witness to a small matter of their own: they have written a will, and want a second signature from someone they do not like. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Read the will carefully before you sign it

effects.log: You read it twice, find it fair and plain, and sign in a steady hand, and {b3_rival} is visibly relieved to be read.

choices.text: Ask what they want to leave to you, and to whom

ok.log: {b3_rival} names three heirs and a debt, and the debt is to you, and you decide to forgive it later.

fail.log: {b3_rival} declines to say, and the will is signed in tense silence.

choices.text: Sign it, and stay for the tea

effects.log: You sign and stay for the tea, which is the worst tea of the century, and you drink it all.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, Three of your finest pupils have been invited to a "reading group" on {b3_rival}'s isle. The reading group has, so far, read only one book, and it is the one you wrote. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Go to the reading group and take a seat at the back

effects.log: You sit at the back and hear your own book read aloud badly and are, to your surprise, delighted.

choices.text: Ask your pupils to read something harder than your book

ok.log: You set them a text you have not read yourself, and they return changed, with an argument for you.

fail.log: You set a text so hard that they come back confused and it goes sour.

choices.text: Let the pupils read, and be pleased that they read at all

effects.log: You let them read, because a pupil who reads will come back, and in time most do.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, the Court proposes to add a hall to the White Library, to be named for one of you. Each of you is told, privately, that it will be the other. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Propose that the hall be named for the pair of you

effects.log: You propose it in the Court, to a silence, and the hall is named for neither, but for a window, and both of you are content.

choices.text: Ask the Court which of you it is, and see who flinches

ok.log: The Court says "the elder", and {b3_rival} flinches, and you learn how old each of you is in the Court's eyes.

fail.log: The Court says "the more deserving", and neither of you flinches enough.

choices.text: Tell the Court to name it for the librarian

effects.log: You suggest the oldest librarian, and the Court, caught off guard, agrees, and the librarian cries.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, {b3_rival} sends a letter containing a single character, "now", and a place, and a time that is a quarter-hour away. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Go to the place in the quarter-hour, and fight in the time left

ok.log: You arrive with a breath to spare, and the fight is quick and clean, and ends with a nod.

fail.log: You arrive late and winded, and {b3_rival} is waiting, and the fight is short.

choices.text: Send back a single character of your own, "later", and a better place

effects.log: You send back "later" and a quieter place, and {b3_rival} sends one back: "agreed", and it is the politest challenge of the century.

choices.text: Go to the place early, and wait with a flask

effects.log: You go early and wait with a flask, and {b3_rival} arrives to find you drinking tea, and the quarrel changes shape.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, {b3_rival} mentions to the Court historian, in your hearing, that your isle "has a great deal of potential", the way one remarks on a damp cellar. You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Agree that the isle has potential, and name a date

effects.log: You tell the historian the exact day the potential will be visible, and the historian writes it down, and so does {b3_rival}.

choices.text: Ask the historian to record what a damp cellar grows

ok.log: The historian records that damp cellars grow the best ginseng, mushrooms and wine, and {b3_rival} goes quiet.

fail.log: The historian records that damp cellars grow mould, in a footnote you cannot unread.

choices.text: Pour the tea and say nothing for the rest of the ceremony

effects.log: You pour three more cups without a word, and the ceremony, which aged a sapling, ages you a little too.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, {b3_rival} sends a seer of the Star Sea to your gate with a warning of a storm at the isle's eastern edge. The seer has been paid in advance, and for the silence. You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Reinforce the eastern edge the same night

effects.log: You rouse the whole isle, lash down the eastern pavilions with sky-rope, and the storm takes a gazebo and nothing else.

choices.text: Pay the seer for the silence too, and ask who sent them

ok.log: The seer, paid twice, names the sender with a straight face, and you thank {b3_rival} by sending a better-paid seer back.

fail.log: The seer keeps the silence and the secret, and goes home richer.

choices.text: Move your guests to the western halls and say nothing

effects.log: You move the guests west before the storm, and {b3_rival} never learns whether the warning was read.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {b3_rival} dares you: the loser must carry the winner's tea tray for a decade. You note that you had not accepted. You note also that you are already winning. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Win it in a single stroke, and decline the tray

ok.log: You win at the first exchange and then refuse the tray with a shrug, which annoys {b3_rival} more than losing.

fail.log: You lose at the first exchange and are handed a tea tray, and a ten-year schedule.

choices.text: Point out you never accepted, and offer to carry it together

effects.log: You carry the tray between you, up the white stairs, and the Court, watching, decides it was always a joke.

choices.text: Let the dare lapse, and note the date

effects.log: You let it lapse, and note the date, because you are, after all, already winning.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, {b3_rival} sits in the lecture hall and nods while a young student says that the third law of the stairs was {b3_rival}'s discovery. It was a footnote of yours. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Stand up in the lecture hall and cite your footnote

ok.log: You cite the footnote, page and line, and the lecturer, flustered, corrects the board while {b3_rival} studies the ceiling.

fail.log: You cite the wrong page, and the lecturer politely corrects you.

choices.text: Take the student aside afterwards and show the original notes

effects.log: You show the notes over tea, and the student leaves with a better law, and your name on it.

choices.text: Let the student have his law, and keep teaching him

effects.log: You teach him the fourth law, which is better, and he will cite you when he is old.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, the Star Sea Pavilion's great lens has been stolen, mid-eclipse, and the thief ran toward the one gate both of you know the way to. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Run to the old gate that only you and {b3_rival} know

ok.log: The thief runs straight into your arms, and into {b3_rival}'s, and the lens is saved from the eclipse and from his pockets.

fail.log: The thief turns the other way, and the lens is lost for the night.

choices.text: Follow the thief with {b3_rival}, splitting at each fork

effects.log: You split at each fork and meet at the end, where the thief, outnumbered, hands over the lens with a bow.

choices.text: Raise the alarm and wait at the Pavilion

effects.log: You raise the alarm and wait, and the wardens bring the lens back before the eclipse is over.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, you find that {b3_rival} has been paying the keeper of the stair a stipend to leave your lamp lit at night for three hundred years. They are very embarrassed. For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Pay the keeper the stipend yourself from now on, and tell {b3_rival}

effects.log: You pay it for a year, then tell {b3_rival}, who cannot meet your eye, and the lamp burns on, paid by the pair of you.

choices.text: Ask the keeper what {b3_rival} said when they paid

ok.log: The keeper reports each word, scrupulously, including the dull ones, and you carry them home like stones.

fail.log: The keeper will not discuss clients, and the stair keeps its secret.

choices.text: Let the lamp burn and thank no one

effects.log: You walk home by the lamp, in the dark, and leave it lit.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, a famous painter you have been courting for a decade turns up at {b3_rival}'s house to paint a screen. The screen is a picture of your isle, seen from across. Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Sit for the painter yourself, on your own bridge

effects.log: You sit on the bridge, and the painter paints you into the screen, and the screen is in {b3_rival}'s house with you in it.

choices.text: Ask the painter what made them accept {b3_rival}'s offer

ok.log: The painter says it was the quiet, and the paint, and you take both into account, and offer a quiet studio.

fail.log: The painter says nothing, politely, and the screen goes on.

choices.text: Hang a plain brush on the wall and keep your own counsel

effects.log: You hang a brush by your door, in case, and keep your own counsel, and some year the painter comes by.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, you receive a gift from the Demon Realm: a rare jade, with a note praising your ascent. {b3_rival} receives the same, with the same note, an hour later. It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Return the jade to the Demon Realm with a polite note

effects.log: You return the jade with a note praising the carving, and the Demon Realm, nonplussed, sends something plainer.

choices.text: Compare notes with {b3_rival} and see what else they were sent

ok.log: You and {b3_rival} lay the notes side by side and find the same flattery, and the same minor error in the third line.

fail.log: You and {b3_rival} compare notes and find nothing, and stare at each other over the jade.

choices.text: Keep the jade and tell the Court at once

effects.log: You hand the jade to the Ministry of Rites, with the note, and the Court gives you a long, tired look of approval.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, a senior minister calls you and {b3_rival} before the Court and orders that the matter be "resolved by honourable means", and then, helpfully, lists them. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Pick the most tedious honourable means on the list: a debate

effects.log: You pick the debate, and it lasts three days, and the Court falls asleep, and {b3_rival} concedes in despair.

choices.text: Choose a contest of calligraphy and outwrite {b3_rival}

ok.log: Your hand is the steadier, and the minister, reading both, awards the margin to you and the grace to {b3_rival}.

fail.log: Your hand shakes on the last stroke, and {b3_rival} wins, humbly.

choices.text: Ask the minister which means he would choose, and do that

effects.log: The minister names a walk round the nine isles, together, and you do it, and by the ninth isle the matter is settled.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, Your name is mispronounced by the herald at the Court of Autumn, and {b3_rival}, three seats off, does not wince, which is how you know it was deliberate. There is no good reply, only several bad ones.

choices.text: Correct the herald from where you sit, softly and once

effects.log: You say it once, in the herald's own cadence, and the hall has to hear your name pronounced right and {b3_rival} sitting very still.

choices.text: Bow to the herald, and pronounce {b3_rival}'s name wrongly in thanks

ok.log: The hall catches it and laughs politely, and {b3_rival} hears a name that is almost theirs, for a century.

fail.log: The hall takes it for a real mistake and the herald apologises to {b3_rival} instead.

choices.text: Answer to the wrong name, and let the bell cover it

effects.log: The bell rings its one note of the century, and your wrong name goes up with it, and nobody remembers.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, a star falls into your orchard. {b3_rival} arrives with a ladder, a net, and ill grace, to help get it out before the Ministry of Omens notices. It is the most irritating kindness of your life.

choices.text: Hand {b3_rival} the end of the net and heave together

effects.log: You pull the star out between you, hot as a kettle, and for an hour you are two immortals with a ladder.

choices.text: Hide the star from the Ministry of Omens yourself

ok.log: The Ministry of Omens comes, sniffs, and goes, and the star is later seen in the sky of another isle.

fail.log: The Ministry arrives early and your orchard is declared a minor sign.

choices.text: Offer {b3_rival} an apple from the tree it fell beside

effects.log: You hand over an apple that is slightly toasted, and eat the other half yourself, on the ladder.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, a cloud-garden competition has produced two finalists, {b3_rival}'s and yours, whose entries are the same shape, because the same plan was stolen from the same drawer. The whole stair has taken sides.

choices.text: Ask the garden warden for the drawer's key and the log

effects.log: The log shows a night visitor in a grey robe, and the warden, who is mortified, awards both entries a ribbon of shame.

choices.text: Redesign yours overnight before the judging

ok.log: By dawn your garden has a new bridge, a stream and a hidden terrace, and the judges walk it twice.

fail.log: By dawn your garden is half rebuilt and entirely wrong.

choices.text: Enter both gardens under one name and share the prize

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} enter the pair jointly, and the stair, having taken sides, has no one to cheer against.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a rumour makes its way across three isles that the cure for the cloud-fever came from {b3_rival}'s kitchen. It came from yours, and was tasted by {b3_rival}. The ink is dry, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Send a bottle of the real cure to every isle that heard the rumour

effects.log: The bottles go out with your seal on the cork, and the rumour dies of its own weight.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to tell the true story at their own table

ok.log: {b3_rival} tells it, honestly, at table, and it spreads faster than the rumour did.

fail.log: {b3_rival} tells the story, and it comes out garbled, and the rumour wins.

choices.text: Keep cooking, and let the sick find the right kitchen

effects.log: You keep cooking, and the cure keeps working, and sick people from three isles find your door.

events.text: Late in a year the immortals had agreed to call quiet, a famine in the cloud-gardens has the lower stairs rioting politely, and the Ministry asks you and {b3_rival} to ration, which is not the same as share. The old quarrel will have to wait its turn.

choices.text: Open your own granary to the lower stairs, and ask {b3_rival} to do the same

effects.log: Both granaries open, and the queues form along the white stairs in good order, and the rationing is shared rather than imposed.

choices.text: Draw up the ration list with {b3_rival} before the Ministry does

ok.log: Your list is fair and brief, and the lower stairs stop riots, politely, and file in.

fail.log: Your list has an error in the second column, and the lower stairs find it.

choices.text: Tend the cloud-gardens and let the Ministry ration

effects.log: You spend the week on your knees in the gardens, coaxing late shoots, and eat what they give.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, {b3_rival} reads you, without comment, a poem written for someone you both knew, and when they have finished you realise they are weeping and are pretending not to. The cloud-sea goes on being very large.

choices.text: Wait until they have finished, and say nothing

effects.log: You wait, and when they stop, the library is very quiet, and you hand them your handkerchief.

choices.text: Say the next line of the poem, softly

ok.log: You say the next line, softly, from memory, and {b3_rival} looks up, and you finish the stanza together.

fail.log: You mis-remember the line, and {b3_rival} corrects you with a wet laugh.

choices.text: Pretend to be absorbed in a scroll

effects.log: You turn to the scroll, and let them have the privacy, and read the same line forty times.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, a vacancy for a teacher at the school of the Jade Court has been filled by a former friend of yours, and {b3_rival} held the horse at the interview. Loyalty at this altitude is a seasonal crop.

choices.text: Write to your friend, warmly, and say you are glad

effects.log: You write the letter in one draft, and mean most of it, and the friend writes back the same evening.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} what they wanted for the horse they held

ok.log: {b3_rival} answers wryly that they wanted nothing, and the interview was a fine one, and the friend deserved it.

fail.log: {b3_rival} answers that it was none of your business, and they are right.

choices.text: Take a teaching post of your own, a rung lower

effects.log: You take a lower post at the school, and the pupils, learning from you, do not notice the rung.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, {b3_rival} emerges from a retreat of sixty years with a sword that sings on the wind, and the isle clears of birds, and a hush goes round the Court. The scales tip, as scales do.

choices.text: Spar with {b3_rival} and the singing sword on the practice isle

ok.log: You spar with the singing sword and the whole isle listens, and you land one clean blow that makes the sword hum in a lower key.

fail.log: The sword out-sings you, and you retire with a ringing in your ears.

choices.text: Ask what the sword is called, and what it costs the birds

effects.log: You ask, and {b3_rival} says the sword has no name and the birds will come back, and the answer is better than expected.

choices.text: Stay in your study and let the hush pass

effects.log: You stay in your study and read, and the hush crosses the Court without finding you.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, the Star Sea, for a fee, will tell you which of you wins a duel on the plain of the lower isle. {b3_rival} has already bought the answer, and is not saying what it was. Both of you know the rules and neither is following them.

choices.text: Buy the same answer from the Star Sea, and read it together

effects.log: You buy the answer and read it with {b3_rival}, and it is a riddle about a bridge, and you both laugh and neither fights.

choices.text: Duel {b3_rival} anyway, to prove the answer false

ok.log: You fight and the answer proves wrong, as you intended, and the Star Sea refunds a fee in embarrassment.

fail.log: You fight and the answer proves right, as it did the whole time.

choices.text: Do not buy the answer and walk home by the long way

effects.log: You do not buy it, and walk home by the long way, and find you would rather not know.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, a guest at a tea gathering asks {b3_rival} what they think of your sword. "I have only seen it from far away," says {b3_rival}, who was in the room when you drew it. The clouds below look very soft.

choices.text: Draw the sword again, here, and let the guest see it

effects.log: You draw it fully in the tea room, and the guest sees it from a foot away, and {b3_rival} sees the guest see it.

choices.text: Remind {b3_rival} that they were in the room at the time

ok.log: You say so lightly, pouring tea, and the guest turns to look, and {b3_rival} reaches for their cup.

fail.log: You say it too lightly, and it sounds like a complaint, and {b3_rival} reaches for a kinder topic.

choices.text: Let the guest think what they like

effects.log: The guest thinks what guests think, and the clouds go on being the colour of old bone, and the sword stays in its sheath.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, you are denied entry at a high gate for lack of a patron, and {b3_rival} steps forward and says they are your patron, in front of the whole line. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival} at the gate, and ask them to stay as the patron

effects.log: You thank them in front of the line and the line cheers softly, and {b3_rival} wishes the gate would swallow them.

choices.text: Name {b3_rival} your patron in the Court record, in earnest

ok.log: The record shows it, and the Court takes you both for friends, which is a nuisance and a protection.

fail.log: The clerk reads it as irony, and no one has told {b3_rival} yet.

choices.text: Walk in without a word, and let the line close behind

effects.log: You pass through the high gate under {b3_rival}'s name and keep going, and your back burns for the length of the hall.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, the question of whose isle the rainbow touches in the first hour of the new year has been sent to the Star Sea, which will answer after the fact. The ministers are enjoying this a little.

choices.text: Send the Star Sea a gift for a kinder answer

effects.log: The Star Sea accepts the gift and answers in riddle, and each of you reads the riddle your own way for a century.

choices.text: Station yourself on the eastern ledge at the hour

ok.log: The rainbow touches your ledge first, by a hair, and the hair is the thing the Court remembers.

fail.log: The rainbow touches {b3_rival}'s isle, with you on the wrong ledge.

choices.text: Invite {b3_rival} to watch it from the shared bridge

effects.log: You watch from the bridge and the rainbow falls on the water between, and the Star Sea declares it a draw.

events.text: In a widely admired memoir, {b3_rival} describes a night on the western wall as one of "quiet teamwork", and you appear as "a figure in the dark". It is hard to be angry at an accurate lie.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a copy of the memoir with the night corrected in the margins

effects.log: Your corrections are mild and exact, and {b3_rival} sends it back with a single mark of agreement, which is worse than a quarrel.

choices.text: Write your own account of the western wall

ok.log: Your account is short and vivid, and the Court prefers it, and the two books are bound side by side.

fail.log: Your account is accurate and dull, and the Court prefers the memoir.

choices.text: Accept the figure in the dark, and let it be a good figure

effects.log: You decide to be the figure in the dark, and take up a night patrol on the wall, which is quiet.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, an unquiet ancestor of a great house wakes in a tomb under the stair, and the only two living immortals who can say the old greeting are the two of you. No one is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Speak the old greeting together, in the old accent

ok.log: The greeting rings in two voices, and the ancestor, who wanted only to be addressed, settles back into the dark.

fail.log: You say the greeting a century out of date, and the ancestor takes offence.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to speak the greeting while you hold the lamp

effects.log: You hold the lamp, and {b3_rival} speaks, and the old voice answers, and you cannot say afterwards which of you it listened to.

choices.text: Leave an offering at the tomb door and withdraw

effects.log: You leave rice and a candle at the door, and withdraw, and the tomb is quiet till spring.

events.text: In a corridor of the Ministry of Rites, {b3_rival} is trying to learn the guard's name for the fiftieth time and failing. It is oddly like looking at yourself. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

choices.text: Tell them the guard's name, and then the guard's mother's name

effects.log: You tell them both, and {b3_rival} writes them on their sleeve, and the guard, passing, is startled to be greeted by name.

choices.text: Offer them a trick for remembering names

ok.log: Your trick is to pin each name to a smell, and {b3_rival} tries it on the guard, who smells of pine resin and is greeted warmly ever after.

fail.log: Your trick is to link names to birds, and {b3_rival} greets the guard as Magpie.

choices.text: Look away and let them struggle

effects.log: You look away, but you are listening, and the name is in your head for good.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, {b3_rival} has found out where you buy your cloud-silk and bought the whole season's weave, leaving you with a robe of patched hemp for the Midwinter Court. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

choices.text: Dress in patched hemp and wear it with great pride

effects.log: You enter the Midwinter Court in patched hemp and carry it so proudly that the next season, hemp is the fashion.

choices.text: Find a spinner on a lower isle and commission silk by midwinter

ok.log: The lower-isle spinner has a bolt in the cellar, the very colour you wanted, and it is yours by dawn.

fail.log: The spinner has nothing but yarn, and you go in hemp.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a thank-you note for the free lesson in humility

effects.log: The note arrives on the festival morning, and {b3_rival} reads it twice, and wonders who has won.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, the Nine Clouds Palace names a new head of alchemists. It is a person you taught. {b3_rival} teaches them now, too, and they bow to both with equal fear. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

choices.text: Invite the head alchemist to a joint lesson with {b3_rival} and yourself

effects.log: You teach on one side and {b3_rival} on the other, and the head alchemist, between you, learns twice as fast and fears twice as much.

choices.text: Teach the head alchemist the one thing {b3_rival} cannot

ok.log: You teach the patient cold furnace, and the head alchemist bows to you for it, which {b3_rival} hears of that evening.

fail.log: You teach a trick {b3_rival} had already taught, and nothing comes of it.

choices.text: Send your congratulations and a book of recipes

effects.log: You send a book of recipes with your seal, and the head alchemist reads it by night.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, {b3_rival} kneels in a strange old courtesy of the Jade Void, a bow that means "I ask you for a lesson", and holds it, and holds it, and holds it. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Bow back as deeply, and hold it as long

effects.log: You bow as deeply and hold it, and the Jade Void stair-keepers lose count of the minutes, and the two of you stay bent till both backs complain.

choices.text: Take up the lesson and teach {b3_rival} a form of your own

ok.log: You teach one form you made yourself, and {b3_rival} learns it in an hour and bows again, without condition.

fail.log: You teach a form with a flaw, and {b3_rival} finds it, and bows with courtesy anyway.

choices.text: Raise {b3_rival} by the elbow and lead them in to tea

effects.log: You raise them by the elbow and walk them in, and the bow is over, and the lesson, it turns out, was the tea.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, {b3_rival} has sent your isle a map of the white stairs with your landing marked "Rest Stop". The map is beautifully drawn and has been hung in three halls. You admire it, as craft.

choices.text: Add a teahouse to the map, at your landing

effects.log: You have a teahouse built exactly at the mark, and "Rest Stop" becomes a name for the best stop on the stairs.
