choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a map of their own isle, corrected

ok.log: Your map is the better drawn, and shows {b3_rival}'s isle with all its stairs marked in a detail they had never noticed.

fail.log: Your map has one stair on the wrong side, and {b3_rival} hangs it in the fourth hall.

choices.text: Hang the map in your own hall, and be rested

effects.log: The map hangs in your hall and guests from other isles linger beneath it, and rest.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, {b3_rival} sits by your bed through the night of a bad illness, and leaves before the dawn, so that you can pretend you did not know. It changes nothing, and everything.

choices.text: Leave the shutters open at dawn and say "thank you" to the empty chair

effects.log: You say it to the empty chair, aloud, and tell no one, and your fever breaks that same week.

choices.text: Seek {b3_rival} out and ask how they knew you were ill

ok.log: They admit that your steward is a dreadful gossip, and the two of you laugh in a way you had forgotten.

fail.log: They go stiff and deny everything, and the thread you pulled snaps.

choices.text: Sleep, and let the pretence stand

effects.log: You sleep, and you are well by the next full moon, and the pretence stays as good as a debt unspoken.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, {b3_rival} announces that they will walk all nine hundred stairs on one leg, for a purse that the Ministry has not offered. The dare is that you will not. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Hop the nine hundred stairs on one leg, backward

ok.log: You hop, and the stair-keepers hold their breath, and you reach the top gasping, and the Ministry says nothing about the purse.

fail.log: You hop two hundred and fall, and the keepers give you tea.

choices.text: Offer to carry {b3_rival}'s purse of nothing up the stairs on two legs

effects.log: You carry the empty purse, in state, up the nine hundred stairs on two legs, and the Court is in stitches.

choices.text: Refuse, and ask the dare in writing

effects.log: You ask it in writing, and {b3_rival} has to compose a dare, and does so with such care that the Court posts it on the stair.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, a ministry clerk gets the names on a medal the wrong way round, and {b3_rival} takes the medal home and, to everyone's surprise, does not give it back. Posterity is a slow court.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to correct the record and let {b3_rival} keep the medal

effects.log: The clerk gapes. You explain that the name on the medal is the least of it, and the Court, hearing it, awards you a better one.

choices.text: Present {b3_rival} with a second medal reading "also"

ok.log: The second medal reads "also", and {b3_rival} wears both on the same sash all week, and the Court roars.

fail.log: The second medal is taken as a mockery, and the clerk takes both back.

choices.text: Wait for {b3_rival} to return it, and do not ask

effects.log: You wait three years, and one morning the medal is on your table, polished, with no note.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, the Jade Court's archive goes up in a bloom of cold white fire, and {b3_rival} is on one side of it, with the oldest annals, and you are on the other, with the door. Whatever happens, you both know it will not be spoken of.

choices.text: Throw the door open and shout the shelf-numbers across to {b3_rival}

effects.log: You shout the shelf-numbers across the fire, and {b3_rival} carries out the annals in order, and only the dust is lost.

choices.text: Run through the cold white fire for the oldest annals yourself

ok.log: The cold fire clings but does not burn, and you come out with the annals and a coat of white frost, and {b3_rival} pulls you clear.

fail.log: The cold fire is stronger than it looks, and you retreat with a handful of pages and frost-bitten hands.

choices.text: Hold the door and let {b3_rival} carry what they can

effects.log: You hold the door against the draught, and {b3_rival} carries out the annals, and you both watch the archive burn out.

events.text: In the gap between one century's grudges and the next, you and {b3_rival} are seated together at an old friend's wedding, and for an hour the grudge lies down in the corner and goes to sleep. You notice you are not angry.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the bride with {b3_rival}, and clink it

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} clink cups for the bride, and nobody at the table sees the grudge turn over in its sleep.

choices.text: Dance the first dance that the old friend asks of you both

ok.log: You dance badly together, in front of everyone, and the old friend weeps with laughter.

fail.log: You dance badly and step on {b3_rival}'s foot, and the grudge wakes with a yawn.

choices.text: Eat the wedding rice and leave the grudge asleep

effects.log: You eat the rice, and the music is soft, and the grudge dozes by the door until the guests go home.

events.text: Somewhere in a decade you have both stopped counting, the Ministry of Rites loses your petition, and {b3_rival}'s clerk finds it, and brings it back with a polite note and, by a happy accident, a seat on {b3_rival}'s committee. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Take the committee seat and vote against {b3_rival} on the first motion

effects.log: You take the seat, read the papers, and vote against {b3_rival} on the first motion, which they respect enormously.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival}'s clerk in person, and ask to see the filing system

ok.log: The clerk, flattered, shows you the whole filing system, and you learn which drawer every petition goes to for ten years.

fail.log: The clerk is polite and shows you a closed drawer.

choices.text: Resubmit the petition through the proper door and wait

effects.log: You resubmit it through the proper door, and wait, and it is returned, stamped, in a century or so.

events.text: On the bridge between two isles, with the sea of clouds slow below, a comet is named for {b3_rival}, and the Star Sea charges nothing for the privilege, and you are told, quite kindly, that it was a close choice. The ladder only goes one way, and everyone is on it.

choices.text: Observe the comet from your roof with {b3_rival}, as a guest

effects.log: You climb the roof together, and the comet crosses, and {b3_rival} is gracious for once, and quiet.

choices.text: Petition the Star Sea to name the next star-fall for you

ok.log: The Star Sea, after a fee and a fair wind, agrees, and in a century a star falls with your name on it.

fail.log: The Star Sea declines, politely, and keeps the fee.

choices.text: Congratulate {b3_rival} and note that comets do not stay

effects.log: You congratulate them and note that comets come back once in a lifetime, which is about the right frequency for fame.

events.text: On a ledge of white jade overlooking the cloud-sea, {b3_rival} unsheathes a plain sword, remarks that it is borrowed, and asks whether you would mind. The crowd is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Ask them whose sword it is, and draw yours anyway

ok.log: It is the old marshal's, you learn after, and you win, narrowly, without ever breaking the marshal's blade.

fail.log: You cross blades and the marshal's sword rings, and you lose by a hair.

choices.text: Say you do mind, a little, and ask for a longer ledge

effects.log: You ask for a wider ledge, and {b3_rival} laughs, and the duel moves to a plain field, and loses its edge.

choices.text: Sheathe your sword and ask to hold the borrowed one

effects.log: You hold the borrowed sword, and feel its weight, and learn from it more than from the duel.

events.text: In the library of an isle that is mostly library, the Court sets a riddle of seven lines, and {b3_rival} solves it, then asks you very gently whether you would like the answer explained. Everyone is looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Explain the answer to {b3_rival} before they finish asking

ok.log: You give the answer, and the proof, and a better answer to the second riddle hidden in the first, and the library, which is mostly library, looks up.

fail.log: You give the answer and miss the second riddle, which {b3_rival} explains, gently.

choices.text: Say yes, you would like it explained, and take notes

effects.log: You take notes, in full, and {b3_rival}'s explanation is so fine that you quote it for a century, and always with credit.

choices.text: Turn the page to the next riddle

effects.log: You turn the page and solve the next one, in front of the rest, quietly.

events.text: In the long afternoon of a festival you both pretended not to attend, a path to your isle has been blocked by a landslip of jade. {b3_rival}'s labourers arrived a day earlier than yours, with picks, and a bill addressed to nobody. You will have to do something about this.

choices.text: Send your labourers to the next block, and share the bill

effects.log: You split the work at the next block, and the bill addressed to nobody is split too, which makes it a bill addressed to both.

choices.text: Present {b3_rival} with the unsigned bill, framed

ok.log: The framed bill hangs in {b3_rival}'s hall by the next festival, and the Court laughs, kindly, for a decade.

fail.log: The framed bill reads as a taunt, and the Court takes {b3_rival}'s side of it.

choices.text: Walk the cleared path to your gate and say nothing

effects.log: You walk the cleared path and the jade grit crunches under your boots, and you do not look back to see who is watching.

events.text: While the stair-keepers were changing shifts, an immortal from a faraway isle must pick a successor, and has invited you and {b3_rival} to cook for them, one dish each, and the dishes must not be the same. You can hear them thinking it through.

choices.text: Cook the dish of the elder's home isle, from memory

ok.log: The dish is, by chance, the very one the elder's mother made, and the elder puts down the spoon and says nothing for a while.

fail.log: The dish is too sweet by half, and the elder takes a second helping of {b3_rival}'s.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} what they are cooking, so that the dishes differ

effects.log: You compare notes, and the elder receives two dishes that agree so well in their difference that it feels planned.

choices.text: Serve plain rice and a clear soup

effects.log: You serve plain rice and a clear soup, and the elder, who has eaten at every table, finishes it all.

events.text: In the hour before the Jade Court sits, the Star Sea sells a prophecy that "the one who bridged the north" will be remembered. Everyone buying it believes this means {b3_rival}. You write three letters and send none.

choices.text: Buy the prophecy and read the small print

effects.log: The print says "bridged", not "bridged first", and you share it round the stair, to general amusement.

choices.text: Offer the Star Sea a better line of prophecy

ok.log: The Star Sea adds your clause to the next printing, for no fee, which has never been known.

fail.log: The Star Sea charges a fee, and keeps the original.

choices.text: Build a smaller bridge somewhere quiet

effects.log: You build a footbridge across a stream in a lower isle, and the prophecy does not mention it, and it is the one you like best.

events.text: On a morning when the clouds had gone the colour of old bone, a fault runs through the white stair itself, and as the steps begin to fall {b3_rival} grabs a boy, you grab the rail, and neither of you has time to argue about who. You are, for the length of one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Seize the rail and hold the stair together while {b3_rival} hauls the boy

ok.log: The rail holds, the boy comes up, and the stair falls away behind, and nobody argues about who did what.

fail.log: The rail gives under both your weights, and you scramble up with scraped hands and the boy safe.

choices.text: Shout the order of the safe steps to {b3_rival}

effects.log: You shout the safe steps in sequence, and {b3_rival} follows each, and the boy rides on their back as they go.

choices.text: Climb up the fallen stairs behind them, as quick as you can

effects.log: You climb behind, as quick as the stone allows, and reach the landing with the others.

events.text: A century into the quarrel, at the Jade Court, {b3_rival} describes the exact weather on the day you first met, down to the cloud. You thought you were the only one who remembered it. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

choices.text: Tell them what you remember of that day that they have wrong

effects.log: You say the cloud was lower and the tea was cold, and {b3_rival} insists, and you argue about the weather for an hour, which is a kind of tenderness.

choices.text: Ask them what they thought of you on that day

ok.log: {b3_rival} admits they took you for a clerk, and that they have been trying to live it down for a century.

fail.log: {b3_rival} blushes and declines, and the weather stays between you.

choices.text: Say you remember it too, and no more

effects.log: You say that you remember it too, and no more, and the sentence sits between you for a long moment.

events.text: In a corridor of cold jade between two audiences, Your oldest correspondent in the Star Sea writes that she is "no longer in a position to write to you", and encloses the receipt for {b3_rival}'s retainer. You feel the ground move a little, if there were ground.

choices.text: Write back one last time, with your own receipt enclosed

effects.log: You enclose a receipt for forty years of her letters, marked "paid in full", and she keeps it in a drawer, you hear.

choices.text: Visit her in the Star Sea and ask her plainly

ok.log: She meets you on the pavilion steps, plain and tired, and says the retainer pays her debts, and you understand, and settle the debt yourself.

fail.log: She declines to see you, courteously, and you go home.

choices.text: Burn nothing, and file the letter with the others

effects.log: You file her final letter with the others, in order, and it makes the pile complete.

events.text: After a sword lecture neither of you had enjoyed, you are honoured with a new title that you cannot pronounce, and {b3_rival} alone does not laugh, because they have been practising it for you. Whatever the Court says, the two of you know.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to teach you the pronunciation, from the start

effects.log: You sit with {b3_rival} for an afternoon and say it fifty times, and by dusk you have it, and the Court has a new in-joke.

choices.text: Pronounce it flawlessly at the next ceremony

ok.log: The syllables come out clean, and the herald nearly drops his staff, and {b3_rival} permits themselves a small smile.

fail.log: You swallow the third syllable and the herald coughs.

choices.text: Shorten the title to what you can say, and let the Court follow

effects.log: You use the shorter title in your own letters, and within a decade the Court uses it too.

events.text: At a tea ceremony long enough to age a sapling, the Court has outlawed formal duels, so {b3_rival} proposes a game of stones, in which the stones are rather heavier than the usual, and thrown. Someone is already taking bets, and you will not look.

choices.text: Throw the heavy stones with all your strength

ok.log: The stones fly over the practice isle, and yours land the farther, and the bets are paid in a hurry.

fail.log: The stones fall short, and one rolls back on your foot.

choices.text: Throw the stones at a target, with a rule that nobody is hit

effects.log: You set a target of old tea-cups and throw for accuracy, and the game becomes an elegant one, and the Court allows it.

choices.text: Hold your stone, and watch {b3_rival} throw theirs

effects.log: You hold your stone and watch {b3_rival} throw, and learn the arc, and keep it for the next game.

events.text: Just as the lamps were being lit along the jade stairs, {b3_rival} nods to you across the Court with such deep, meaningful respect that three ministers assume you have just been demoted. You will think about this for a decade.

choices.text: Return the nod, exactly as deep

effects.log: You nod back, exactly as deep and meaningful, and now six ministers assume you have both been demoted.

choices.text: Walk over and ask {b3_rival} after their health, gravely

ok.log: You ask with such gravity that the Court decides {b3_rival} is gravely ill, and sends soup.

fail.log: You ask so gravely that {b3_rival} shows alarm, and the Court decides you are the one who has been demoted.

choices.text: Light the lamp beside you and say nothing

effects.log: You light your lamp, the stairs go gold below, and the ministers' confusion is a private joke you keep.

events.text: At the foot of the white stairs, where all news arrives first, Your disciples find a new roof on the library and a note: "The old one was an insult to books." The hand is {b3_rival}'s, and the roof is excellent. You will owe a century of tea.

choices.text: Have your disciples carve a thanks in the beam

effects.log: The disciples carve it into a roof-beam where only the sun can read it, and {b3_rival} comes by in the spring to look at the light.

choices.text: Write {b3_rival} a note on what else is wrong with your books

ok.log: Your note is a long list, and a week later the cellars of your library are dry.

fail.log: Your list is so long that {b3_rival} takes it for scorn, and sends only a very short reply.

choices.text: Let the roof be, and read under it

effects.log: You read under the new roof for a century, and the books like it, and so do you.

events.text: At a banquet whose seating had been argued over for a month, you and {b3_rival} are told to write the epitaph for a retiring marshal. Each is assured the other is writing a longer one. You would like to win it more than you would like to be wise.

choices.text: Write a short epitaph, and a better one

ok.log: Your epitaph is eleven words, and it is read aloud at the funeral, and cut in the stone.

fail.log: Your epitaph is eleven words, and two of them are wrong, and the marshal's widow says so.

choices.text: Show {b3_rival} your draft, and ask what they would add

effects.log: {b3_rival} adds a single line, a good one, and you cut half of yours, and the two together are carved.

choices.text: Write the long one and let {b3_rival} write the short one

effects.log: You write the long one with great care, and it is read, and nobody remembers the short one at all.

events.text: On the stairs of an isle you had both come to for different reasons, a school on the lower stairs adopts {b3_rival}'s name for its prize in carving. You taught the founder of that school, and were not asked. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Visit the school and teach a class for nothing

effects.log: You teach a class on the second Tuesday of each month, and the pupils learn the founder was yours.

choices.text: Write to the school's board, kindly and with dates

ok.log: The board is embarrassed and adds a second prize, named for you, the same size.

fail.log: The board thanks you for your interest and does nothing.

choices.text: Carve something yourself and leave it at the school gate

effects.log: You carve a small bird in white jade and leave it on the step, and the pupils fight over it.

events.text: At a stone gate where the guards know everyone and say nothing, Fog comes up the isle thick as milk, and a lamp-lit procession is lost on it. You and {b3_rival} are the two best voices in the Court, and you have not sung together in two hundred years. There will be no one to witness it, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Sing the old guiding hymn, with {b3_rival} taking the answering line

ok.log: Your voices find each other on the second verse, and the procession follows the sound home through the fog.

fail.log: Your voices clash, and the procession wanders on the isle until the fog thins.

choices.text: Sing alone and let {b3_rival} walk the lines to find the stragglers

effects.log: You sing the long note and {b3_rival} goes out along the fog and brings the stragglers back, one by one, by the sleeve.

choices.text: Ring the isle's fog-bell and keep ringing until dawn

effects.log: You ring the bell all night, a flat iron note, and it is not beautiful, and every lamp comes home to it.

events.text: On a night of low cloud over the eastern isles, {b3_rival} leaves a jar of honey on your threshold with a card: "For the cough." You had told no one about the cough. For a moment the stairs are only stairs.

choices.text: Leave a jar of your own tea on their step in return

effects.log: You leave a small jar of your own black tea, unlabelled, and the next week it is gone, and the step swept.

choices.text: Find out who told them about the cough

ok.log: The ferryman had told them, in passing, and neither of you minds, and the cough eases.

fail.log: The trail runs cold in a tea-house, and you never find out.

choices.text: Take the honey in with the morning milk

effects.log: You take a spoonful with the morning milk, and the cough is better by the fourth day.

events.text: During the first rain the isles had seen in forty years, a rival school poaches your best archer, who sends back a long, kind letter of explanation and a pair of shoes you had once lent her. Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

choices.text: Send the archer a bow-string and a reference

effects.log: You send a new bow-string, tough as a cloud-whale's sinew, and a reference, and she writes to say she is shooting better already.

choices.text: Challenge the archer to one last friendly match before she goes

ok.log: You shoot to a draw, with the shoes on the line, and she gives them back with a laugh.

fail.log: She wins by a feather, and the shoes stay with her.

choices.text: Wear the shoes she returned, and wish her luck

effects.log: You wear the old shoes the length of the lower stair, and they still fit.

events.text: At the spring when lanterns are floated off the edge of the isles, {b3_rival} takes a young disciple of whom the whole Court expects great things, and the disciple, on being introduced to you, says you are "much shorter than {b3_rival} said". It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Stand beside the disciple and compare heights, gravely

effects.log: You measure yourselves against the pillar, and the disciple, appalled, finds you are taller than {b3_rival} after all.

choices.text: Offer the disciple a lesson in what {b3_rival} has not taught them

ok.log: You teach something small and exact, and the disciple, who expected a sermon, writes it down.

fail.log: You teach something small, and the disciple already knows it from {b3_rival}.

choices.text: Smile and say that {b3_rival} exaggerates, always

effects.log: You smile, and say that {b3_rival} has always been generous with lengths, and the disciple blushes.

events.text: Under the great bell that rings once a century and was ringing, Dawn at the training isle: {b3_rival} is already there, in their shirtsleeves, with two wooden swords, and an expression that dares you to say it is beneath you. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

choices.text: Take the wooden sword and spar until the sun clears the cloud

ok.log: You spar until the sun clears, and the bruises are fair, and the last blow is yours.

fail.log: You spar until the sun clears, and the last blow is theirs, and you sit down in the dew.

choices.text: Say it is not beneath you, and spar three rounds, evenly

effects.log: You spar exactly three rounds, evenly, and the sweat is honest, and the dawn-bell rings the draw.

choices.text: Hand the wooden sword back and make breakfast instead

effects.log: You make rice and pickles on the training isle, and {b3_rival} eats, and the dare is dissolved in steam.

events.text: Ten years on, the Jade Void rebuilds its courtyard and the bench is turned over by a mason. {b3_rival}'s joke, your name on the underside, is now read aloud to the whole yard, and is not funny any more, only odd.

choices.text: Have the bench left as it is

effects.log: You have the bench left as it is, and the apprentices sit on your name every day with great respect.

choices.text: Carve something under theirs

effects.log: You carve a short line under {b3_rival}'s own bench in the same yard. It takes them a year to find it.

choices.text: Ask the mason for the chip

effects.log: You ask the mason for the chip of jade with your name on it, and keep it on your desk.

events.text: Ten years on, the rebuilt alchemy hall bears a small plaque by the door, put there by your apprentices unasked: the name of the fire-fighters. {b3_rival}'s disciples are on it, and {b3_rival} has never seen it.

choices.text: Invite {b3_rival} to see it

effects.log: You invite {b3_rival} to see the plaque. They read it for a very long time, and say only that the carving is poor.

choices.text: Send a cask of the first batch

effects.log: You send a cask of the hall's first batch of elixir, no note. It is returned, empty, with a dried flower.

choices.text: Leave it unmentioned

effects.log: You leave it unmentioned. The plaque weathers well.

events.text: Ten years on, the orchid you and {b3_rival} both used has gone extinct on the lower isles, and the only living plants are the two in your rival gardens. The Court asks you both for cuttings.

choices.text: Give the cutting freely

effects.log: You give the cutting freely, and the Court publishes a note thanking you, with {b3_rival}'s name beside yours.

choices.text: Set a price

effects.log: You set a price. {b3_rival} gives theirs away, and the Court remembers.

choices.text: Propose a joint garden

effects.log: You propose a joint garden. It takes a decade to agree on the fence.

events.text: Ten years on, the cornerstone has been chipped by a storm, and the stonemasons offer to recut it. {b3_rival}'s name above yours, three fingers up. The masons have asked which of you wishes to be on top.

choices.text: Ask for the stone to be left chipped

effects.log: You ask for it to be left chipped. The chip looks, from the right angle, like a smile.

choices.text: Ask for your name above theirs

effects.log: You ask for your name above theirs, by a finger. {b3_rival} asks for it by two. The mason leaves, in tears.

choices.text: Suggest both names go in the middle

effects.log: You suggest both names go side by side. The mason sighs with relief, and the stone is cut.

events.text: Ten years on, the bridge chain that snapped is mended with a link marked by both your hands, forged on the spot by a smith who had never seen two immortals work a winch. The Court hangs the old link in the hall.

choices.text: Visit the link with {b3_rival}

effects.log: You visit the old link with {b3_rival}, and stand under it for some time. Neither of you remembers who held the winch.

choices.text: Have a plaque cut for the smith

effects.log: You pay for a plaque for the smith. The smith is moved, and offers you a lifetime of nails.

choices.text: Test the new link yourself

effects.log: You test the new link yourself, hanging off it for a minute. It holds.

events.text: Ten years on, the pear tree on the library roof is in bloom, and {b3_rival} has sent a basket of the fruit with a single line in a careful hand: "Half." You eat half. You leave the other half on a plate on the roof.

choices.text: Go up to the roof at dusk

effects.log: You go up at dusk. The other half of the pear is gone, and someone has left a stone in its place.

choices.text: Send a basket in return

effects.log: You send a basket of your own, full. The next morning, one pear comes back on a plate.

choices.text: Write a letter about the roof

effects.log: You write a letter about the roof, the sky, the sea of clouds, and tear it up, and write it again, shorter.

events.text: Ten years on, the apprentice seer who defected to {b3_rival} has become a Star Sea master, and returns to your isle to read for it. The reading is accurate, long, and, to your surprise, kind.

choices.text: Thank the master

effects.log: You thank the master gravely, and ask for the reading to be put in writing. It is a very good piece of work.

choices.text: Ask them about {b3_rival}

effects.log: You ask about {b3_rival}, and learn a dozen small things you had not known: the tea, the cat, the early mornings.

choices.text: Make an offer

effects.log: You make an offer to hire them back. They smile and refuse, and they are right.

events.text: Ten years on, the Warden of the Eastern Isles sends for you. It is {b3_rival}, who has found that the post is mostly paperwork and weather, and wants the one person in the Court who will tell them so honestly.

choices.text: Go to the Eastern Isles

effects.log: You go. {b3_rival} has a map, a ledger, and a long list of questions; you answer for a season and enjoy it.

choices.text: Send a long, frank letter

effects.log: You send a long, frank letter, three pages on weather and one on nerves. They answer in two lines: "Noted."

choices.text: Decline, and send tea

effects.log: You decline and send tea. It is warmly acknowledged.

events.text: Ten years on, the tea duel has become an annual event at the Jade Void, and you and {b3_rival} are asked to judge it. The finalists are, sadly, your two worst pupils. The Court is watching with interest.

choices.text: Judge fairly

effects.log: You judge fairly and the finalists are both kind enough to look chastened. {b3_rival} gives the same verdict.

choices.text: Compete against your own pupil

effects.log: You step into the contest against your pupil, and win, narrowly, and {b3_rival} loudly points out that it was not fair.

choices.text: Invite {b3_rival} to pour for you

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} to pour for you, in the old courtesy. They do, and the tea is excellent, and a lesson.

events.text: Ten years on, the Demon Realm general returns to the Court and greets you, by name, correctly, and then bows to {b3_rival} with a small smile that says he remembers the three wrong pointings.

choices.text: Tell {b3_rival} the general knew

effects.log: You tell {b3_rival} that the general knew all along. They go a deep and satisfactory red.

choices.text: Dine with the general

effects.log: You dine with the general, who turns out to be good company, and who tells you three things about the Demon Realm that are true.

choices.text: Say nothing, and pour wine

effects.log: You pour wine for both, and nobody mentions the old joke, and the dinner is better for it.

events.text: Ten years on, the Treasury's debt is repaid in full, with interest, and a clerk lets slip that {b3_rival}'s speech to the Ministry was written in a single night and delivered from memory.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} the interest

effects.log: You send {b3_rival} the interest. They send it back, with the principal, and a note that says "I do not like owing."

choices.text: Thank them over tea

effects.log: You thank them over tea at the Court garden. They say "It was efficient" four times.

choices.text: Make a gift of the speech to the library

effects.log: You have the speech copied into the library, with {b3_rival}'s name at the head, and they hear about it from a student.

events.text: Ten years on, the scroll that was bid for in the silent auction goes missing from the buyer's library, and the whole Star Sea suspects either you or {b3_rival}. Each of you says the other did it. Each is lying, a little.

choices.text: Join forces to find the thief

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} find the thief together: a pet cloud-goat. The Court has not laughed so much in a century.

choices.text: Look alone

effects.log: You look alone, and find nothing, and learn something about how little you know of the Star Sea.

choices.text: Accuse them politely

effects.log: You accuse {b3_rival} very politely, in public. The apology you receive is longer than the accusation.

events.text: Ten years on, the festival play is staged again, and this year the actor playing the wise immortal wears a grey wig and says a line you wrote yourself, and the audience laughs at {b3_rival}.

choices.text: Take a bow from the audience

effects.log: You rise and take a bow when the line is spoken. The Court turns and laughs again, at you.

choices.text: Leave quietly

effects.log: You leave quietly, and {b3_rival} leaves a moment later, and you cross at the gate and nod.

choices.text: Send the troupe a better line

effects.log: You send the troupe a better line, anonymously. It becomes famous, and {b3_rival} wonders who wrote it.

events.text: Ten years on, the cloud-wolf pups from the Jade Void's pens have grown into the isle's best flock-dogs, and one of them, to everyone's surprise, will follow only {b3_rival}, and is sleeping on their doorstep.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to share the dog

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} to share the dog. They consider it with the seriousness of a treaty and agree to alternate weeks.

choices.text: Bring the dog a bone, alone

effects.log: You bring the dog a bone each night, in secret. In a year it follows you, too.

choices.text: Leave them to it

effects.log: You leave them to it, and enjoy the dog from a distance.

events.text: Ten years on, {b3_rival} has stopped asking what you will do when you have won, and begun to ask what they will do when you have. You find you have an answer you did not expect to give them.

choices.text: Tell them the truth

effects.log: You tell them the truth: that you would be lonely. {b3_rival} says nothing at all, and does not leave.

choices.text: Make a joke of it

effects.log: You make a joke of it, and {b3_rival} laughs and does not believe you.

choices.text: Ask them the same

effects.log: You ask them the same. Their answer takes an evening, and is long, and honest.

events.text: Ten years on, the ferrymen who land at {b3_rival}'s isle first have grown tired of the uphill and begun to land at the middle isle, where neither of you is. A small market has grown up there, and the Court is amused.

choices.text: Open a stall at the market

effects.log: You open a stall at the market with {b3_rival}, on a neutral bench, and it is a success.

choices.text: Ignore the market

effects.log: You ignore the market. It prospers anyway, and you are a shade jealous.

choices.text: Lend the ferrymen a lantern

effects.log: You lend the ferrymen a lantern for the night run. They name it after you.

events.text: Ten years on, the treatise by {b3_rival} that you saw carried reverently past your door is in its fifth printing and is now taught. Its argument has a flaw that only you have seen, and the flaw is delightful.

choices.text: Write to {b3_rival} about the flaw

effects.log: You write to {b3_rival}. They reply in nine days: "I know. I left it for you."

choices.text: Publish a reply

effects.log: You publish a reply. It is polite, devastating, and widely read, and {b3_rival} buys forty copies.

choices.text: Keep the flaw a secret

effects.log: You keep the flaw to yourself, for later. It is a small bright thing to own.

events.text: Ten years on, the Demon Realm delegation returns for another demonstration, and the general who saw the quay fight asks for the same two swordsmen again. {b3_rival} has been practising in secret. So have you.

choices.text: Fight again, in earnest

effects.log: You fight again, and the quay shakes, and the delegation applauds in the way demons do, with their feet.

choices.text: Propose a draw in advance

effects.log: You propose a draw in advance. The general is baffled. The audience is thrilled.

choices.text: Let the pupils demonstrate

effects.log: You let your pupils demonstrate. The general's eyebrows rise, and the quay is quiet.

events.text: Ten years on, the book {b3_rival} returned, with the smoothed pages and the slip, is the only one in your library you still open. You have, at last, read it. It is better than you wanted it to be.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a note of thanks

effects.log: You send a note of thanks, short, with no sting in it. The reply is a single flat line: "Not at all."

choices.text: Annotate it, and send it back

effects.log: You fill the margins and return it. The two of you pass it back and forth for a decade, as a kind of conversation.

choices.text: Keep it, and say nothing

effects.log: You keep it and say nothing, and the nothing sits on your shelf beside the book.

events.text: Ten years on, the lad {b3_rival} taught to read is a scribe in the Ministry of Rites, and one of the best. He tells everyone who will listen that his first teacher was the rival of his second.

choices.text: Promote the lad

effects.log: You speak for him at the Ministry, and he is raised. {b3_rival} hears and sends the lad a pen, and a lecture on handwriting.

choices.text: Ask him what {b3_rival} was like

effects.log: You ask what {b3_rival} was like as a teacher. "Terrible," he says, "and I would die for them."

choices.text: Let the lad be

effects.log: You let the lad be, and his life goes well without you, which is best.

events.text: Ten years on, the two boys from the Nine Clouds exam are inseparable, and have invented a game in the courtyard that is, unfortunately, a better one than anything either of you taught them.

choices.text: Learn the game from them

effects.log: You learn the game from the boys. {b3_rival} turns up on day three, pretending to be passing.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to referee

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} to referee. It is the first match of your lives that neither of you can win.

choices.text: Let them keep it secret

effects.log: You let them keep it secret. Some games are best left to the young.

events.text: Ten years on, a second edition of the book on cloud-beasts adds your name to the thanks, in small type, after a typo. The migration chapter is still uncredited, and now two authors disclaim it.

choices.text: Write a letter to the editor

effects.log: You write to the editor. The third edition carries a full page about the chapter, and its author.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: You let it go, and watch the chapter be cited by strangers for a century. It is a decent revenge.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} to say it was yours

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} to put it in writing. They do, with a look of pain, and the pain is the best part.

events.text: Ten years on, the rope bridge is a stone arch, and the two of you are named on the first stone as the ones who held it. You come to look. {b3_rival} is there, standing in the middle, testing the stone with the toe of a boot.

choices.text: Stand beside them

effects.log: You stand beside them in the middle of the arch, and nothing at all is said, and it is easy.

choices.text: Joke about the swinging

effects.log: You joke about the swinging. {b3_rival} laughs, once, a short bark, and it starts a conversation.

choices.text: Walk across and keep going

effects.log: You walk across and keep going. Some things should be left to age.

events.text: Ten years on, the seeds from the isle that no longer exists have grown into a dozen plants of a kind nobody on the Court can name. The Nine Clouds Palace sends a botanist, who weeps at the sight of them. {b3_rival} asks, very softly, if they may come and see.

choices.text: Welcome {b3_rival} to the garden

effects.log: You welcome them, and {b3_rival} walks the rows touching the leaves, and does not say a word for an hour.

choices.text: Give them a cutting to take home

effects.log: You give them a cutting. It takes root in their courtyard, and in spring you receive a pressed flower.

choices.text: Name the plant together

effects.log: You name the plant together, a long argument. The name is a compromise, and slightly wrong, and perfect.

events.text: Ten years on, the retired gatekeeper writes to you from {b3_rival}'s isle. He is very comfortable, and ashamed of it. He begs your forgiveness, and encloses a small carved gate, no bigger than a thumb.

choices.text: Forgive him in writing

effects.log: You write to forgive him, at length, and mean it. He frames the letter.

choices.text: Visit the old man

effects.log: You visit the old man on {b3_rival}'s isle, and are served tea by {b3_rival} themselves.

choices.text: Put the little gate on your desk

effects.log: You put the little gate on your desk, where it guards the pens.

events.text: Ten years on, {b3_rival} returns to the Court after their long illness, thinner and quieter, and takes the lower seat by the door. The Court nods, and moves along. You rise from your seat and walk down the hall to sit beside them.

choices.text: Sit beside them, openly

effects.log: You sit beside them, openly, and the Court, to its credit, rearranges itself to make room.

choices.text: Bring them tea

effects.log: You bring them a cup, hot, and set it down without a word. They hold it with both hands.

choices.text: Ask what they need

effects.log: You ask what they need. The answer is a long list, with four things on it that you can do.

events.text: Ten years on, the Star Sea's prophecy is the talk of the Court: the next great duel of the century "will end without a winner." {b3_rival} sends a copy to you, underlined, with an inked arrow pointing at the word "end".

choices.text: Reply with an underlined word of your own

effects.log: You underline "winner" and send it back. The correspondence runs for nineteen years.

choices.text: Take the prophecy seriously

effects.log: You take the prophecy seriously and begin to wonder what it means to lose a duel by not ending it.

choices.text: Burn your copy

effects.log: You burn your copy, and the Star Sea charges you for the reading all the same.

events.text: Ten years on, {b3_rival} has been to visit your isle. They said it had "a great deal of potential" again, in the same tone, but this time at the end of a long tour, and the potential was in the plural.

choices.text: Take the compliment

effects.log: You take the compliment as it was meant, finally. {b3_rival} blinks at the lack of resistance.

choices.text: Ask what they would change

effects.log: You ask what they would change. The list is long, precise, and mostly right, which is the real insult.

choices.text: Show them the cellar

effects.log: You show them the cellar, which is dry, and holds forty years of rice wine. They stay for supper.

events.text: Ten years on, the storm {b3_rival}'s seer warned of is remembered as the Night of the Lantern Tree, because your isle lit its tree early and saved the ferries. {b3_rival} wants the credit, as a joke, and means it only a little.

choices.text: Share the credit in full

effects.log: You tell the Court that the warning was {b3_rival}'s, in full. They are delighted, and furious, in exactly equal parts.

choices.text: Joke that you will split it

effects.log: You joke that you will split it down the middle. {b3_rival} weighs this with the gravity of a customs clerk, and agrees.

choices.text: Keep the tree lit every year

effects.log: You light the tree every year. {b3_rival} comes to the lighting, and stands at the back.

events.text: Ten years on, you finally lose the dare and carry the tea-tray for a decade, in earnest. {b3_rival} insists on a formal ceremony, a bow at the start of each day, and a different cup every time. By the fourth year, it is a ritual.

choices.text: Carry it with grace

effects.log: You carry the tray with grace, and the Court begins to treat your service as an art.

choices.text: Buy the cups yourself

effects.log: You start buying the cups yourself, rare ones, and {b3_rival} notices by the second year and says nothing.

choices.text: Ask to renegotiate

effects.log: You ask to renegotiate. {b3_rival} grants it in the manner of a king pardoning a thief, and pours the tea.

events.text: Ten years on, the student in the lecture hall is a lecturer, and still says the third law was {b3_rival}'s discovery, and has been quoted in four books. {b3_rival} has begun to correct them, mildly, and it is not working.

choices.text: Join {b3_rival} in correcting it

effects.log: You join {b3_rival} in correcting it, from opposite sides of the hall, and the student gets confused.

choices.text: Send the lecturer the footnote

effects.log: You send the lecturer the old footnote. They write back, mortified, and add a long note to the next lecture.

choices.text: Enjoy the confusion

effects.log: You enjoy the confusion. It has a flavour, like a cold radish.

events.text: Ten years on, the stolen lens of the Star Sea Pavilion is returned by a weeping thief and rehung. The Pavilion invites you and {b3_rival} to the first night it is used, to look through it, side by side.

choices.text: Look together

effects.log: You look through it together. It shows a star neither of you has a name for, and {b3_rival} says "Ours," quietly.

choices.text: Let {b3_rival} look first

effects.log: You let {b3_rival} look first. They take a very long time, and when they step back their eyes are wet.

choices.text: Ask what it shows

effects.log: You ask the seer what it shows. "A bridge," says the seer. "Not a metaphor."

events.text: Ten years on, the keeper of the stair is dead, and left a ledger. In it, a payment of three hundred years from {b3_rival}, to leave a lamp lit at your door. The keeper noted, at the bottom: "Never told them why it was the rival."

choices.text: Light the lamp yourself from now on

effects.log: You light the lamp yourself, every night, from now on. {b3_rival} notices it burning as they pass, and slows.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} the ledger

effects.log: You send {b3_rival} the ledger, unannotated. They read it standing in the doorway, and shut the door.

choices.text: Burn it, to spare them

effects.log: You burn the ledger, to spare them. You will carry the knowledge alone.

events.text: Ten years on, the painter's screen of your isle, painted from across the water in {b3_rival}'s house, is the most admired painting of the age. It is a loving view. The painter says it was {b3_rival} who chose the angle.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} why

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} why they chose that angle. "It was the one where it looked best," they say, and leave in a hurry.

choices.text: Commission a pair

effects.log: You commission a pair: a view of {b3_rival}'s isle, from yours. The painter charges double.

choices.text: Buy the screen

effects.log: You buy the screen. {b3_rival} pays double, and then you are in an auction, and so is the screen.

events.text: Ten years on, the jade from the Demon Realm has been cut into a pair of seals, one for you and one for {b3_rival}, and come with a cordial invitation to a council on the borders. Both of you are asked to attend, separately, on the same day.

choices.text: Attend, with {b3_rival}'s seal in your sleeve

effects.log: You attend and carry both seals, for the love of a joke. The council laughs, in the Demon fashion, loudly.

choices.text: Decline both invitations

effects.log: You decline both. The Demon Realm, who despise a tidy refusal, respect it.

choices.text: Go as {b3_rival}'s second

effects.log: You go as {b3_rival}'s second. It is the least dignified and most useful role of your life.

events.text: Ten years on, the Court's order to resolve the matter by "honourable means" has produced a standing committee, a rota of three kinds of duel, and a ledger of results. It is the longest feud in the records, and the dullest. You and {b3_rival} are both bored.

choices.text: Propose to dissolve the committee

effects.log: You propose to dissolve the committee. {b3_rival} seconds it with such alacrity that the Court takes it for a joke.

choices.text: Fix the next match as a draw

effects.log: You fix the next match as a draw. The ledger has no column for it, and the clerk faints.

choices.text: Take the committee seat

effects.log: You take the committee seat. Somebody has to keep the other side honest.

events.text: Ten years on, the map with your landing marked "Rest Stop" has become real: a stall has opened there selling hot tea and pickled plums, and the sign says Rest Stop, and the queue is long.

choices.text: Buy tea from the stall

effects.log: You buy tea from the stall, and tip, and the stall-keeper tells you proudly that {b3_rival} sends the signboard paint every year.

choices.text: Take the profit and rename it

effects.log: You rename the stall and keep the profits. {b3_rival} is the first to send a congratulatory basket.

choices.text: Leave the sign

effects.log: You leave the sign. The Court begins to call your isle by its new name, which is a defeat of a kind, and you wear it well.

events.text: Ten years on, after the illness you barely remember, {b3_rival} asks nothing. You learn from a nurse that they sat the whole of the worst night and had written a will before dawn, just in case.

choices.text: Tell {b3_rival} you know

effects.log: You tell {b3_rival} that you know. They say "I was in the neighbourhood," and cannot meet your eye.

choices.text: Sit with them in turn, when they are sick

effects.log: You wait, and the next time {b3_rival} is ill you sit the night. Nothing is said about it for forty years.

choices.text: Bury the thought

effects.log: You bury it, as the sensible do, and it keeps growing anyway.

events.text: Ten years on, a stair-walker on one leg is a Court custom, and the winner is always whoever {b3_rival} loses to. This year it is you again, and you are no longer sure the dare was ever about the stairs.

choices.text: Walk them with {b3_rival}, both on one leg

effects.log: You and {b3_rival} walk the stairs side by side, both on one leg, to scandalised applause.

choices.text: Sit this one out

effects.log: You sit it out. The silence from the stairs is noticed.

choices.text: Name a new dare

effects.log: You name a new dare: a decade of silence on the subject. It lasts eleven days.

events.text: Ten years on, {b3_rival} still has the medal that had your name on it by mistake. It is on a shelf, not on display. A visitor asks about it and {b3_rival} answers, frankly: "That one is somebody else's."

choices.text: Ask for it back

effects.log: You ask for the medal back. {b3_rival} hands it over at once, polished, and says "Now we are even," and goes away.

choices.text: Tell them to keep it

effects.log: You tell them to keep it. It means more on their shelf than on yours.

choices.text: Have both made into a pair

effects.log: You have a second one made, identical, and send it to {b3_rival} with a single line. They hang them together.

events.text: Ten years on, the archive that burned is half-restored, and a clerk finds in the char a single leaf in two hands: yours, and {b3_rival}'s, a joint record from the night itself, written as the fire took the room.

choices.text: Frame the leaf

effects.log: You frame the leaf. It hangs in the lobby of the new archive, with a small bronze label that gets the dates wrong.

choices.text: Read it with {b3_rival}

effects.log: You read it with {b3_rival}. It records no quarrel at all.

choices.text: Seal it in a box

effects.log: You seal it in a box for the century after. The box will be opened in nine hundred years.

events.text: Ten years on, the old friend whose wedding you shared with {b3_rival} has a child, and the child is to be named. The old friend asks the two of you to choose the name between you. You are given a day.

choices.text: Choose together

effects.log: You choose together, in a tea-house, at length. The name is nobody's first choice, and is exactly right.

choices.text: Let {b3_rival} choose

effects.log: You let {b3_rival} choose. They pick a name of a star, a quiet one, and cry a little at the table.

choices.text: Suggest a name of your own

effects.log: You suggest a name of your own. {b3_rival} accepts it too fast, and you suspect it was their idea.

events.text: Ten years on, the lost petition has become a minor legend of the Ministry of Rites. {b3_rival}'s committee, which you reluctantly joined, has turned out to be the only one in the Court that gets anything done. They offer you the chair.

choices.text: Accept the chair

effects.log: You accept the chair, and the first act is to thank {b3_rival}. They stare. They had expected a quarrel.

choices.text: Decline, and sit at the end

effects.log: You decline, and sit at the end, and are more useful there than you ever were at the head.

choices.text: Propose a rotation

effects.log: You propose a rotation of chairs. It is adopted by nobody and then, after three years, by everybody.

events.text: Ten years on, the comet {b3_rival} is named for returns, bright and long, and the whole Court goes up on the roofs to watch. {b3_rival} stays indoors with the shutters closed. The comet is, for a comet, rather conspicuous.

choices.text: Go and sit with {b3_rival}

effects.log: You go and sit with {b3_rival} in the dark. After a while they ask if the comet is any good. "It is quite good," you say.

choices.text: Bring the comet to them

effects.log: You describe it in detail, from the roof, by shouting, through a shutter. They yell back corrections.

choices.text: Watch it from the roof

effects.log: You watch it from the roof. It is a fine comet, and you tell no one it reminded you of them.

events.text: Ten years on, the plain sword {b3_rival} borrowed on the ledge is returned to its owner, sharpened, with a long note of thanks and a remark that it had "an admirable temper". The owner shows you the note, completely baffled.

choices.text: Explain it to the owner

effects.log: You explain it to the owner, who asks if swords have tempers. "This one did," you say.

choices.text: Ask to borrow it yourself

effects.log: You ask to borrow the sword. The owner hands it over, saying that it has had enough of rivals.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a whetstone

effects.log: You send {b3_rival} a whetstone. It is returned, with a single character, "again".

events.text: Ten years on, the three ministers who took {b3_rival}'s meaningful nod for a sign of your downfall are proved wrong, one by one, by your promotion. {b3_rival} is the only one who gave the nod and is not embarrassed.

choices.text: Thank {b3_rival} for the nod

effects.log: You thank {b3_rival} for the nod, with perfect gravity. They are the one to look uncomfortable.

choices.text: Remember the three ministers

effects.log: You file the three ministers' names in the part of your memory that keeps accounts.

choices.text: Laugh about it in company

effects.log: You tell the story at a banquet, laughing hardest at yourself, and the Court warms to you.

events.text: Ten years on, the new roof on your library has outlasted the books under it. The Ministry of Works offers to renew it, and {b3_rival} writes to say, mildly, that the roof was to be left to weather and that nobody should touch it.

choices.text: Leave the roof

effects.log: You leave the roof. It becomes a minor landmark of the isle, with a story that is slightly wrong.

choices.text: Send {b3_rival} a book for the shelves

effects.log: You send {b3_rival} a book of your own writing, bound in the same green cloth as the roof tiles. The reply is a poem, and it rhymes.

choices.text: Repair it quietly

effects.log: You repair a loose tile, in the night, with your own hands, and tell no one. The roof goes on.

events.text: Ten years on, the retiring marshal asks for your epitaph and {b3_rival}'s to be read together at the farewell, back to back, a line at a time. They are, in the end, written to complete one another.

choices.text: Read yours with feeling

effects.log: You read yours with feeling, and the old marshal weeps, and the Court sniffs.

choices.text: Trade lines in the middle

effects.log: You trade a line in the middle, for the love of the music. {b3_rival} accepts it without a word.

choices.text: Read theirs aloud

effects.log: You read {b3_rival}'s epitaph aloud, on request, and {b3_rival} reads yours. It is the kindest thing either of you has said.

events.text: Ten years on, the school with {b3_rival}'s name on its carving prize has had its first winner who is a grandchild of someone you taught. The family invites you both to the ceremony, together, on one invitation.

choices.text: Go, and sit beside {b3_rival}

effects.log: You go, and sit beside {b3_rival}, and the child wins and bows to both. It is very hard on the dignity.

choices.text: Send a gift instead

effects.log: You send a gift instead, a carving knife of the old pattern. It is used for forty years.

choices.text: Offer to teach at the school

effects.log: You offer to teach a season at the school. The school accepts so fast that you suspect {b3_rival} told them.

events.text: Ten years on, the fog that lost the procession returns in a mild form once a year, and the isle has made a festival of it: the Singing Night, in which two voices go out on the stair with lanterns. They always ask you and {b3_rival}.

choices.text: Sing with {b3_rival}

effects.log: You sing with {b3_rival}, badly, in harmony, and the lanterns bob, and the fog thins.

choices.text: Send a student instead

effects.log: You send a student with a better voice. {b3_rival} sends one too, and the two duet.

choices.text: Sit out the festival

effects.log: You sit out the festival and hear it from the balcony. It sounds like a long forgiving.

events.text: Ten years on, the honey arrives again, this time in a better jar, with a card that says only "For the cough, again." You have never mentioned the cough since. You have, in fact, stopped coughing; the cough is something they know about you.

choices.text: Ask how they knew

effects.log: You ask how they knew. "You hum before you clear your throat," says {b3_rival}. "You always have."

choices.text: Send honey of your own

effects.log: You send honey of your own, from a different hive, and wait to see if they can tell.

choices.text: Keep the jar for the cough

effects.log: You keep the jar for the next cough. It does not come for a long time, and the jar stays full.

events.text: Ten years on, the archer who left for the rival school sends you an arrow with a note: "To the first teacher, for the first lesson." It arrives point-first in your gatepost, and a feather on it is dyed in {b3_rival}'s colour.

choices.text: Send an arrow back

effects.log: You send an arrow back, with a note. The archer replies with the world's longest apology.

choices.text: Hang it over the door

effects.log: You hang it over the door. Pupils ask about it for years, and the story improves.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} about the feather

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} about the feather. "It was the only colour we had left," they say, entirely unconvincingly.

events.text: Ten years on, the disciple who said you were "much shorter" has grown up into a famous teacher and, at a festival, introduces you as "the shorter of my two masters". The Court roars. {b3_rival} tries to look stern and cannot.

choices.text: Take the joke

effects.log: You take it with a bow, and ask the disciple to stand on a stool next time. The room roars again.

choices.text: Trade a stool for a sword

effects.log: You trade an old stool for a sword in the teacher's collection. It is an excellent sword.

choices.text: Ask {b3_rival} what they told them

effects.log: You ask {b3_rival} what they told the disciple. "Only the truth," they say. "At the time, you were."

events.text: Ten years on, the dawn practice with wooden swords has become a habit neither of you can stop. The two of you now do it every seventh day, without comment, on the training isle, and the students have named the hour after you both.

choices.text: Keep it as it is

effects.log: You keep it as it is, a plain hour in the grey light, and neither of you says what it is.

choices.text: Invite a student to join

effects.log: You invite a student to join. The student is terrified and wins a point. {b3_rival} buys the student breakfast.

choices.text: Change the sword

effects.log: You bring a real sword one morning. {b3_rival} looks at it, at you, and leaves, and comes back with one of their own.

events.text: {b3_rival} offers to swap the star-charts of their isle for yours, chart for chart. A fair offer, and a rival who has never made one. The charts are the work of three hundred years, and the Star Sea seers would pay dearly for either.

choices.text: Swap them honestly

effects.log: You swap them honestly. Each of you reads the other's work all night, and neither says what was found.

choices.text: Leave a small false gap in yours

effects.log: You leave a small false gap in yours, as insurance. It is a very small gap, and your conscience notes it.

choices.text: Decline, and send them tea

effects.log: You decline, and send tea. {b3_rival} returns the tea, with a note saying it was an excellent tea.

events.text: A decade on, the two sets of charts agree on a missing isle that neither of you had marked, drifting at the edge of the sea of clouds. {b3_rival} proposes a joint voyage, with a map-case, a lantern, and a mutual list of rules.

choices.text: Go together

effects.log: You go together. The isle is small and plain and unclaimed, and you name it between you, with a coin, in the old fashion.

choices.text: Send an apprentice in your place

effects.log: You send an apprentice. The apprentice returns with news of an isle and a lifelong friendship with {b3_rival}'s apprentice, which is worse.

choices.text: Offer to share the credit only on paper

effects.log: You offer to share the credit on paper. {b3_rival} accepts, and the paper lasts a decade.

events.text: A decade on, {b3_rival} finds the false gap in your chart. They come to your gate holding it, and say nothing for some time. When they speak, it is only: "I was hoping it would not be there."

choices.text: Own it, and apologise

effects.log: You own it. {b3_rival} says the apology is the first honest line of your chart, and the two of you stand on the step in the cold.

choices.text: Say it was a test

effects.log: You say it was a test. {b3_rival} says they failed it, and they do not smile. The quarrel gains a new and uglier edge.

choices.text: Offer to correct the chart together

effects.log: You offer to correct the chart together. {b3_rival} agrees, grimly, and the work takes a year, and is done in silence, and is very good.

events.text: {b3_rival}'s best pupil comes to your gate in the rain, with a bundle and a letter, and asks to study under you. The letter is from {b3_rival}: "I have taught all I can. Do what you will, and do not tell me." It is hard to read.

choices.text: Take the pupil in

effects.log: You take the pupil in, and dry the bundle, and say nothing of the letter. The pupil sleeps in your best room.

choices.text: Send the pupil back with a reply

effects.log: You send the pupil back with a reply, courteous, and a basket of plums. The pupil weeps, quietly, and goes.

choices.text: Set the pupil a test

effects.log: You set the pupil a test, of patience. They pass, and are sent home to {b3_rival} with a glowing report, which is almost worse.

events.text: A decade on, the pupil returns to your gate: grown, quick, and carrying {b3_rival}'s respects, in a letter for the first time civil. The pupil has outgrown both of you, and says so, gently.

choices.text: Be proud of them

effects.log: You are proud, and say so, and the pupil goes up the stair with a lighter step. A matching letter goes to {b3_rival}.

choices.text: Ask what {b3_rival} said

effects.log: You ask. The pupil repeats it. It is a shortish sentence, and you read it into the evening for a long time.

choices.text: Challenge the pupil to a game of stones

effects.log: You challenge the pupil. The pupil wins, kindly, and the two of you laugh in a way that you did not expect to.

events.text: A decade on, a letter from {b3_rival}, thanking you for sending the pupil home, and saying that the pupil is now the best teacher on the isle. It is the most generous thing they have ever put in writing, and it is signed with a small, shy flourish.

choices.text: Reply in kind

effects.log: You reply in kind. The correspondence becomes the longest and politest feud on the isles.

choices.text: Visit them

effects.log: You visit. {b3_rival} receives you with a bow and a kettle, and the visit lasts three days.

choices.text: Put the letter away

effects.log: You put it away. Some letters one reads every year, and not more often.

events.text: The Jade Court asks you and {b3_rival} to rebuild the bridge between your two isles, which a storm has taken. They give you a purse of stones, a plan, and a ruling: each builds from their own side, and the two halves are to meet in the middle.

choices.text: Build your half first, and well

effects.log: You build your half first, and well, and wait for the other half at the middle, which does not come for a year.

choices.text: Offer to build the whole

effects.log: You offer to build the whole. The Court is delighted. {b3_rival} is furious, and silent, and sends no reply.

choices.text: Visit {b3_rival} and agree on the span

effects.log: You visit, and agree on the span, and the two of you spend a week arguing about rope.

events.text: A decade on, the two halves meet in the middle with a gap of one hand-width, and the whole bridge hangs on a pin. {b3_rival} comes out onto it with a hammer and an expression of perfect resignation: "Now, this is ours."

choices.text: Drive the pin together

effects.log: You drive the pin together. The bridge hums. The Court names it, and both your names go on a small plaque, upside down.

choices.text: Let them drive it

effects.log: You let them. They do it badly, and then properly, and say it is your half that is better, and mean it.

choices.text: Test the span first

effects.log: You test the span. It holds. You have never been so relieved, and so annoyed to be relieved.

events.text: A decade on, the bridge you built alone stands, and the Court is proud, and {b3_rival}'s isle is cut off from it, and goes on being cut off. {b3_rival} sends nothing. You see a lamp lit on their shore at night, small and steady.

choices.text: Build them a way over, quietly

effects.log: You build a way over, quietly, at night. In the morning there is a lamp at each end and no one will say whose idea it was.

choices.text: Leave it

effects.log: You leave it. The Court praises you, and the lamp across the water goes on being lit, and you notice it every evening.

choices.text: Row across and talk

effects.log: You row across and talk. The rowing takes an hour. The talk takes the night. The bridge, in the end, is extended.

events.text: The Jade Court prints an anthology of the century's verse, and two poems are set side by side: one by you, and one by {b3_rival}, by the editor's whim. Both are about the same autumn, and both are about the other, and neither says so.

choices.text: Add a line to yours in reply

effects.log: You add a line, in your own hand, in the margin of the proof. It answers theirs. It is a small, bold thing to do.

choices.text: Ask the editor to strike yours

effects.log: You ask the editor to strike yours. The editor blinks, and refuses, and prints it larger.

choices.text: Say nothing, and buy a hundred copies

effects.log: You buy a hundred copies and give them away. It is a strange form of advertisement, and it works.

events.text: A decade on, a young poet quotes the pair of verses together in a lecture, as the Jade Court's most famous dialogue. {b3_rival} sits two rows from you, and does not look at you, and mouths the last line, with the room.

choices.text: Mouth it too

effects.log: You mouth it too, and in the silence between you the lecture falters, and nobody minds.

choices.text: Applaud the poet

effects.log: You applaud the poet, and {b3_rival} does too, and for a moment the whole row is clapping the same way.

choices.text: Slip out quietly

effects.log: You slip out. In the corridor, {b3_rival} is already there, pretending to read a notice.

events.text: A decade on, the anthology is reprinted, and {b3_rival} has asked the editor to remove their poem, and keep yours alone, "as the century's true word". The editor shows you the letter, shaking.

choices.text: Refuse, and keep both

effects.log: You refuse, in writing, and say the pair is the poem. The reply is a single character: "Fine."

choices.text: Let the editor decide

effects.log: You let the editor decide. The editor keeps both, and is dismissed, and then reinstated, and the book sells very well.

choices.text: Write them a new poem

effects.log: You write a new poem, in answer, and send it unsigned. The anthology that follows has it as its first page.
